name: Agent Trace specification (Cursor)
status: beta
what_is_stored: JSON-based Trace Records containing: version (semantic), unique identifier (UUID), RFC 3339 timestamp, file paths with line-level code attribution (start_line, end_line), contributor type (human, ai, mixed, unknown), AI model identification (models.dev convention, e.g. anthropic/claude-opus-4-5-20251101), conversation URLs, related resources (sessions, prompts via URL), content hashes for position-independent tracking, version control info (git, jj, hg, svn with revision), tool name/version, and extensible metadata object with reverse-domain-notation vendor fields.
where_stored: Storage-agnostic by design. Specification explicitly states: 'This spec intentionally does not define how traces are stored. This could be local files, git notes, a database, or anything else.' Implementation-dependent; no prescribed location.
format_and_model: JSON format adhering to JSON Schema draft 2020-12. Schema published at https://agent-trace.dev/schemas/v1/trace-record.json. Root TraceRecord object with required fields: version (semantic string), id (UUID), timestamp (RFC 3339), files array. File objects contain path, conversations array with url, contributor, model_id, ranges array (line numbers 1-indexed), and optional related array.
multi_writer_and_merge: Not specified. FAQ explicitly states: 'How should I handle rebases or merge commits? We expect to see different implementations in open source.' Concurrent write coordination, conflict resolution strategies, and merge semantics are intentionally deferred to implementations. This represents an open question during RFC phase.
realtime: Reference implementation includes hook integration ('Hook integration for automatic trace capture on file changes'), indicating intent for real-time capture during development. Specific mechanisms remain implementation-dependent. No performance or latency guarantees defined.
search_retrieval: Provides foundational elements: line-number ranges for positional queries, content hashes enabling position-independent tracking when code relocates, conversation URLs for traversal. Specification expects VCS blame integration ('Use VCS blame to find the revision that last touched line N') as primary query mechanism. No native search API defined.
links_sessions_to_code: Yes. Through 'related' array in conversation records with type and URL fields. Supports linking to sessions, prompts, and other resources. Each conversation record includes url field pointing to the conversation itself, and line ranges map which code lines were produced by which conversation. Model ID also links to specific AI model used.
privacy_security: Specification explicitly excludes 'legal ownership or copyright' tracking and does not address access controls. No data encryption, redaction, or secret-handling guidance provided. Implementers must independently design security layers and determine what trace data requires protection. No privacy-by-default mechanisms specified.
scale: No explicit scale claims, performance benchmarks, or capacity metrics provided. Specification is unopinionated about infrastructure, so performance depends entirely on storage implementation choice.
lesson_for_parinn: Agent Trace's strength is vendor-neutral flexibility and extensibility (metadata with reverse-domain notation, multi-VCS support). However, its weakness—deliberate incompleteness on storage, concurrent writes, merge strategies, and security—creates standardization uncertainty. For ParleyInn's security-first model, being more prescriptive about these safety-critical concerns (e.g., requiring append-only semantics, specifying conflict resolution for auditing, mandating per-record signatures) would strengthen the invariants and prevent unsafe implementations. The spec's philosophy 'we expect to see different implementations' works for best-effort attribution but not for security guarantees or forensic integrity.
notes: Agent Trace is in early RFC phase (v0.1.0, January 2026). Reported backers/contributors include Cursor, Cognition, Cloudflare, Vercel, Jules, Amp, OpenCode. Reference implementation in TypeScript (trace-store.ts, trace-hook.ts) available in GitHub but not directly accessible via public fetch. No confirmed production implementations beyond reference code and early tools like Cline. GitHub repository assumed at cursor-ai/agent-trace but not directly verified via web search.

name: agent-memory (xChuCx)
category: in-repo git-native memory (curated project knowledge as Markdown in the repo, served over MCP)
status: shipped
what_is_stored: Curated, agent-proposed project knowledge, not raw session history. Durable categories: conventions.md, decisions.md (each section needs Date, Status of active/superseded/deprecated/proposed, and Confidence), pitfalls.md, modules/<name>.md, write-once archive/<date>-*.md, and a server-maintained index.md. Ephemeral categories: branch-scoped working notes in local/current.<branch-slug>.md, cross-branch notes in local/current.shared.md, and per-day agent-written session summaries in sessions/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md, written through intent=session_log. Pending proposals live in staging/<id>/ (proposal.json, target-checksums.json, files/). The audit log is meta/rejection-log.jsonl, and fetch writes grounding nonces to a SQLite NonceStore. It does not capture transcripts, prompts or tool calls: I found no transcript, JSONL or hook ingestion in internal/ at commit 978421c. Sources: README https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory ; design doc sections 8-10 https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/agent-memory-design-doc-v0.4.1.md ; nonce code https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/internal/memory/fetch.go
where_stored: Working-tree files under .agent-memory/ in the project repo. Only the durable files are git-tracked by default: index.md, conventions.md, decisions.md, pitfalls.md, modules/, archive/, meta/manifest.yaml, meta/schema.yaml. The committed .agent-memory/.gitignore excludes local/, sessions/, staging/, meta/*.sqlite, the lock files and rejection-log.jsonl, so session logs and working notes stay on each machine unless the manifest sets git.track_local or git.track_sessions to true (the design doc advises against this for teams). The SQLite FTS5 index (meta/index.sqlite, pure-Go modernc.org/sqlite) is a gitignored local cache that can be rebuilt. Federated read-only "landscape" stores are cloned into the gitignored meta/cache/stores/<name>/ and pinned by commit in meta/stores.lock, which is committed. Sources: https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/.agent-memory/.gitignore ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/.agent-memory/meta/manifest.yaml ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/internal/memory/sync.go ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/go.mod
format_and_model: Plain Markdown is the source of truth. The basic unit is a section: a heading followed by an immutable `<!-- @id: kebab-slug -->` anchor that is unique within its file and survives renames and moves. Edits are byte-preserving: a goldmark AST finds the section and the engine splices bytes, so untouched text is never reflowed. Agents never write files directly. They send a ProposeRequest of structured operations (create_file, append_section, replace_section, append_to_section, replace_section_content, archive_section, remove_section, rename_heading) with an intent (update_current, update_shared, session_log, add_pitfall, record_decision, refresh_module, update_conventions, archive_stale), provenance sources (type file|test|user|session|inference|external, plus a ref), a confidence level and, since v0.6.0, a GroundingReceipt (pack_digest plus a single-use read_nonce from an earlier fetch). A per-category approval policy in manifest.yaml routes each proposal. Decisions, conventions, modules, archive and pitfall replacements are staged. New pitfalls, current notes and sessions apply at once. index.md is server-only. Since v0.6.1 the category, not the caller's intent, decides routing. Writes use atomic rename. There is no hash chain: tamper evidence is limited to an on-demand SHA-256 Merkle root (`agent-memory digest`) and git history. Sources: design doc sections 12 and 15-16 https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/agent-memory-design-doc-v0.4.1.md ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/internal/memory/provenance.go ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/CHANGELOG.md
multi_writer_and_merge:
On one host, writers take an exclusive kernel advisory lock (gofrs/flock on .agent-memory/meta/lock, auto-released on crash, 10 s default wait, then a LockHeld error), and per the README fetch takes a shared lock. Staged proposals carry target checksums and, since v0.6.1, whole-file pre-state SHA-256 (PreHashes). `apply` fails with target_drift if a file changed, and `rebase` re-plans the proposal against the new state. The design doc says distributed coordination is out of scope ("concurrency is single-host"). Across machines, git is the only transport. `merge-driver --install` writes the committed `.agent-memory/.gitattributes` line `*.md merge=agent-memory` and registers the driver in .git/config, which every clone must do once. The driver runs a recursive section-tree 3-way merge keyed by @id:
- A section added on one side is kept, so concurrent appends union cleanly.
- A section changed on one side takes that side.
- A section changed differently on both sides gets a `<!-- @merge-conflict -->` block and is left unmerged for a human.
- Since v0.6.1 (AM-008), delete vs unchanged deletes, and delete vs modified conflicts. The header comment in merge.go still describes the older keep-on-delete rule, but the code implements AM-008.
- Parse failure falls back to git's default merge.

Branch isolation comes from per-branch local/current.<slug>.md files, and each worktree has its own local/. Sources: design doc section 11 https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/agent-memory-design-doc-v0.4.1.md ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/internal/markdown/merge.go ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/internal/git/merge_driver.go ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/internal/cli/merge_driver.go
realtime: None. Sharing goes through ordinary git commit, push and pull. git.auto_stage_changes and git.auto_commit both default to false. When auto_commit is on, each apply makes a 'chore(memory):' commit and never pushes. Automatic background push/pull sync is only a roadmap item for v1.0.0. Within one machine, several agent processes (for example Claude Code and Cursor) see each other's writes at once through the shared files and lock. Sources: https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/.agent-memory/meta/manifest.yaml ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/internal/git/commit.go ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/ROADMAP.md
search_retrieval: There are 3 MCP tools over stdio: memory.fetch_context, memory.propose_update and memory.status. The README CLI help for `mcp` lists only the first two, the MCP tools table lists all three. With an empty query, fetch_context returns a bootstrap pack: local/current.<branch>.md + current.shared.md + conventions.md + the index.md summary, about 12,000 characters by default. With a query, it runs a BM25 search over the SQLite FTS5 shadow index (memory_sections keyed by file and section_id). Since 0.6.1 queries match any term and drop stopwords. Results are re-ranked by scope, active branch and git-changed files, then packed under a character budget (24,000 by default). Federated stores contribute at most 20 candidates each, local results win ties (priority multiplier 0.8), and there is cross-store dedup. Self-reported quality on a 28-query / 28-section labeled benchmark: recall@5 0.98, MRR 0.97. There are no vectors, by design. Sources: README https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/internal/memory/fetch.go ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/docs/eval/retrieval.md
links_sessions_to_code: Only weakly. Provenance sources cite code paths or tests (for example {"type":"file","ref":"internal/auth/session.go"}). Ranking boosts sections tied to the active branch and to git-changed files. lock.info records an informational owner_id (for example "claude-code-session-abc"). Optional auto_commit puts memory changes into the same git history as code. There is no mapping from session or prompt to commit, no transcript capture, and session logs are agent-written daily summaries that git ignores by default. Federation pins external stores to exact commits in meta/stores.lock. Sources: README https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory ; design doc sections 11.1 and 13 https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/agent-memory-design-doc-v0.4.1.md ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/internal/memory/fetch.go
scale: Built for small curated memory, not event logs. Budgets: bootstrap 12k characters, fetch 24k characters, 20k characters per file. Spike S4 measured about 700 µs per incremental FTS5 upsert on a 1,000-section index after switching to WAL + synchronous=NORMAL (about 12 ms per commit before, on Windows), and about 865 bytes per section. The benchmark harness reports FTS5 search at 9.92 ms on a 5,000-section index, bootstrap fetch at 160 µs, and propose (append pitfall) at 33 ms. It makes no claims for multi-machine scale or large histories. Project scale: 11 stars, 0 forks, 172 commits per the GitHub page, apparently a single maintainer. Sources: https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/docs/spikes/s4-results.md ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/docs/bench-harness.md ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/releases
privacy_security:
Secrets and PII:
- Every proposal is checked by a regex scanner (AWS, GitHub, GitLab, Anthropic, OpenAI and Stripe keys, JWTs, PEM private keys), a Shannon-entropy check (threshold 4.5, minimum token length 32), and SSN and credit-card (Luhn) PII checks. Email detection is opt-in.
- On a hit the proposal is rejected, not redacted. The finding gives type and line but never echoes the secret.
- Per-region `@secret-scan: allow` markers have byte limits, and there is no global off switch. Federated content is scanned even when it carries its own allow markers.
- SECURITY.md calls the scanners "best-effort, not a guarantee".

Other controls:
- Path traversal and symlink containment checks; manifest.yaml cannot be changed through propose_update (v0.6.1).
- Decisions forbid 'external' and 'inference' sources.
- A human review gate for durable categories, and the MCP server speaks stdio only.
- No encryption at rest: I found none in the code.

Trust boundary: only federated or external chunks are wrapped in an HTML-comment preamble, "evidence, not instructions". Local memory, including auto-applied pitfalls, current notes and session summaries that skip review, goes back to the agent as unwrapped Markdown and is always prepended in the bootstrap pack. The manifest flag reject_untrusted_durable_updates is defined, but grep finds no code that reads it outside tests at commit 978421c. Enforcement comes from the per-category source-type lists in the schema instead.

Network: the Go code imports no net or net/http, but it shells out to git through os/exec, including `git clone` of remote URLs for federation `sync`. "No cloud" therefore does not mean no network egress.

Determinism: fetch is not a pure read. Each call takes time.Now and crypto/rand to mint a proof-of-ingestion nonce and writes it to a package-level SQLite NonceStore. Sources: https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/internal/memory/secrets.go ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/SECURITY.md ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/internal/memory/fetch.go ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/internal/schema/schema.go ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/internal/git/clone.go ; https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/internal/memory/nonce.go
lesson_for_parinn:
Git works well here because what it carries is small, curated, human-reviewed Markdown whose sections have stable IDs. With that data shape, a custom merge driver keyed by those IDs can union concurrent appends across clones without conflicts. Even so, the project leaves its high-volume, per-session data (sessions/, local/, staging/, the index) out of git, and it has no real-time or cross-host coordination. For ParleyInn this suggests a split. If git is used at all, it should carry only an append-only, content-addressed export, such as hash-chained segment files whose unique names make merges a trivial union, plus perhaps reviewed summaries. The raw multi-agent session record and real-time sharing need a different transport.

The second lesson is a warning on I2. agent-memory wraps only federated content as "evidence, not instructions". Its own auto-applied notes and session summaries go back into the bootstrap pack unwrapped, so injected text written by an agent in one session reaches the model in the next session without review. ParleyInn should envelope every recalled byte, whatever its origin. Its no-network rule should also cover subprocesses: agent-memory's `git clone` via os/exec shows how "no net imports" still leaks egress.
license: Apache-2.0. Sources: https://github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory/blob/978421c051fa62931d0f1b8ce5d7105857df5706/LICENSE and https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/xChuCx/agent-memory. Go 1.25+, CGo-free. Six direct dependencies: gofrs/flock, modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk, cobra, goldmark, yaml.v3, modernc.org/sqlite. Release status: v0.6.1, published 2026-09-23, pre-1.0, and the latest tag as of 2026-10-02. The last commit on main is 978421c (2026-10-01). Roadmap milestone v0.7.0, targeted for Q3 2026, had not shipped by early October 2026. VTP-1 (the Verifiable Task Protocol) is labelled experimental in the README.

name: agent-sync (lidongpeng36)
status: shipped
what_is_stored:
agent-sync has no store of its own. It copies the files that coding agents already keep in their home directories between two machines. For Claude Code it handles session transcripts at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl. It also handles each session's sidecar folder: subagent transcripts at <uuid>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl and tool-result files at <uuid>/tool-results/*. Project memory is the third Claude resource: top-level *.md files under projects/<project>/memory/, including the MEMORY.md index. The source excludes everything outside projects/, which leaves out history.jsonl, todos and settings. For Codex it syncs rollouts, archives, history/index, catalog timestamps and memory. For OpenCode it syncs portable session exports only. It never copies credentials, settings, plugins, caches, lock files or SQLite databases (README; claude.rs archive_excluded). It also keeps some state of its own:
- disposable per-peer hash checkpoints and transaction journals under the OS cache directory (agent-sync/state)
- a random node-id
- plaintext memory 'baselines' under ~/.local/share/agent-sync/memory-baselines, or ~/Library/Application Support on macOS
- tar.gz backups inside the agent root, e.g. ~/.claude/agent-sync-backups
- a copy of its own binary on the peer at ~/.cache/agent-sync/remotes/<version>/agent-sync
Sources: README, ARCHITECTURE.md, src/state.rs, src/remote.rs.
where_stored: Files in place on each machine. History stays in the agents' own home directories (~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.local/share/opencode) on the local machine and on one SSH peer. Sync state lives in the local cache and data directories, and backups sit inside the agent root. Nothing goes to a server, git or a cloud service. There are also portable single-file .tar.gz archives (export/import), each holding a manifest.json and a payload/ folder.
format_and_model:
The format is whatever the agent writes; agent-sync adds no format of its own. The data model is file-level manifests: path, SHA-256, size and mtime, plus, for JSONL, the newest event timestamp. A Claude 'session bundle' is the main <uuid>.jsonl plus its sidecar folder. Subagents and tool results always travel with their parent session.

Validation of Claude JSONL (src/adapters/claude.rs validate_claude_jsonl):
- no blank lines
- every line is a JSON object
- every record's sessionId equals the UUID in the path, and agentId matches agent-<id> for subagents
- record uuid values are unique, valid UUIDs
- RFC3339 timestamps; the newest one becomes the file's mtime

Codex rollouts are compared as parsed JSON records, so key order and whitespace are ignored. Memory is plain Markdown with name/description frontmatter, linked from MEMORY.md.

Archives carry a versioned manifest with per-file sizes and SHA-256. The remote helper speaks a typed serde protocol over SSH stdin/stdout, currently version 8. There is no hash chain or signature over history; hashes only detect change and check transfers.
multi_writer_and_merge:
The tool is pairwise: one local machine and one SSH peer per run. Hub-and-spoke use is implied, since locks 'serialize mini I/O and writes across multiple peers' (ARCHITECTURE.md).

How sessions merge:
- Same SHA means identical.
- If one JSONL is a strict byte prefix of the other, the longer one wins, a 'linear advance' (file_prefix).
- Files that exist on only one side are unioned.
- A true divergence is kept as a fork. The running side's copy keeps the original session ID. The other side's bundle is copied under a fork ID: UUIDv5, with the parent session UUID as namespace and, as name, the 'uuid' of the first differing record (or the SHA-256 of that line). Running the same rule recursively folds an existing fork forward instead of creating a duplicate.
- Making a fork rewrites sessionId/session_id in every JSONL line of the forked bundle. It re-serializes each line with serde_json without preserve_order, so key order changes and the bytes differ from the original (copy_session_member; Cargo.lock).
- Deletions are never propagated; sync is additive only.

How memory merges:
- independent Markdown heading blocks merge on their own
- a three-way diff3 runs against a 'baseline', a memory snapshot both machines verified at the last sync
- leftover conflicts follow the chosen strategy: ask (local, remote or $EDITOR with <<<<<<< markers), local, or remote
- an optional LLM backend can resolve leftovers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Codex or OpenCode

How concurrent writers are handled:
- Live Claude sessions are found from the sessions/*.json process list plus lsof write descriptors. The union of active IDs on both sides is skipped, together with the shared memory and indexes of the affected projects.
- An unknown writer stops the run.
- Locks on both machines are taken in a stable node-ID order.
- A plan is rejected if anything changed after the preview.
- Both sides are backed up before any write.
- A transaction journal on each side moves through prepared, local_applied, remote_applied and verified. An unfinished journal blocks later writes.
Sources: README, AGENTS.md.
realtime: None. It is a manual, on-demand CLI with a read-only preview by default; --apply, or --apply --yes in scripts, actually writes. There is no daemon, watcher or push, and live sessions are skipped on purpose until they close. The architecture document lists 'append-aware JSONL range transfer' only as a possible later step (README, ARCHITECTURE.md).
search_retrieval: Not applicable. It offers no search, index or recall. Its outputs are human, JSON and full unified-diff (--format diff) views of a sync plan. The README warns that diff output can contain complete session and memory content and should be treated as sensitive.
links_sessions_to_code: No. It does not link sessions to commits, files or repos. Sessions are keyed only by Claude's project folder name, which encodes the working directory, plus the session UUID. I found no remapping of project paths in the source, so folder names are copied as they are. Two machines with different home paths therefore get separate project folders; this is my inference from the code, not a documented claim. The only git link is an example in the README, where a memory statement about 'git lfs prune --dry-run' is used to illustrate evidence review.
privacy_security:
Transport and remote execution:
- OpenSSH is the only trust boundary. The tool keeps the user's ssh config, ProxyJump, ssh-agent and known_hosts, and does not weaken host-key checks.
- Remote reads go through an explicit rsync allowlist (--files-from, --checksum, --compress).
- The remote helper is the same binary. It is checked by SHA-256, uploaded atomically with umask 077 and chmod 700, and its typed protocol deliberately has no arbitrary-command request.
- User values are never placed into shell snippets, except in a fixed bootstrap script.

Exclusions:
- Credentials, settings, plugins, caches, lock files and SQLite databases are excluded.
- OpenCode auth, account and permission tables never travel.
- Archives reject unsafe paths, symlinks, undeclared files and oversized expansion, and are written 0600.

What is missing:
- No content redaction or secret scanning: transcripts and tool results are copied byte-for-byte.
- No encryption at rest: backups are plain tar.gz files in the agent root, and baselines and checkpoints are plaintext.
- Confidentiality in transit depends entirely on SSH.

Optional semantic backends:
- They send memory text, plus the baseline when there is one, to OpenAI, Anthropic, a Codex process or an OpenCode process.
- They are opt-in, but once configured they run during preview as well.
- API keys stay on the coordinating machine and never enter SSH payloads, argv or diagnostics. URL credentials, query strings and redirects are rejected.
- Model output is written into memory files that agents later load automatically. The mechanical checks (fingerprint binding, no conflict markers, quoting at least 12 characters of verbatim evidence from immutable originals, edits capped at 4096 bytes) narrow this path but do not close it. The README admits that 'semantic claims remain model judgments'.

Because of those backends the binary links reqwest, so it does talk to the network.
Sources: README, ARCHITECTURE.md, Cargo.toml, src/transport.rs.
scale:
No scale claims or benchmarks. The CHANGELOG for 0.8.1 reports 106 unit tests and 11 CLI integration tests. It also reports a validation run on isolated copies of 281 conflicting Codex sessions: 280 became equivalent histories after the official migration, one was a strict append, and the second preview showed zero changes.

The project is very young:
- 28 commits by one author, from 2026-08-10 to 2026-09-20
- about 19.5k lines of Rust and tests (my count from a clone)
- 1 star and 0 forks on GitHub
- 263 total downloads on crates.io across 13 versions
Sources: git log, GitHub releases page, crates.io API.
license: MIT
lesson_for_parinn:
Two things carry over directly. Treat 'strict prefix' as the only automatic merge. When histories truly diverge, name the fork deterministically, so every machine that sees the split arrives at the same fork ID without coordinating: agent-sync uses UUIDv5 of the parent session with the first differing record. For ParleyInn that becomes fork ID = H(parent chain ID ‖ hash of the first differing event), and fork detection is simply the first unequal chain hash.

What not to copy: agent-sync builds a fork by rewriting sessionId in every record and re-serializing the lines, which changes their bytes. In ParleyInn that would break the hash chain and make the history impossible to verify against the original. ParleyInn should record a fork as a separate, append-only branch record that points at the parent chain and the divergence event, and leave the original events unchanged.

Its other rules also fit ParleyInn's I6 and I9:
- Hash caches and checkpoints are only an optimization and never decide correctness.
- An unknown writer stops the sync.
- An unfinished journal blocks later writes until someone looks at it.

Its optional LLM memory merge is an example of the automatic path from untrusted content to the model that I2 forbids.

name: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol
status: shipped
what_is_stored: Agent Cards (JSON metadata declaring agent identity, capabilities, authentication requirements); Tasks with strict lifecycle states (SUBMITTED, WORKING, INPUT_REQUIRED, COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED, REJECTED); Messages organized into Parts (text, file, data, URI references, raw bytes); Artifacts (tangible outputs from task execution); Task status and message history; Context information groupable by contextId (server-generated identifier for conversation threads)
where_stored: Agent Cards published at /.well-known/agent-card.json endpoints; Task storage in shared persistent stores (SQL databases, Redis, or Git repositories); Context storage in database/cache accessible to multiple agents, or embedded directly in message payloads; Cryptographic keys stored in Hardware Security Modules (HSM) or cloud Key Management Services, never in source code or container images
format_and_model: Canonical data model defined in Protocol Buffers; JSON Schema for validation; Three-layer spec: Data (Protobuf/JSON Schema) → Operations (abstract verbs independent of transport) → Bindings (JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTPS/TLS 1.3+, gRPC, HTTP+JSON/REST); Messages use Part-based structure (discriminated union); Agent Cards signed with JSON Web Signatures (RFC 7515) using JCS canonicalization (RFC 8785)
multi_writer_and_merge: Multiple agents coordinate through strict task state machine without exposing internal state. Three coordination patterns: (1) Shared Storage—agents reference contextId to retrieve conversation history from centralized store; (2) Embedded Context—coordinator includes summarized context directly in message payloads; (3) Per-Agent State—agents maintain own context stores keyed by contextId. No explicit git merge semantics; a2ahub reference implementation uses Git as durable state where either agent can rebuild view from repository. Transport abstraction allows swapping HTTP, gRPC, etc. without rewriting agent logic. Token downscoping (RFC 8693) enables privilege reduction in delegation chains.
realtime: Server-Sent Events (SSE) for asynchronous updates instead of polling. SubscribeToTask operation streams TaskStatusUpdateEvent and TaskArtifactUpdateEvent. Push notifications via webhook URLs registered through CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig. Handles disconnections and variable execution times across distributed agents. Optional immediate HTTP polling fallback for clients unable to maintain SSE connections.
search_retrieval: Task retrieval by ID via GetTask operation. Context history retrievable via contextId (conversation thread identifier). SubscribeToTask for real-time monitoring of task progress. No full-text search explicitly specified in core v1.0 spec. Message Parts carry metadata (type, schemaVersion) for content discrimination. Conversation threads persist via contextId linking many task IDs in single thread.
links_sessions_to_code: Agent Cards link agents to declared capabilities and skill definitions. Some implementations (a2ahub) use Git repositories as shared state space, enabling both agents to inspect durable artifacts and rebuild view from commit history. Task artifacts can contain structured JSON data linked to agent operations. No built-in linking to source code repositories in core A2A spec; agent implementation details remain opaque to protocol. Token downscoping enables tracking privilege delegation chains.
privacy_security: Multiple authentication schemes: OAuth 2.0 with scope claims per skill, OpenID Connect (OIDC) for cryptographic identity assertion, Mutual TLS (mTLS) with X.509 certificates. Signed Agent Cards via JWS (RFC 7515) with JCS canonicalization prevent tampering and prompt injection attacks on capability declarations. Sender-constrained tokens (RFC 8705, RFC 9449) prevent token replay attacks. Token Exchange (RFC 8693) enables privilege downscoping in delegation chains. Recommended 'zero-trust' posture combining mTLS with OAuth2. OpenTelemetry with W3C Trace Context for end-to-end observability. No field-level encryption in wire format; security relies on TLS 1.3+. No automatic redaction mechanism; coordinators control what each agent sees via embedded context. Private key management via HSM or cloud KMS required for production.
lesson_for_parinn: A2A's layered separation (canonical data → abstract operations → transport bindings) provides a blueprint for ParleyInn's multi-transport future without compromising the core record. Most valuable: A2A's use of cryptographically signed Agent Cards (JWS + JCS) to prevent prompt injection on capability declarations—analogous to ParleyInn's need to protect constraint blocks as TrustedText. The a2ahub pattern (Git as durable state, rebuild-from-repo auditability) aligns with ParleyInn's append-only principle but A2A allows task state mutations. For ParleyInn, combining A2A's signed manifests with strict append-only semantics (beyond A2A) would strengthen agent isolation and session auditability: constraints remain cryptographically grounded, and the record can never silently degrade via state mutations. Consider whether A2A's contextId grouping (many tasks per thread) maps to ParleyInn's session-level compaction strategy.

name: agentattest (AuroraAeon/agentattest)
category: Signed attestation of agent runs: an in-toto predicate, a deterministic verifier and a merge-gate policy. It is not a session store.
status: shipped
what_is_stored:
One in-toto Statement v1 JSON document per agent run. It holds no transcript, prompt or tool output, only metadata, references and SHA-256 digests (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/docs/DATA_MODEL.md).

Subjects:
- The docs allow `patch.diff`, `repo-tree`, `pr-<n>` and build artifacts as subjects.
- The CLI and the capture SDK actually emit one subject: `patch.diff` = sha256 of the raw output of `git diff --binary --no-color` (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/internal/predicate/create.go, https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/internal/gitbind/gitbind.go).

Required predicate fields: predicateVersion, runId, verificationLevel (evidence-grade / policy-grade / high-assurance), repo (url, baseCommit, optional headCommit, branch, pullRequest), agent (self-asserted name, version, invocationKind, declaredIdentity), environment (executionType, builder, witnesses), humanApproval (state, reviewerRefs), privacy declarations, timestamps, and evidence[]. Each evidence entry has type, uri, sha256, storage and visibility.

Optional fields: model, runtime (OTel/OpenInference trace IDs; when present, a trace evidence entry with URI and digest is required), changes, sidecars (SPDX/CycloneDX/OpenVEX references), materials, and extensions (closed, digest-only).

v1 additions (https://agentattest.dev/predicate/v1): capture.method (harness-native / wrapper / ci-step / manual), agentConfig (digest of AGENTS.md and rule files), mcpServers and tools (manifest and schema digests), and delegation.delegationChain (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/README.md).

Locally:
- `.agentattest/` SQLite cache with three tables, refs, digests and timestamps (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/internal/cache/cache.go).
- An opt-in SQLite registry with one table mapping subject_digest to repo_url, run_id, predicate_type, level, statement_path and indexed_at (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/internal/registry/registry.go).
- Neither stores pass/fail results or statement bytes.
where_stored:
Local file, plus attestation stores the project delegates to but does not itself write.

- `predicate create --out` writes the statement as a local JSON file (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/README.md).
- Signing is delegated. The library's `Sign` wraps the payload in a DSSE envelope using a caller-supplied crypto.Signer. The CLI has no sign command, and nothing in the repo requests a Fulcio certificate (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/internal/signing/signing.go, https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/internal/app/app.go).
- Keyless Sigstore signing and storage in GitHub Artifact Attestations or Rekor is meant to be done by external tools: cosign, `actions/attest` in custom-predicate mode, or `gh attestation` (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/docs/EXISTING_WHEELS.md). agentattest only ingests the resulting bundles with `verify bundle`.
- The shipped composite Action does not call actions/attest and does not request id-token. It builds an unsigned statement in $RUNNER_TEMP, verifies it at evidence-grade by default and writes a summary to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/action/action.yml, https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/action/README.md).
- Trace documents live wherever the evidence URI points, for example `artifact://...`.
- The TUF trust-root cache lives in os.UserCacheDir()/agentattest/tuf (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/docs/VERIFICATION_MODEL.md).
- Nothing is written to git notes, refs or branches.
format_and_model:
Container and envelope:
- JSON in-toto Statement v1 (`_type`, `subject[]`, `predicateType`, `predicate`).
- DSSE envelope, payloadType application/vnd.in-toto+json, via go-securesystemslib (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/internal/signing/signing.go).
- Sigstore bundle JSON for keyless verification.

Validation (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/docs/VERIFICATION_MODEL.md):
- The predicate is validated by JSON Schema 2020-12 (closed objects, additionalProperties: false) and by CUE for cross-field rules, kept in lockstep.
- Policy is OPA Rego.
- A five-phase verifier runs Go version routing, then schema, then CUE, then Rego, then Go failure-code ordering. It returns `{valid, level, failureCodes[]}` with 18 stable failure-code strings.

Data model:
- One standalone statement per run. Statements are not chained to each other (no prev-hash) and carry no sequence number.
- The CLI's runId is `run_<UTC timestamp>_<pid>` (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/internal/predicate/create.go).
- Patch binding hashes exact bytes with no semantic normalization: a reformat or rebase breaks the binding, and the documented fix is to re-capture under a new runId (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/docs/DATA_MODEL.md).

Caveat (my inference from git semantics, not tested): plain `git diff` compares the working tree with the index (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff). So the bound patch covers only unstaged changes. In a clean CI checkout of committed work it would hash empty input.

Versioning: a breaking change needs a new predicate URI. The predicate URIs are identifiers only; https://agentattest.dev/predicate/v0 returned HTTP 503 when fetched on 2026-10-02.
multi_writer_and_merge:
There is no merge model.
- Each run produces an independent, immutable claim. Many attestations can exist for one subject; the registry key is (subject_digest, statement_path) (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/internal/registry/registry.go).
- Multiple agents in one run are described only by a self-asserted `delegation.delegationChain` inside a single statement. At policy-grade and above, every step's agentRef must appear in a verifier-supplied `verifiedDelegation` allowlist, or the check fails closed (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/docs/DATA_MODEL.md).
- Concurrency and ordering across writers are left to the external store (GitHub attestations or Rekor).
realtime: None. Statements are created after a run and verified at PR or merge time. There is no streaming, subscription or live sharing (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/action/README.md).
search_retrieval:
Exact-key lookup only; no content search.
- The opt-in local SQLite registry offers BySubject(digest), ByRepo(url) and ByRunID. It returns statement paths, never statement bytes, and is never a trust root (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/internal/registry/registry.go).
- Remote retrieval is delegated to `gh attestation download/verify` (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/docs/EXISTING_WHEELS.md).
- Trace content is left to OTel backends. The non-goals explicitly exclude becoming a trace search or observability backend (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/docs/NON_GOALS.md).
links_sessions_to_code:
Yes; this is its whole purpose.

What it binds: runId, agent and model metadata, the AGENTS.md digest, the MCP surface, and the trace IDs plus trace-document digest. These are tied to the patch.diff sha256, repo URL, base and head commit, branch, PR number and human-approval state (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/docs/DATA_MODEL.md).

How the session is linked: only by reference, through the OTel/OpenInference trace URI and digest. The session content is never embedded. The capture SDK requires trace IDs, URI and digest for harness-native capture and lists Claude Code as an example harness (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/docs/examples/capture.md).

How the verifier checks it, all from explicit verifier context:
- Statement subjects must equal the recomputed subjects as a set.
- Replay is checked against expected PR and runId.
- Freshness uses `context.now`; the policy reads no clock (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/policies/default.rego).
privacy_security:
Privacy defaults:
- Raw prompts and tool outputs are not stored by default. stored=false forces visibility none, and raw evidence can never be public.
- Visibility classes are public / team / secret / encrypted.
- Evidence URIs reject `data:` payloads and HTTP userinfo credentials.
- Extensions are closed, digest-only and never public.
- Only metadata-shaped evidence types may go to a transparency log: local-log-root, builder-record, agent-config, mcp-server.
- Identity, reviewer, MCP and tool names must match non-PII patterns (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/docs/PRIVACY_MODEL.md).

Self-declared limits:
- The checks are structural. Referenced content is never scanned, and the docs say redaction is "not a proof of safety".
- No encryption is implemented. "encrypted" is a label pointing at blobs whose keys are controlled elsewhere.
- tools[].schemaDigest is not checked by policy (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/docs/SECURITY_REVIEW.md).

Trust model (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):
- Agent and model fields are self-asserted. Trust comes from the verified certificate identity: the Fulcio SAN plus the OIDC-issuer OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.1.
- The chain must lead to a Fulcio root, supplied as explicit PEM or fetched over the network from Sigstore TUF. That fetch fails closed and is the only network path.
- An RFC 6962 Rekor inclusion proof is checked through transparency-dev/merkle, optionally pinned to a known root hash.
- A test enforces that crypto imports appear only in internal/signing.
- External commands run as argv arrays, never shell strings.

Gaps found by reading the code (not tested against live bundles):
- Chain verification sets no CurrentTime, so certificate validity is checked against wall-clock now (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/internal/signing/signing.go). Fulcio certificates are valid 10 minutes (https://docs.sigstore.dev/certificate_authority/overview/). A genuine keyless bundle would therefore likely fail once its certificate expires, because neither the Rekor integrated time nor a signed timestamp is used.
- The tlog entry's canonicalizedBody is not checked against the verified envelope (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/internal/signing/rekor.go).
- The release workflow neither signs nor attests its own binaries (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/.github/workflows/release.yml).
scale:
The project makes no scale or performance claims. It is a very early, single-maintainer project:
- 1 star, 0 forks, 0 watchers (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest).
- One release, v0.1.0, tagged 2026-09-23 (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/releases). The CHANGELOG dates it 2026-09-19 (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/CHANGELOG.md).
- From the clone: 20 commits, almost all on 2026-09-22/23 after an April 2026 bootstrap; about 4.7k lines of Go under internal/ including tests; 46 golden fixtures (34 v0, 12 v1).

No adopters or third-party technical discussion could be verified; the session's web-search budget was exhausted, so I could not search for either.
license: Apache-2.0 (https://github.com/AuroraAeon/agentattest/blob/v0.1.0/LICENSE)
lesson_for_parinn:
Publish a signed claim to git or GitHub, not the session.

1. Shape of the claim. For each session segment or commit, ParleyInn could emit an in-toto Statement v1:
   - subject = git commit/tree object IDs;
   - predicate = the ParleyInn hash-chain head and segment range, by digest plus an opaque URI;
   - transcript content excluded by design. Borrow agentattest's rules: visibility classes, `data:`/userinfo URI rejection, closed digest-only extensions, and a transparency-log allowlist.
   This keeps stored history out of any automatic model path (I2).

2. Keep the network outside ParleyInn. Signing and distribution belong to external tools (cosign, actions/attest, gh attestation), so ParleyInn's core never talks to the network (I4). In agentattest the TUF fetch is the only network path.

3. Pass time and identity in as inputs. agentattest's verifier takes `now`, expected PR/runId and verified signer identity as explicit context, which is the property I10 needs.

4. Avoid two of its mistakes:
   - Don't bind to `git diff` bytes. Plain `git diff` omits committed work, and any reformat breaks the binding. Bind to git's own content addresses.
   - Verify certificate validity at the logged signing time, not wall-clock now, or short-lived keyless certificates become unverifiable after 10 minutes.

name: AgentBlame (mesa-dot-dev/agentblame, npm @mesadev/agentblame)
category: git-notes line attribution + PR overlay (browser extension)
status: shipped. It is on npm as @mesadev/agentblame 3.1.12, in the Chrome Web Store and on Firefox Add-ons. It has been dormant since February 2026 but is not archived. The last commit on main and the last npm release are both dated 2026-02-09. The repo has 53 commits, 101 stars and 7 forks. 3 PRs are open, including an outside PR from 2026-05-14 ('Safe Migration from JSONL -> Sqlite') that has not been merged. The first release was on 2026-01-13/14.
what_is_stored:
This describes note format v3, merged 2026-02-02 (PR #39), which is the current code. Each commit that has AI lines gets one JSON git note with these fields:
- version 3 and a timestamp.
- A `sessions` map. The key is a 16-hex session id, defined as SHA256(agent:conversation_id) truncated to 16. Each value holds the agent (cursor|claude|opencode), the model, startedAt, and a `prompts` array. Each prompt has a local DB id, an ISO timestamp, the prompt text verbatim (or null when storePromptContent=false), tool-call counts per tool, and a duration in seconds until the next prompt.
- A `files` map from file path to a list of {session, prompt id, lines:"compressed range string"}. Only AI-written ranges go into the note. Human ranges are computed but not written.

A second note holds repo-wide analytics:
- Totals of AI, human and 'unknown' lines.
- Breakdowns by agent and by model.
- Per-contributor stats, keyed by commit-author email (local writes) or GitHub login (CI writes).
- Recent PRs with title and author.
- Up to 72 hourly and 30 daily time-series points.

Local-only state:
- A global SQLite DB at ~/.agentblame/agentblame.db. Its tables: sessions (with the raw conversation_id and the repo), prompts (content plus a SHA256 for dedup), tool_calls (tool name, file path, timestamp only) and enabled_repos.
- Logs under ~/.agentblame/logs.
- An append-only delta log at .git/agentblame/working/<base_sha>/deltas.jsonl. Each record is {ts, file, sessionId|null, promptId, unified-diff hunks, afterBlob}.
- Per-conversation checkpoints at .git/agentblame/checkpoints/<id>.json.
- Before/after file snapshots, written as loose git blobs via `git hash-object -w`.

Not stored anywhere: full transcripts, assistant replies and tool inputs.

The older v2 format (up to about late January 2026) stored something different: per-range provider, model, confidence (1.0 exact / 0.95 normalized / 0.85 move), matchType and contentHash. That v2 design is what the 2026-01-26 deep-dive blog describes, so the blog is partly out of date.
where_stored:
Custom git notes refs inside the project's own repo:
- refs/notes/agentblame holds per-commit attribution. The notes tree is keyed by commit SHA.
- refs/notes/agentblame-analytics holds the analytics note, attached to the repo's root commit and anchored by a tag named agentblame-analytics-anchor.

The refs are shared by pushing them to the GitHub remote. Working state stays local: a SQLite DB in ~/.agentblame, files under .git/agentblame, and loose blobs in .git/objects.

Setup also commits config files into the working tree so teammates get the hooks:
- .claude/settings.json
- .cursor/hooks.json
- .opencode/plugin/agentblame.ts
- .github/workflows/agentblame.yml

No backend server is involved.
format_and_model:
Note format:
- Each note is a single-line JSON blob, written with `git notes --ref=refs/notes/agentblame add -f -m <json> <sha>`.
- The analytics note is pretty-printed JSON.
- The data model maps a commit SHA to a list of files, each file to line ranges, each range to a session id plus prompt id, and each session to agent, model and prompts. Line numbers refer to the committed file version.

How lines get attributed:
1. Capture comes from agent hooks:
   - Claude Code: a synchronous PreToolUse hook for Edit, Write and MultiEdit (one matcher each) plus an async PostToolUse hook with matcher '.*'.
   - Cursor: beforeSubmitPrompt and afterFileEdit.
   - OpenCode: a plugin that captures prompts through chat.message.
2. Each edit becomes before/after snapshots, then unified-diff hunks appended to deltas.jsonl.
3. A git post-commit hook (`bunx @mesadev/agentblame process HEAD || true`) replays the deltas against the committed diff. Each added line is assigned to a session and prompt, or else to human.

For Claude Code, the prompt text is taken by reading the last user message in the hook payload's transcript_path JSONL. Nothing else from the transcript is kept.

The deep-dive blog describes the earlier content-hash design: exact SHA256 matches, and whitespace-normalized hashes with confidence 0.95.
multi_writer_and_merge:
Writers and pushing:
- Every developer's post-commit hook writes to their own local refs/notes/agentblame.
- `ab init` no longer sets push or fetch refspecs. Older versions did; a removal helper still exists but nothing calls it. So the ref has to be pushed by hand with `git push origin refs/notes/agentblame` (README troubleshooting).

Fetching and conflicts:
- Before processing, the post-commit hook runs `git fetch origin refs/notes/agentblame:refs/notes/agentblame` 'to avoid push conflicts'. That refspec has no forced '+', has a 30-second timeout, and its errors are swallowed.
- The code never calls `git notes merge`. My reading of the code (not documented): once two developers' notes refs diverge, both fetch and push fail as non-fast-forward, and nobody is told.
- Git's union and cat_sort_uniq strategies concatenate text. Applied to these single-JSON notes they would produce invalid JSON (my inference).
- Writes use `-f`, so the last writer wins for a given commit.

Squash and rebase (which change commit SHAs):
- A GitHub Actions workflow runs on pull_request closed+merged, with `contents: write`. It fetches both notes refs and the PR head.
- It works out the merge type. More than one parent means a merge commit. A single parent whose subject contains #PR or the PR title means a squash. Anything else is treated as a rebase.
- It gathers the notes from the PR's commits and re-keys the AI ranges onto the new SHAs by exact line-sequence matching in the new commit's diff. Then it updates analytics and pushes the notes refs and the anchor tag. Each push is wrapped in `|| echo`, so failures are tolerated quietly.
- `ab sync` does the same job locally for merges where the workflow did not run. It looks for '#123' in commit subjects.
- For true merge commits nothing is re-keyed: the original commits stay reachable with their notes.

Cross-fork attribution does not work (open issue #34). There is no CRDT and no per-writer ref.
realtime: None. Attribution reaches other people only when someone pushes or fetches the notes refs, or when CI pushes after a PR merges. There is no streaming, no presence and no live session sharing. Capture on one machine is synchronous to local files on each hook event (PreToolUse blocks; PostToolUse is async). The browser extension fetches notes through the GitHub REST API when a page loads, and caches them.
search_retrieval:
- `ab blame <file>` merges `git blame` output with the notes to show, per line, the agent, model and prompt.
- `ab status` shows per-repo tracking stats.
- The Chrome/Firefox extension reads the notes through the GitHub REST API: GET git/refs/notes/agentblame, then git/trees/<sha>?recursive=1, then git/blobs. It draws a PR summary (AI vs human line counts and percentage), per-file badges, orange gutter markers, and hover cards showing tool, model and prompt.
- An 'Insights' analytics dashboard reads the analytics note. It shows trends, breakdowns by tool, model and contributor, and recent PRs.

There is no full-text search over prompts or sessions, and no query API beyond git notes show/list.
links_sessions_to_code: Yes, and this is the core feature. Each committed line range points to a session id, which gives the agent and model, and to a specific prompt id, which gives the prompt text and timestamp. The session id is a truncated hash of the agent's conversation id; the raw conversation id stays in the local SQLite DB. Transcripts are not linked or stored: only the last user message is pulled from Claude Code's transcript_path. The links are keyed by commit SHA, so a rewrite breaks them unless the CI workflow or `ab sync` re-keys them by content. Lines that were heavily edited after the AI wrote them, or changed outside hook capture, are left unattributed by design ('false attribution is worse than missing attribution').
scale:
No scale or performance claims are published; the deep-dive blog gives no numbers. The project itself is small: 53 commits, 101 stars, 7 forks.

Structural limits I found in the code (inferences, not documented):
- Each commit's note repeats every prompt of every session that touched it (getPromptsWithToolCounts for the whole session). Note size therefore grows with session length, and the same prompts are duplicated across commits.
- The extension lists the whole notes tree with the recursive Trees API and never checks `truncated`. GitHub caps recursive trees at 100,000 entries and 7 MB, so very large notes refs would be silently cut off.
- The analytics note stays bounded: at most 72 hourly points, 30 daily points, and a capped list of recent PRs.
privacy_security:
Prompt storage:
- `storePromptContent` defaults to true. Verbatim user prompts go into git notes, and once pushed anyone who can read the repo can read them, which for a public repo means everyone.
- The opt-out is `agentblame.storePromptContent=false` in the per-clone .git/config. It lives in each clone's .git/config, which is never committed, so each teammate has to set it separately.
- I grepped the CLI source and found no redaction, no secret scanning and no encryption.
- The local SQLite DB keeps raw prompts and conversation ids in plaintext under ~/.agentblame.
- Contributor emails or logins end up in the analytics note.

Browser extension:
- It needs a GitHub PAT: fine-grained with contents:read, or classic with repo scope. The token is kept in chrome.storage.local.
- The privacy policy says the token is sent only to api.github.com and that there is no telemetry.

Supply chain:
- The committed hook configs run unpinned `bunx @mesadev/agentblame`.
- The CI workflow runs `bunx @mesadev/agentblame@latest` with `contents: write`.
- So a compromised npm release would run on every agent tool call of every teammate and in CI with push rights.

Failure handling:
- Hooks fail open and stay silent (`2>/dev/null || true`), so lost attribution never shows up anywhere.
- The post-commit hook makes a network fetch to origin on every commit.

Prompt text read back from notes is only rendered in the browser. It is never fed back to a model, so it is not a prompt-injection channel.
lesson_for_parinn:
AgentBlame tests the 'put agent provenance in git notes' idea in practice. The upside is real: the data travels with the repo, the forge API can read it with no backend, and it works offline. Its failure modes are the ones ParleyInn must design out.

What goes wrong:
1. The notes ref must be pushed by hand and has no merge strategy, so diverged writers silently lose data.
2. Notes are keyed by commit SHA, so every squash or rebase needs a privileged CI job that re-attaches history by fuzzy content matching.
3. Verbatim prompts go by default into a ref that, on a public repo, anyone can read, with no redaction.
4. Every failure is swallowed (`|| true`, `|| echo`).

What this means for ParleyInn if git ever becomes a transport:
- Key records by session and content hash, never by commit SHA.
- Make the layout conflict-free: append-only, one object per event, per-writer refs or a union-merge-safe line format. Single-JSON notes break under union merges.
- Redact and classify before anything leaves the local store; sharing is opt-in.
- Audit and count every failed push or fetch (I6) instead of hiding it.
- Run sync in a separate, explicitly enabled process. AgentBlame's hook fetches from origin on every commit, which is exactly what ParleyInn's core may not do (I4).
license: Apache-2.0

name: agentdiff (codeprakhar25/agentdiff)
category: Signed, commit-scoped AI attribution kept in custom git refs (refs/agentdiff/*), using the Agent Trace v0.1 record shape
status: shipped. Pre-1.0 and quiet. v0.1.30 came out on 2026-06-08 on GitHub and on crates.io (329 downloads in total). Repo HEAD f9ffbd2 is that release commit, so nothing has been committed in the roughly four months to 2026-10-02. Not archived. 47 stars, 4 forks, 70 commits. Note an unrelated project named agentdiff.dev.
what_is_stored: There is one record per git commit, called an AgentTrace. Its top-level fields are: version "0.1.0"; id, a UUIDv4 that serves as the primary key instead of the commit SHA; timestamp, the committer date (%cI); vcs {type: git, revision: commit SHA}; tool.name, the agent such as claude-code; and files[]. Each file entry holds path and conversations[]. Each conversation holds contributor {type ai|human, model_id} and ranges[] {start_line, end_line}. Optional metadata.agentdiff holds: prompt_excerpt (collapsed whitespace, cut to 160 characters, although the README says about 100); prompt_hash (unsalted SHA-256 of the full prompt); session_id; files_read; intent and intent_type (set by the MCP tool set_intent); trust (0-100); flags; author (git user.name); and capture_tool. An optional sig holds {alg: ed25519, key_id, value}. The line ranges are the staged diff hunks (git diff --cached -U0), not the exact lines the agent typed. Each file goes wholly to the most recent overlapping non-Copilot agent event, and a file with no event goes to "human". Raw events live only in a local .git/agentdiff/session.jsonl and are never pushed. They carry the prompt (Claude: the latest ~/.claude/history.jsonl entry, up to 500 characters including pasted text), the model (read from ~/.claude/projects/**/{session}.jsonl), the tool, the file, line guesses, and old/new snippets of up to 200 characters. Public keys are stored as base64 in refs/agentdiff/keys/{key_id}:pub.key.
where_stored: There are three tiers, all inside the git repo and none in the working tree. Tier 1 is a local buffer at .git/agentdiff/traces/{branch}.jsonl, with "/" in branch names written as %2F. Tier 2 is a per-branch custom ref, refs/agentdiff/traces/{branch}, whose commit tree holds a single traces.jsonl. The README calls it "per developer", but the code keys it by branch only. Tier 3 is a permanent ref, refs/agentdiff/meta:traces.jsonl, which CI consolidates when a pull request merges. Keys go in refs/agentdiff/keys/{key_id}. Global config and the private key sit in ~/.agentdiff/: config.toml, and keys/private.key, an unencrypted base64 seed with mode 0600. An optional policy file sits at <repo>/.agentdiff/policy.toml. Refs are written locally with plumbing (hash-object, mktree, commit-tree, update-ref). They reach the remote only through the GitHub Git Database REST API, called by shelling out to `gh api`, because the code says git push of custom ref namespaces hangs over HTTPS. So remote writes need a GitHub or GitHub Enterprise remote (GH_HOST) and an authenticated gh. On other hosts, Forgejo included, only local refs are written. `agentdiff init` adds the fetch refspec +refs/agentdiff/*:refs/agentdiff/*, so a plain git fetch pulls teammates' refs.
format_and_model: Each tier is a JSONL file with one AgentTrace per line, in the shape of the Agent Trace spec 0.1.0 RFC from Cursor (CC BY 4.0). That spec deliberately leaves storage open ("local files, git notes, a database") and defines no signing; agentdiff adds the sig and metadata.agentdiff on top. Writing is a pipeline. Capture hooks per agent append raw events: Claude Code PostToolUse on Edit/Write/MultiEdit, Cursor afterFileEdit, Codex notify, Windsurf post_write_code, OpenCode tool.execute.after, Gemini/Antigravity AfterTool, and a VS Code extension for Copilot. Then the git pre-commit hook runs prepare-ledger.py, which writes pending-ledger.json. The post-commit hook runs finalize-ledger.py, which appends the trace, and then `agentdiff sign-entry`. Signing covers the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON with sig removed. key_id is the first 8 bytes of SHA-256(pubkey), as 16 hex characters. Each ref commit's tree holds the whole file, so every update is a new full blob that names the previous tip as parent. There is no hash chain between records. The schema has range content_hash and conversation url fields, but the finalizer never fills them.
multi_writer_and_merge: Records merge as a union keyed on UUID, and a ref update is protected only by a single compare-and-swap. Push works like this. It reads the remote ref through the API, adds local traces whose UUIDs are new, writes the whole traces.jsonl, and updates the ref with a non-force PATCH. If that is not a fast-forward (HTTP 422), it retries up to 10 times with exponential backoff from 200 ms, capped at 5 s. A code comment claims this "covers ~100 concurrent pushes at sprint-end merge bursts". Consolidate does the same into refs/agentdiff/meta and then deletes the branch ref. It runs on PR merge in GitHub Actions, or from the client's pre-push hook on direct pushes to main or master. Readers dedupe by UUID and keep the newer timestamp. Defect found by reading the code at f9ffbd2 (not run): push_content_to_ref creates the content blob once, before the retry loop. On a conflict it fetches only the new parent SHA and commits the same stale full-file blob as a fast-forward. The winning writer's traces therefore disappear from the tip file, and readers only read the tip, even though the records remain in the ref's commit history. That is a lost update: the CAS stops non-fast-forward updates but never re-merges the content. Squash, rebase and cherry-pick keep the UUID, but vcs.revision and the line numbers are never remapped. Locally, sign-entry rewrites the last line of the buffer; the only lock is a lockfile in the post-commit hook.
realtime: Not real time. Events land in the local session.jsonl on each tool call, but only on that machine. A trace exists only after a commit. Others can see it only after a git push (the pre-push hook calls `agentdiff push`, with a 30 s timeout and failures ignored) and their own git fetch. The permanent meta store updates only when a pull request merges, through CI. Nothing streams, watches or notifies.
search_retrieval: Retrieval is CLI-only, with no index. Every command loads all of meta, the branch ref and the local buffer into memory and dedupes them. Commands: list (filter with --agent, --file substring, -n, --uncommitted); show by UUID or SHA prefix; diff over a commit range; blame; context <file> --json; report (by agent, model or file, with --since, as text, markdown, JSON, JSONL or GitHub annotations; can post a PR comment); verify; policy check (max_ai_percent, require_attribution, require_signed). There is also an MCP server, agentdiff-mcp, but it only writes context (record_context, set_intent) and offers no query tool. blame lays the recorded line numbers straight onto the current file, last write wins, and treats any untraced line as "human". It does not track lines that moved since the commit, so its output drifts. Open issue #25 admits --limit is applied only after a full load.
links_sessions_to_code: Yes, at commit, file and hunk-range level. Each trace ties together the commit SHA, the files and line ranges, agent, model, session_id (the Claude Code session ID), a prompt excerpt of up to 160 characters plus a SHA-256 of the full prompt, the files the agent read, and the stated intent. It does not store or link the transcript. The Agent Trace conversation.url field exists but stays empty. Session-to-code matching is a guess: an event counts if its file path matches and its line guesses overlap the staged hunks, and the most recent agent per file wins.
scale: No benchmarks are published. The code comment claims retry coverage for "~100 concurrent pushes". Open issue #25 says that at 100k+ traces (enterprise scale, more than a year of data) list and stats "will take seconds and consume hundreds of MB", because everything is loaded on every run. Each consolidate rewrites the whole meta JSONL as a new blob, so cost grows with total history, and git's delta compression only partly offsets it. Adoption is small: 47 stars, 329 crate downloads.
privacy_security: Redaction and secret scanning: none. Grepping the source finds no redaction code. The only control is capture_prompts=false, which drops prompt_excerpt and prompt_hash from traces. finalize-ledger.py admits that capture scripts other than Claude's may still write prompts into the local session.jsonl. The README warns that once pushed, prompt excerpts are readable by anyone with repo read access. The Claude prompt includes pasted text, so a secret pasted after a short prompt could land inside the 160-character excerpt. prompt_hash is unsalted, so anyone can test a guessed prompt against it. Encryption: none for traces, and the private key is a plaintext base64 seed with mode 0600. The custom ref namespace is outside refs/heads, so branch protection never blocks it. My inference: it is also unprotected, and anyone with write access can rewrite or delete refs/agentdiff/meta. Signature trust model: keys are self-registered as refs by anyone with write access, with no tie to a forge identity, and key_id is truncated to 64 bits. Signatures cover single records with no chain, so dropping, reordering or omitting records goes undetected, and consolidate rewrites the whole file anyway. A signature proves the record was not altered after signing, not that the hook-reported attribution is true. Two code-reading findings, not run: (1) `keys register` writes only a local ref, and no code path pushes refs/agentdiff/keys/* to the remote, so cross-machine verification needs a manual push. (2) Traces are signed over raw JSON holding the git %cI timestamp, such as "+00:00". push and consolidate re-serialize records through a typed DateTime<Utc>, which serde/chrono likely writes as "...Z". That would break signatures on records read back from refs. This is a hypothesis; I could not execute it because the build was denied. Network and supply chain: agentdiff sends no telemetry, but it shells out to gh for GitHub API calls. It installs via curl | sh, and the generated CI workflows fetch install.sh from the main branch unpinned.
lesson_for_parinn: A CAS on a git ref is not a merge. agentdiff keeps each tier as one mutable JSONL blob and retries a non-force ref update without recomputing the content, so concurrent writers silently lose each other's records. Its per-record signatures with no chain cannot detect the loss, and its custom-ref store also escapes branch protection. If ParleyInn moves its record over git, two rules follow. First, make every append content-addressed and collision-free, for example one object per event, or per writer, segment and sequence, in a tree whose merge is a pure set union. Then any race costs a retry, never data. Second, put integrity in the hash chain itself, not in per-record signatures or in where the data is stored. The chain heads per writer should be verifiable, so a dropped, reordered or overwritten record shows up as a broken chain and is audited (I6). Beyond that: sign the stored bytes exactly and never re-serialize them; treat a self-registered key ref as an untrusted claim; and never rely on a forge-specific API (here GitHub through gh) for transport if Forgejo and offline use matter. That last point also fits I4.
license: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (dual)
confidence: high for the storage layout, data model, merge mechanics and privacy controls, all read directly from source at commit f9ffbd2. medium for the lost-update defect: clear from the code, but not reproduced. low for the timestamp re-serialization breaking signatures: inferred, could not be run.

name: agentgit (monperrus/agentgit, a fork of btucker/agentgit)
status: beta
what_is_stored:
The tool turns Claude Code JSONL transcripts (~/.claude/projects/) and Codex CLI transcripts (~/.codex/sessions/) into git history. It can also pull Claude Code web sessions. It stores two kinds of content.
(a) File states. Every Write/Edit/Delete the agent made is replayed as real file content in a working tree. When the transcript's originalFile is null, the pre-edit content is rebuilt from structuredPatch.
(b) The conversation, as commit messages. Each message holds the full user prompt text, the assistant text, the extended-thinking blocks verbatim under "## Extended Thinking", and the full tool-call input JSON for calls that changed no files. Trailers carry Entry-Id, Prompt-Id (an md5), Tool-Id, Session-Id, Timestamp, File and Operation.
Messages over 100,000 chars go in via `git commit -F` because "transcript entries (full Write payloads, giant tool outputs) regularly exceed" the argv limit (git_builder.py _commit_with_date).
There is also an optional blame index. An orphan branch `agentgit-index` holds `.agentgit/lines/<path>` files with rows of `sha256(line)|session|commit_sha|context`.
An optional `--file-ops-only` mode (added in the fork, 2026-09-13) keeps only the file events, as a linear history.
where_stored:
A separate local git repo at ~/.agentgit/projects/<repo-id>/. The repo-id is the first 12 chars of the code repo's root commit SHA. The repo's objects/info/alternates points at the code repo's .git/objects, so the two share one object store. The code repo itself is never modified.
The design doc says this repo is bare, but the current code calls Repo.init and builds a normal repo with a working tree.
Settings live in git config: agentgit.coderepo, agentgit.enhancer, agentgit.llmModel. Commit signing is turned off (commit.gpgsign=false).
No remote, push or sync code exists.
format_and_model:
Plain git objects, with this data model:
- one branch per session: `session(s)/<agent>/<date-prefixed short name>`, the name either rule-based or written by an LLM, max 50 chars
- each user prompt is a merge commit whose subject is the prompt text
- the agent's entries or turns are child commits between that merge and its first parent, each carrying the file changes as a diff plus the reasoning in the commit message
So `git log --first-parent session/X` shows only prompts and plain `git log` shows every operation.
Commit dates are set from the transcript timestamps (GIT_AUTHOR_DATE/GIT_COMMITTER_DATE). The author is copied from the code repo's git identity.
Incremental runs skip work already done by reading the trailers back (get_processed_operations, _get_processed_entries).
Formats and enhancers are pluggy plugins, so it is extensible. The implementation is Python, about 9.9k lines in src/.
multi_writer_and_merge:
Single user, single machine. Concurrent sessions become separate branches, and the design doc says this means "no conflicts" because sessions are "parallel realities".
There is no lock, no handling for two concurrent agentgit processes writing the same repo, no cross-machine merge, and no conflict resolution.
Duplicates are avoided only by the trailer-based dedup when one local process re-runs over the same transcripts. The `--reprocess` flag rebuilds the repo from scratch.
Nothing covers sharing between agents or machines, or pushing to GitHub/Forgejo.
realtime:
`agentgit --watch` uses the Python watchdog library to watch a local transcript file. On modify/create events, after an mtime/size debounce, it runs an incremental build and commits the new entries (watcher.py).
It is local and near-real-time for one file. Nothing propagates to other machines or agents in real time.
search_retrieval:
All search goes through plain git: `agentgit log/show/diff` passes through to git, with a custom markdown pager. `git diff session/A session/B` compares two approaches. There is also a lazygit TUI wrapper (alazygit) and an interactive `agentgit discover` transcript picker.
`agentgit blame <file>` runs git blame on the code repo. It hashes each line with sha256 and runs `git grep "^<hash>" refs/heads/agentgit-index` to find the session, commit and context.
The design doc also describes blob-level matching via `git log --all --find-object=<blob>`.
There is no full-text index beyond git grep, no semantic search, and no MCP or agent-facing recall API. A Python API exists: agentgit.transcript_to_repo().
links_sessions_to_code:
Yes, and this is the tool's whole purpose. There are two mechanisms.
(1) Shared object store via git alternates. If an agent wrote the same file content that was later committed, both repos hold the same blob SHA, so `--find-object` lines them up.
(2) A per-line index. A line that was rewritten, or survived edits around it, can still be traced: sha256 of the line → session branch, commit and context sentence, on the agentgit-index branch.
`agentgit blame` prints the session branch and the agent's reasoning next to each code line.
The correlation is purely content-based. It is heuristic: common lines such as `}` or `return None` can match more than one session. No trailer or note is written into the code repo's own commits.
privacy_security:
No redaction, secret scanning, encryption or signing in the source. A grep for redact/secret/encrypt/sanitiz finds only branch-name sanitizing, and commit.gpgsign is turned off.
What lands in plaintext git: full prompts, assistant text, extended thinking verbatim, and full tool inputs (Bash commands, file payloads). Any secret that reached the transcript goes into commit messages, and into blobs that share the code repo's object store.
The design doc's privacy claim is only that the separate repo "can be private/local".
The optional `llm` enhancer sends prompt and turn content to an LLM through the `llm`/`llm-claude-cli` packages.
The claude_code_web format reads the Claude Code OAuth access token from ~/.claude credentials or the macOS keychain. It calls https://api.anthropic.com/v1/sessions and /v1/session_ingress/session/<id>, so this path makes network calls with the user's credentials.
Recalled content gets no untrusted-content treatment.
Alternates risk: if the code repo prunes objects that only the agentgit repo still references (for example after a rebase plus gc), the agentgit repo can break. Git's documentation warns about this.
scale:
No scale claims or benchmarks. The README says git grep searches "millions of lines per second", which describes git, not a measured result for agentgit.
Upstream does have a "Batch process session names and commit messages for massive speedup" commit (2026-01-06). The fork's oversized-message fix (2026-09-13) shows that single entries regularly go past 100 KB.
license: MIT (LICENSE file, "Copyright (c) 2025 Ben Tucker"; pyproject license = "MIT")
lesson_for_parinn:
Build code-to-session provenance as a derived, rebuildable index keyed only by content hashes, the way agentgit does, without git alternates. agentgit's sha256-per-line index lives on an orphan agentgit-index branch and is looked up with git grep. It maps a code line back to the session entry that wrote it, survives later edits to surrounding lines, and never touches the code repo.
ParleyInn could project the same index from its append-only record, which keeps I10, and serve it through pull-only, enveloped recall (I2).
ParleyInn should avoid agentgit's other choices:
- coupling stores through objects/info/alternates (absolute local paths that break under gc, in ephemeral sandboxes and across machines)
- writing unredacted thinking and tool payloads into git
- any network path, such as its keychain-token fetch from api.anthropic.com
It should also treat single-line matches as low-confidence: common lines match many sessions.
