- Auto Approval (experimental) sends captured terminal output to `claude -p --model haiku`, or to a custom command. That content leaves the machine through Claude Code's API. The prompt wraps the output in <terminal-output> tags and labels it untrusted. A deterministic regex blocklist runs before the LLM 'as defense-in-depth that cannot be bypassed by prompt injection', and any error or timeout falls back to manual approval.
- Devcontainer mode keeps the manager on the host while the agents run in sandboxes.
- CCManager injects --teammate-mode in-process so Claude agent teams do not conflict with its PTY handling.
lesson_for_parinn:
Don't carry context across worktrees by copying the record. CCManager's 'Session Data Copying' is a cp -r of ~/.claude/projects/<path>. It produces two directories holding the same sessionIds, with cwd and gitBranch fields that are wrong in the copy. It records no lineage, and it duplicates every secret in the transcript. Its 'restore' only re-runs the launch command.

ParleyInn should model a fork as a new append-only chain whose genesis event names the parent chain id and the parent's head hash. The parent stays untouched and verifiable, the lineage can be checked, and per-worktree identity stays unique. What the new worktree needs at start should arrive as pinned TrustedText through the restore block, not as duplicated raw history (I2, I10).

Two secondary takeaways:
- Atomic temp-file-plus-rename with PID ownership is crash-safe but not multi-writer-safe. CCManager's shared sessions.json still has a lost-update window, so ParleyInn needs per-writer append-only segments or a real lock.
- Its project-level config can define shell hooks with no trust gate. That is exactly the 'repo-supplied content becomes execution' channel ParleyInn's invariants rule out.
confidence: high. The facts come from reading the cloned source at commit ee0af83 (2026-09-27) plus the README and docs. The items marked as inference are my readings of the code: the lost-update race, PID reuse, stale cwd in copies, and repo-config hooks with no trust gate. The JSONL field names come from inspecting local Claude Code transcripts, not from CCManager documentation. Star count is from a 2026-10-02 page fetch.

name: Claude Agent SDK sessions (continue / resume / fork, SessionStore mirror)
status: shipped
what_is_stored: The whole conversation: the prompt, every tool call, every tool result and every response. The docs say "Sessions persist the conversation, not the filesystem". File changes are covered by a separate file-checkpointing feature (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/sessions). Each JSONL line is "a JSON object for a message, tool use, or metadata entry". The entry format is "internal to Claude Code and changes between versions" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions). Subagent transcripts and sidecar files are stored under subpaths such as `subagents/agent-<id>`. A per-session summary sidecar holds opaque, SDK-owned `data` for listings (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage). Sessions also carry a title or rename, tags and created_at. Python added tag_session and rename_session in 0.1.49, and the tag and created_at fields with get_session_info in 0.1.50 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/main/CHANGELOG.md). After auto-compaction the raw record keeps the turns from before compaction. getSessionMessages returns only the chain after compaction: the docs give an example of 503 raw entries against 18 messages. `store.load(key)` returns the full raw history (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage).
where_stored: Local disk is the default and always comes first. Each session is one JSONL file at `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<session-id>.jsonl`, or under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/`. The encoding replaces every non-alphanumeric character with `-`. Names over 200 characters are truncated and a hash is appended (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/sessions, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions). `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` can pin the directory name (CLI v2.1.234+, TS SDK v0.3.234+, Python SDK v0.2.140+). A pluggable `SessionStore` adapter mirrors each batch to a backend you run: an object store, a key-value store or a database. The reference adapters cover S3, Redis and Postgres. They are copy-in examples, not published packages (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage). The architecture is dual-write: the subprocess writes locally, then the SDK forwards the same batch to `append()`. When a run resumes from the store, the SDK materialises the transcript in a temporary CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and deletes it at the end of the run. On that path the store holds the only durable copy (same source). `persistSession: false` (TS) keeps a session in memory only, and `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY` suppresses writes. Neither git nor any git ref is involved.
format_and_model:
Append-only JSONL, one entry per line. Entries are `{type: string, ...}` objects with a `uuid`, linked into a message chain. The parent-link field name is not documented: the docs speak only of a "linked message chain" and of remapping message UUIDs (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage). A session is addressed by a UUID session ID. The store key is `SessionKey {projectKey, sessionId, subpath?}`, where projectKey is a filesystem-safe encoding of the cwd. The SessionStore interface has two required methods:
- `append(key, entries[])`
- `load(key) -> entries[] | null`

It has four optional methods: `listSessions`, `listSessionSummaries`, `delete` and `listSubkeys`. `delete` on the main key must cascade to subkeys and the summary. Leaving `delete` out makes deletion a no-op, which the docs say "suits append-only backends". `load` must return entries deep-equal to what was appended and in the same order; byte-equality is not required (same source). Fork rewrites history rather than sharing it: `forkSession` "reads the source entries, rewrites every sessionId field and remaps message UUIDs, then appends the transformed entries under a new key". The docs call it "not a byte copy", so there is no content addressing or structural sharing. Continue resumes the newest session for the cwd. Resume takes an explicit ID. Python 0.2.137 added `resume_session_at` to fork at an earlier entry (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/main/CHANGELOG.md). The reference adapters store data as follows (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/main/examples/session_stores/s3_session_store.py, .../postgres_session_store.py):
- **S3:** one object per append, `part-{epochMs13}-{rand6}.jsonl`. Load lists, sorts and concatenates the parts.
- **Redis:** RPUSH and LRANGE lists plus a zset index.
- **Postgres:** one jsonb row per entry, ordered by a bigserial `seq`.
multi_writer_and_merge:
There is no merge model. A session has one linear history. To branch you fork, which copies the history into a new session with a new ID; forks are never reconciled. The CLI docs warn: "If you resume the same session in two terminals without forking, messages from both interleave into one transcript" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions). The store contract offers no concurrency control:
- Concurrent `append` calls can race on the summary sidecar. Adapters must serialise read-fold-write "with a transaction, a compare-and-swap, or a per-session lock" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage).
- A failed append is retried up to three times, so entries can be delivered twice. The docs tell adapters to "deduplicate by entry.uuid" (same source).

The reference adapters do not follow that advice. My reading of the code found no uuid dedup in the S3 or Postgres adapters. The S3 adapter orders parts by wall-clock milliseconds, which is monotonic within one instance only, and uses a random suffix "to disambiguate concurrent instances". Two hosts with skewed clocks could therefore interleave out of order. It also silently skips JSONL lines it cannot parse (`contextlib.suppress(json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError)`) (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/main/examples/session_stores/s3_session_store.py). Resume lookup by ID across projects succeeds only when exactly one other project holds the ID. A hand-copied duplicate makes the lookup report not-found (CLI v2.1.223+) (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions).
realtime: Real-time sharing is only partial and works by mirroring, not by subscription. By default the SDK flushes batches to `append()` "after each batch of transcript entries is written locally" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage). Python 0.1.73 added `session_store_flush="eager"`, which delivers frames to `append()` in near-real-time instead of at the end-of-turn flush. The changelog says it enables "live-tailing UIs, cross-process resume, and crash-durability" (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/main/CHANGELOG.md). The interface has no push, watch or subscribe method; readers must poll `load`/`listSessions`. I could not verify whether TypeScript has an equivalent eager-flush option. Store writes are best-effort. On final failure the SDK logs the error, emits a `{type:"system", subtype:"mirror_error"}` message, drops the batch and carries on. On a run resumed from the store, the dropped batch is then lost for good (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage).
search_retrieval:
There is no full-text or semantic search in the SDK. Retrieval goes by ID or listing:
- `listSessions()` (Python 0.1.52 added offset pagination), `getSessionInfo()` and `getSessionMessages()` (the chain after compaction)
- `listSubagents()` and `getSubagentMessages()`
- `renameSession()` and `tagSession()` for organising sessions
- `store.load()` for the raw full history

Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/sessions, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/main/CHANGELOG.md. Listing reads a summary sidecar in O(1) per session through the optional `listSessionSummaries`, kept up to date with `foldSessionSummary` inside `append`. Without it, listing falls back to one `load` per session (Python 0.1.65). In the CLI, the session picker searches by name, title or first prompt and filters by worktree or branch (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions). Any deeper search is up to whoever runs the store backend.
links_sessions_to_code:
The link to code is weak and indirect:
- A session is keyed by working directory (projectKey or encoded cwd), not by commit or repository identity. Resume from the store must use a matching cwd (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage).
- The CLI picker shows the git branch, can filter by branch and can widen to all worktrees of a repository. `claude --from-pr <number>` and pasting a PR or MR URL find "the session that created it". The docs do not say how that link is stored (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions).
- Sessions and forks record the conversation only. File changes are real and shared across forks unless file checkpointing is on, and file checkpointing is incompatible with a SessionStore: the SDK throws at startup (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage).
- Commit SHAs are not recorded on entries, as far as the public docs show.
scale:
Anthropic publishes no throughput or size figures. The documented scale features are:
- O(1) listing through summary sidecars (Python 0.1.65)
- bounded parallel loads: the S3 adapter reads 16 parts at a time
- local retention of 30 days by default through `cleanupPeriodDays`

The SDK "never deletes from your store on its own", so retention in the store is the adapter's job (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage). The S3 adapter writes one object per append, so long sessions with eager flushing produce many small objects. This is my inference from the code (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/main/examples/session_stores/s3_session_store.py).
privacy_security: Local transcripts are plaintext. The docs say clients "store session transcripts locally in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects/ for 30 days by default" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage). The SDK applies no encryption, redaction or secret scanning to transcripts or store mirrors. Encryption, access control and retention are left to the backend; the docs pitch the store for compliance "with your own retention rules, encryption, and access controls" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage). Adapters take a client you configure yourself, so you control credentials and TLS. Redaction of "known API key and token patterns" happens only on feedback and survey uploads, not on stored transcripts (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage). Resuming from the store copies credentials, `.claude.json` and, in TypeScript, a filtered user `settings.json` into a temporary config directory (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage). That temporary directory therefore briefly holds secrets next to the restored transcript. Recalled content has no integrity protection: there is no hash chain or signature. `load` returns whatever the store holds, and that goes straight back into the model's context on resume. A tampered store row therefore becomes an injection channel (my inference from the interface; no mitigation is documented). The S3 adapter's silent skipping of malformed lines means corruption is hidden rather than surfaced.
lesson_for_parinn:
Copy the interface shape but tighten it where Anthropic's is loose. A two-method append/load sink keyed by (project, session, subpath), with a conformance suite any backend must pass, is the right way to keep ParleyInn's networkless core: transport lives in adapters outside the core. Anthropic's contract leaves gaps ParleyInn must close:
- **Idempotency:** dedup by uuid is only advised, and the reference adapters skip it.
- **Ordering:** order across writers rests on wall clocks.
- **Failures:** failed mirror batches are dropped with only an in-stream message, and the S3 adapter silently skips malformed lines.
- **Integrity:** loaded entries go straight back into the model's context unchecked.

ParleyInn's closures:
- Make idempotency and hash-chain verification part of the conformance contract.
- Order by chain position, not timestamps.
- Audit and count every dropped or skipped entry (I6).
- Treat `load` output as untrusted data, enveloped and never auto-injected (I2).

Two more points. Anthropic's fork rewrites IDs instead of sharing a prefix by hash, so content addressing would let ParleyInn fork and dedup cheaply. And because the JSONL format is officially internal and unstable, ParleyInn should ingest through hooks or SDK messages behind a versioned parser, not depend on the file layout.
license: The docs pages do not state a license. I did not check the SDK repositories' LICENSE files in this session (GitHub API access was blocked), so this is unverified here.

name: Claude Agent SDK SessionStore
status: shipped
what_is_stored: Agent transcript entries (conversation history, tool calls, results, metadata). Each entry is an opaque JSON-safe object with a uuid field for deduplication. SessionSummaryEntry holds metadata (sessionId, mtime, opaque data dict). Entries are stored in order as they are appended.
where_stored: Depends on adapter implementation. Three reference implementations provided: S3 (one part file per append, concatenated on load), Redis (lists with per-session index), Postgres (one JSONB row per entry with insertion order). Adapters take pre-configured clients, so storage location and credentials controlled by application.
format_and_model: JSON-safe objects (entries are uninterpreted). Local mirror is JSONL (one entry per line). SessionKey model: {projectKey, sessionId, subpath?}. projectKey encodes working directory filesystem-safely. subpath used for subagent transcripts (e.g., 'subagents/agent-<id>'). SessionStoreEntry is opaque {type: string, ...}. SessionSummaryEntry: {sessionId, mtime, data: Record<string, unknown>}. mtime is storage write time; data is SDK-owned and must be persisted verbatim.
multi_writer_and_merge: No automatic merge. Concurrent append() calls for same session require external serialization (transaction, compare-and-swap, or per-session lock). Mirror writes are best-effort: 3 attempts max with short backoff. No automatic retry on timeout. Deduplication by entry.uuid required in adapter. Session summary fold (foldSessionSummary/fold_session_summary) is pure function; concurrency handled by caller via locks/transactions when updating sidecar.
realtime: Not real-time. Entries written in batches to local filesystem first, then forwarded to store's append() (dual-write architecture). Store is mirror, not primary on fresh sessions. Resume materializes full transcript from store into temp config directory before subprocess runs. No subscription or notification mechanism for updates across hosts.
search_retrieval: No full-text search built-in. listSessionSummaries(projectKey) returns metadata for all sessions. load(key) returns full entry list. getSessionMessages(sessionStore) returns linked message chain after auto-compaction (earlier turns replaced by summary). Resume lookup by projectKey (all sessions) then sessionId. No cross-project query capability.
links_sessions_to_code: Yes, via projectKey which encodes working directory. Encoded name derived by replacing non-alphanumeric characters with dashes; names >200 chars truncated with hash appended. In TypeScript v0.3.234+, can set CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME for stable naming. Subpath distinguishes main transcript from subagent transcripts. Supports multi-host resume from same working directory.
privacy_security: No encryption built into SessionStore interface. Adapter responsible for encryption, credentials, TLS. Each adapter takes pre-configured client (S3Client, Redis, pg connection, etc.), so application controls all auth/encryption. Retention policy is adapter responsibility (backend expiry/lifecycle or scheduled cleanup). Mirror writes fail gracefully (logged, system message emitted, batch dropped). Adapter must handle secrets in transcripts; no redaction at SDK level. Local transcripts under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR swept per cleanupPeriodDays. Resumed runs delete local copy, so store is sole durable copy.
lesson_for_parinn: SessionStore demonstrates append-only external storage pattern with best-effort mirroring. Key insights: (1) Keep store interface simple (two required methods append/load plus optional list/delete/listSubkeys). (2) Don't encrypt at SDK level; let adapters choose transport security. (3) Use content-addressed deduplication (entry.uuid) rather than retry logic. (4) Dual-write ensures local resilience; store outage doesn't block agent. (5) Ordering via insertion order + uuid preserves causality without clock. (6) Session-level summary sidecar pattern separates append-only entries from mutable metadata. (7) Require external synchronization for concurrent writers (no automatic merging). (8) Subpath prefix for subagent transcripts simplifies multi-session lookup. (9) projectKey as stable working-directory hash enables cross-host resume without central session registry.

name: Claude API memory tool (memory_20250818)
category: first-party memory primitive (Anthropic-defined client tool on the Messages API)
status: shipped. It launched as a public beta on 2025-09-29 (release notes; https://claude.com/blog/context-management). The release notes for 2026-02-17 say the memory tool "no longer require[s] a beta header" (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview). The Tool reference lists type `memory_20250818`, execution "Client", beta header "None" (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-reference). memory_20250818 is still the only version listed as of Oct 2026. The SDK helper classes still sit in the SDKs' beta namespaces (memory-tool doc). The docs say it works on "all Claude 4 and later models". At launch it was announced for the Claude Developer Platform, Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI (blog). There is a separate, newer, server-side product: Managed Agents "memory stores". They entered public beta 2026-04-23 and use beta header agent-memory-2026-07-22 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory). They are not the same feature, but they show where Anthropic took the design next.
what_is_stored: Free-form text files (plus .jpg/.jpeg/.png images, which `view` can display) that Claude itself decides to write under a virtual `/memories` directory. Typical content is progress logs, learned patterns, preferences, checklists and decisions. It is not a transcript and not session history: Anthropic's cookbook says to "Store task-relevant patterns, not conversation history" (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cookbooks/blob/main/tool_use/memory_cookbook.ipynb). Files are mutable in place: create (which per the tool description "creates or overwrites"), str_replace, insert, delete (recursive for directories) and rename. No history, versions, authorship or timestamps are part of the protocol (memory-tool doc).
where_stored: Wherever the application's handler puts it. "The memory tool operates client-side: Claude requests file operations, and your application executes them." "The /memories path is a prefix that your handler maps onto real storage, such as a per-user directory or keys in a database. Memory lives entirely in your application." (memory-tool doc). Anthropic stores nothing beyond normal API handling. The retention page lists it as ZDR-eligible and HIPAA-eligible: "Client-side memory storage where you control data retention." (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention). The reference backend is BetaLocalFilesystemMemoryTool (Python, TypeScript), which writes to local files under `<base_path>/memories` (default ./memory/memories). Python and C# subclass BetaAbstractMemoryTool, TypeScript uses betaMemoryTool, and Java implements BetaMemoryToolHandler. The docs say the Go and Ruby SDKs have no memory helper (memory-tool doc).
format_and_model:
The tool definition is just `{"type":"memory_20250818","name":"memory"}`, with no schema to supply. Claude emits tool_use blocks with `command` set to one of these:
- view (path, optional view_range [start,end|-1])
- create (path, file_text)
- str_replace (path, old_str, optional new_str; must match exactly once)
- insert (path, insert_line, insert_text)
- delete (path)
- rename (old_path, new_path)

The handler returns plain text in a tool_result, or `is_error: true`.

Directory view: a listing up to 2 levels deep with human-readable sizes, tab-separated, excluding dotfiles and node_modules.

File view: a 6-wide, right-aligned, 1-indexed line number, then a tab, then the content. There is a 999,999-line cap, and the tool description says text views of files longer than 16,000 characters are truncated.

Rename must not overwrite. The memory root cannot be deleted or renamed. The data model is a plain hierarchical filesystem of UTF-8 text with last-write-wins semantics. The reference SDK writes files atomically (temp file, fsync, os.replace) with modes 0600/0700 (https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/main/src/anthropic/lib/tools/_beta_builtin_memory_tool.py). The API also auto-injects a system prompt: "IMPORTANT: ALWAYS VIEW YOUR MEMORY DIRECTORY BEFORE DOING ANYTHING ELSE ... ASSUME INTERRUPTION" (memory-tool doc).
multi_writer_and_merge: The protocol has no concurrency or merge story. There are no ETags, preconditions, locks or versions, and every command is a blind read-modify-write by one model turn (memory-tool doc). In the Python reference backend, str_replace and insert read the file, change it in memory and write the whole file back atomically, with no lock. Two agents sharing a store therefore get torn-free files but lose updates (last writer wins). The SDK error text acknowledges concurrent deletes and renames ("may have been deleted or renamed concurrently") (Python SDK source). The TypeScript backend comments that "POSIX rename() silently overwrites existing files without error, so we can't catch this atomically. Best-effort check" (https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/blob/main/src/tools/memory/node.ts). Sharing across agents or machines is left entirely to the handler's storage. Contrast: Anthropic's later server-side Managed Agents memory stores added an immutable version on every write (memver_...), optimistic concurrency via a `content_sha256` precondition, and per-session read_only/read_write access. Self-hosted sandboxes sync a local copy at most every 15 s by default, so cross-session visibility is eventual (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory).
realtime: No. Nothing is pushed or subscribed to. Claude sees memory only when it issues a `view`, which the auto-injected protocol makes it do at the start of each task, and when it reads files later (memory-tool doc). Whether another agent's write is visible depends on the handler's backing store. Managed Agents memory stores (a different product) keep live mounts in sync across sessions, and self-hosted copies reconcile on a sync interval (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory).
search_retrieval: There is no search command. Retrieval is navigational and model-driven: list the directory (2 levels), open files, and page with view_range. The docs call this "just-in-time context retrieval" (memory-tool doc). There is no index, full-text search, embeddings or ranking. Organizing memory falls to Claude, guided by its tool description, plus optional prompts. Context editing (beta header context-management-2025-06-27) warns Claude near the clearing threshold so it can save tool results to memory before they are cleared (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing). Anthropic also recommends pairing memory with server-side compaction (memory-tool doc).
links_sessions_to_code: Not built in. Memory files carry no session IDs, commit SHAs, file paths or prompt provenance unless Claude chooses to write them as text. The docs' "Multisession software development pattern" asks for a deliberate progress log, a feature checklist and a reference to an init script, updated at the end of each session (memory-tool doc). It points to the long-running harness case study, which uses plain repo files (claude-progress.txt, feature_list.json chosen because JSON is less likely to be overwritten inappropriately) and git commits for recovery, not the memory tool (https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents).
scale: There are no storage-scale claims, because size, count and retention are whatever the handler implements. The protocol and reference limits are a 999,999-line file cap, a 16,000-character text-view truncation (per the tool description) and 2-level directory listings (memory-tool doc). The docs tell implementers to cap file sizes and view output, and to expire files not accessed in a long time. On quality, the launch post claims memory plus context editing improved an internal agentic-search evaluation by 39% versus 29% for context editing alone. It also says context editing cut token use by 84% in a 100-turn web-search evaluation (https://claude.com/blog/context-management). These are Anthropic's own internal figures and are not independently verified. For contrast, Managed Agents memory stores are capped at 100 kB per memory, 10,000 memories per store and 8 stores per session (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory).
privacy_security:
All safeguards are the implementer's job ("Your application executes every file operation Claude requests, so these safeguards are your responsibility").

Path traversal: the docs warn that `/memories/../../secrets.env` can escape the store and require validating every path. That means a /memories prefix, canonical resolution that must stay within the root, rejecting ../ and ..\ and URL-encoded %2e%2e%2f, and using pathlib resolve()/relative_to() (memory-tool doc). The Python and TypeScript reference backends add a check that symlinks do not escape the root, 0600/0700 permissions (to survive Docker's permissive umask), exclusive temp-file creation and atomic replace (Python and TS SDK sources).

Secrets: "Claude usually refuses to write sensitive information to memory files. For stronger guarantees, add validation that strips sensitive data before your handler writes the file." There is no built-in redaction or encryption, though encrypted files are named as a possible custom backend (memory-tool doc; Python SDK docstring).

Prompt injection: Anthropic's cookbook flags memory poisoning as a "Critical Risk: Memory files are read back into Claude's context, making them a potential vector for prompt injection." The suggested mitigations are sanitization, per-user/per-project isolation, auditing, and prompting Claude to ignore instructions found in memory (cookbook). The Managed Agents docs give the same warning more sharply: with read_write access, a prompt injection "could write malicious content into the store. Later sessions then read that content as trusted memory." (managed-agents/memory).

Retention: ZDR-eligible and HIPAA-eligible because storage is client-side (api-and-data-retention).
license: The API feature is proprietary (Anthropic commercial terms). The SDK helpers, including BetaLocalFilesystemMemoryTool, ship in MIT-licensed SDKs (https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/main/LICENSE, https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/blob/main/LICENSE).
lesson_for_parinn:
memory_20250818 shows how far the cheap design goes and where it breaks. It is a mutable, model-written, last-writer-wins file tree. It has no history, no concurrency control and no provenance. An auto-injected "ALWAYS VIEW YOUR MEMORY DIRECTORY" prompt makes its contents de facto automatically re-read into context, the exact poisoning channel Anthropic's own cookbook calls critical.

Anthropic's own follow-up (Managed Agents memory stores) had to add immutable per-write versions, content_sha256 compare-and-swap preconditions, read_only mounts and redaction.

Concrete lesson: if ParleyInn ever offers a memory_20250818-compatible handler (useful because the Go SDK ships none), it should not keep a separate mutable store. Instead:
- Every create, str_replace, insert, delete and rename becomes an appended, hash-chained event in ParleyInn's record, carrying the session, agent and expected prior-content hash. A stale hash is rejected and audited, which serves I6.
- The /memories tree becomes a derived projection rebuilt from the record (I10).
- Every `view` result goes back wrapped in the untrusted-content envelope. Only explicitly pinned TrustedText ever enters a restore block, so memory never becomes an automatic injection path (I2).
- Path validation follows the SDK's resolve-plus-symlink-escape-check model.

name: Claude Code agent teams
category: Multi-agent team (one lead plus teammates) that coordinates through local file mailboxes and a shared task list. It is a feature of the proprietary Claude Code CLI, not a standalone project.
status: beta. Shipped as an experimental research preview in Claude Code v2.1.32 alongside Opus 4.6 on 2026-02-05 (https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-4-6, https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). It is still off by default behind CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 as of the current docs and changelog head, v2.1.287 (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams). There are two superseded designs. First, user-named teams created with the TeamCreate/TeamDelete tools were removed in v2.1.178; every session now has exactly one implicit team (CHANGELOG 2.1.178). Second, on newer models the shared task list is opt-in: the Task tools ship by default only on Claude 3.x, Opus 4–4.7, Sonnet 4–4.6 and Haiku 4.5. Without them, teammates coordinate by messages only (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#task-tool-availability).
what_is_stored:
Team coordination state only. The team does not keep its own conversation history.
(1) Team config. A members array holds each member's name, agent ID and agent type: the lead is always 'team-lead'. It also holds runtime state such as session IDs and tmux pane IDs (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#architecture). A user report says each member's spawn prompt is stored there once and never updated (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/82687).
(2) One mailbox per agent. It carries plain-text messages plus structured protocol messages: plan approval requests and responses, shutdown requests and responses, and idle notifications. Idle notifications carry the teammate's final answer or its API error (docs, Architecture and Context-and-communication sections). Permission requests also go through it (CHANGELOG 2.1.257).
(3) Shared task list. Tasks are pending, in progress or completed, and can depend on other tasks (docs, Assign-and-claim section).
Conversation history lives elsewhere: each agent's full transcript is in Claude Code's ordinary per-session JSONL under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl, and subagent transcripts are under <session>/subagents/ (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory). The docs do not say where in-process teammate transcripts land. Unverified.
where_stored:
Local files under the user's home directory, outside any repository. None of it is in git.
- Mailbox: ~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/inboxes/{agent-name}.json
- Team config: ~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/config.json
- Task list: ~/.claude/tasks/{team-name}/
- team-name is generated from the session: 'session-' plus the first 8 characters of the session ID (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#architecture).

Lifetimes differ:
- The teams directory is deleted when the session ends.
- The tasks directory persists locally and 'is never uploaded', so a resumed session keeps its tasks.
- Old task lists are deleted by the cleanupPeriodDays sweep: default 30 days, minimum 1 (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically). The sweep has covered tasks/ since v2.1.117 (CHANGELOG 2.1.117).

A project-level file such as .claude/teams/teams.json is not recognised as config (docs). There is no cross-machine or cloud copy of team state.
format_and_model:
Everything is JSON on disk. The inbox entry schema is not documented, so the shape below comes from user reports and one local observation.

Mailbox:
- One JSON array per recipient, rewritten whole on each write.
- Entries look like {from, text, summary, timestamp, color, read}.
- Protocol messages share the same array, for example {"type":"idle_notification","from":...,"idleReason":"available"} and shutdown_approved with requestId, paneId and backendType (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/53896, /60199, /82687).
- The per-entry 'read' flag is the delivery state; there is no separate cursor (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/63684).
- Claude Code checks every entry on read and deletes malformed ones from the file. Before v2.1.207 one bad entry blocked the whole mailbox (docs).
- Messages reach the model as <teammate-message teammate_id=...> blocks (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/50779).

Task list:
- One JSON file per task, plus an empty .lock file in the list directory.
- Observed locally on Claude Code 2.1.287 in this container, for a non-team session task list (no URL available): fields are id, subject, description, activeForm, status, blocks and blockedBy.
- I could not verify whether team tasks add an owner or assignee field.
- Hooks expose task_id, task_subject and task_description (TaskCreated, TaskCompleted) and team_name, teammate_name and teammate_type (TeammateIdle) (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks).

Overall this is mutable current state — inbox queues and task status — not an event log. There is no hashing or history.
multi_writer_and_merge:
Every agent runs on one machine against one shared home directory, so the writers are the lead plus the in-process or tmux/iTerm2-pane teammates.

Tasks:
- The docs say claiming uses file locking to prevent races when two teammates claim the same task. Self-claim picks the next unassigned, unblocked task, and completing a task automatically unblocks the tasks that depend on it (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#assign-and-claim-tasks).

Mailboxes:
- A message counts as sent only once the write to the recipient's file succeeds. Otherwise the sender gets 'Failed to write to <name>'s inbox — nothing was sent' (docs and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors). Before v2.1.224, SendMessage could report success after a failed write (CHANGELOG 2.1.224).
- A 2026-04 report showed concurrent SendMessage calls losing messages through read-modify-write of the array. It was closed as 'not planned' (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/53896).
- A later changelog entry mentions the leader's mailbox write being 'briefly locked', which suggests a lock now exists (CHANGELOG 2.1.257). That is my inference, not documented.
- External tools that write to inboxes have no documented contract (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/88332).

Team config is overwritten by the runtime, so hand edits are lost (docs).

There are no merge semantics at all: no CRDT, no conflict resolution, and no sharing across sessions ('One team per session… can't share a team across sessions'). Teammates also share one working tree, and the docs warn that two teammates editing the same file overwrite each other (docs, Limitations and Best practices sections).
realtime:
Same machine only, close to real time, with known delays.
- Delivery is automatic and the lead does not need to poll (docs).
- Underneath, in-process teammates poll their mailbox file every 500 ms. User debug logs show '[TeammateMailbox] readUnreadMessages' and a 30 s idle-eviction timer (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/89515).
- Messages are injected only at turn boundaries. Users measured delays of 5–62 minutes while the receiver was busy, and up to 14.5 h when the lead sat idle (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/76500, /82687, /50779).
- Users also report a /clear queue leak and re-delivery of pre-compaction messages 30–60 minutes later (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/76500, /97798).
- There is no network transport for teams. The separate cross-session messaging feature is plain text only, and team protocol messages stay inside the team. It uses a per-session Unix socket or named pipe locally, and Anthropic servers via Remote Control for other machines or the cloud (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging).
search_retrieval:
Minimal.
- Agents read tasks with TaskList and TaskGet, and change them with TaskCreate and TaskUpdate (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference).
- Teammates find each other by reading config.json (docs). ListAgents lists teammates, which needs v2.1.239 or later (tools-reference).
- Humans view a teammate's transcript through the agent panel. Ctrl+T toggles the task list and shows up to five tasks (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#task-list).
- The inbox is effectively a drain queue: entries are flagged read once delivered. There is no search, index or query over messages or past teams, and team config is deleted at session end. Recovering lost content meant grepping the teammate's JSONL transcript (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/82687, /76500).
links_sessions_to_code:
No.
- Team state records session IDs and pane IDs, but no commits, branches or diffs.
- Teammates share the lead's working directory. A spawn that passes isolation (for example a worktree) launches an ordinary subagent, not a teammate (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#how-claude-starts-agent-teams).
- The only code link in Claude Code generally is per-session file-history snapshots used for checkpoints, which is not team-specific (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory).
- For parallel work on code, the docs point to manual git worktrees instead (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#next-steps).
scale:
There is no hard limit on teammates. The docs recommend 3–5 teammates and 5–6 tasks per teammate. Token cost grows roughly linearly with teammates, about 7x a standard session when teammates run in plan mode (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#choose-an-appropriate-team-size, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs). Other limits:
- One team per session.
- No nested teams.
- The lead is fixed for the session's lifetime.
- /resume and /rewind do not restore in-process teammates.
- Interactive sessions only: no -p or Agent SDK (docs).

User-reported limits:
- A lead inbox reused across sessions stopped surfacing messages at about 1 MB / 1,065 entries (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/63684).
- Idle teammates were never evicted, with polling running for about 20 h (/89515).
- A lead lost awareness of its team after compaction (/23620).
- One session ran 30+ teammates, and another 50–90 sub-agents in a day (/60199).
privacy_security:
Storage:
- All files under ~/.claude are plaintext and not encrypted at rest; OS file permissions are the only protection. Secrets that pass through tools end up in transcripts (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#plaintext-storage).
- The task directory is 'never uploaded' (docs). No redaction is documented for mailbox, task or config files.

Trust model (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams#messages-between-agents):
- A SendMessage from a peer is labelled as coming from another Claude session, not the user. It cannot approve a permission prompt or supply consent.
- A teammate that was denied an action cannot relay it to another teammate to get around the check.
- In auto mode a classifier treats approval claims relayed from another agent as untrusted, and reviews every message before delivery. A message it blocks never arrives.
- Cross-session messages additionally cannot change config, and slash commands in them arrive as plain text without running (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#how-a-session-treats-an-incoming-message).

Gaps:
- Teammates inherit the lead's permission mode, including --dangerously-skip-permissions but not dontAsk, and their permission prompts appear in the lead's session.
- Plan approvals are auto-granted by the lead without the user reviewing them; the docs call this the designed exception.
- When a teammate is brought back, an agent definition from an untrusted project folder is not re-applied (docs).

Hardening noted in the changelog: mailbox entries are validated, and malformed ones are dropped and reported (CHANGELOG 2.1.207).
license: Proprietary: '© Anthropic PBC. All rights reserved. Use is subject to Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service' (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/LICENSE.md). There is no published source; the user analyses cited above came from reading strings in the shipped bundle.
lesson_for_parinn:
Do not copy the mailbox's mutable-state design; do adopt its trust label.
- The mailbox is a mutable JSON array per recipient, with a 'read' flag serving as the delivery state.
- Most of the reported failures trace back to that design: lost messages under concurrent writes, re-delivery after compaction, leaks across /clear, and silent stalls at about 1,000 entries.
- ParleyInn should model coordination as append-only, immutable, hash-chained events with monotonic IDs. Each reader keeps a separate cursor, so redelivery is idempotent and deduplicated by ID, and growth or loss is detectable. That is what I6 (no silent failures) and I10 (rebuildable) already demand.
- Claude Code deletes ~/.claude/teams at session end and treats inboxes as drain queues. ParleyInn should therefore capture team traffic into its own record if it wants this history: mailbox entries, plus task-state changes through the local TaskCreated, TaskCompleted and TeammateIdle hooks, which need no network (I4).
- Every such record should carry the same provenance Anthropic applies — 'from another agent, not the user; cannot grant consent' — so recalled peer content stays enveloped as untrusted (I2).

name: Claude Code auto memory + CLAUDE.md (with subagent memory and the cloud Projects memory variant)
status: shipped. CLAUDE.md has been in Claude Code for a long time: changelog 0.2.54 already had '#' quick-add to Memory, and .claude/rules arrived in 2.0.64. Auto memory shipped in v2.1.32 on 2026-02-05 ("Claude now automatically records and recalls memories as it works"). v2.1.59 (2026-02-25) added auto-save managed through /memory. Worktree sharing came in v2.1.63 (2026-02-28). It is still under active development: v2.1.284 (2026-09-28) sanitizes memory, v2.1.285 hardens the toggle, and the latest release is 2.1.287 (2026-10-01). Sources: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md and npm release times at https://registry.npmjs.org/@anthropic-ai/claude-code. The cloud "Projects" memory variant is public beta on Pro/Max only (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects).
what_is_stored:
There are two separate systems (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory).

(1) CLAUDE.md, written by humans: instructions and rules such as build commands, conventions, layout and "always do X". Scopes are managed policy, user, project and local. AGENTS.md can stand in for or sit alongside it (needs v2.1.277+). .claude/rules/*.md hold topic rules, which can be limited to file paths.

(2) Auto memory, written by Claude: notes it judges useful in future sessions, in four kinds recorded as a frontmatter `type`:
- user: role, expertise, preferences
- feedback: corrections and confirmed approaches
- project: ongoing work, deadlines and decisions "that Claude can't derive from the code or git history"
- reference: pointers to outside systems such as issue trackers and dashboards

Claude deliberately skips anything derivable from the codebase (architecture, file paths, debugging fixes) and anything CLAUDE.md already says. It does not save something every session (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory).

Neither system stores the session itself. Full transcripts are separate files, `projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl` holding every message, tool call and tool result, and they are swept after cleanupPeriodDays, default 30 (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory).

Related variants:
- Subagent memory: a `memory:` frontmatter field set to user, project or local, each with its own MEMORY.md (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents).
- Cloud Projects memory: requirements, decisions and pitfalls shared across parallel cloud threads (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects).
where_stored:
Auto memory lives in local files under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`. The <project> name "is derived from the git repository, so all worktrees and subdirectories within the same repo share one auto memory directory". Outside git, the project root is used. The directory is "machine-local... not shared across machines or cloud environments" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory). The directory name encodes the path, for example `~/.claude/projects/-home-user-work-my-repo` holding "project transcripts (.jsonl) and memory/" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory). My inference is that separate clones of one repo at different paths get separate directories; the docs do not say.

Ways to move it:
- `autoMemoryDirectory` (absolute or ~/ path), readable from any settings scope (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory)
- `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` together with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars)

CLAUDE.md lives in working-tree files:
- `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md`, committed to git
- `./CLAUDE.local.md`, gitignored
- `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `~/.claude/rules/` for the user
- managed policy files at `/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md` (Linux), `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md` (macOS), `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md` (Windows), or a `claudeMd` key in managed-settings.json

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.

Subagent memory locations: `~/.claude/agent-memory/<agent>/`, `.claude/agent-memory/<agent>/` (meant to be committed), and `.claude/agent-memory-local/<agent>/` (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents).

Cloud Projects memory is stored by Anthropic's service and managed in Project settings > Memory. It is separate from local auto memory (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects).

Cloud sessions see the repo's CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules because they are part of the clone. They do not see `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or user settings (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings).
format_and_model:
Everything is plain Markdown. Records are mutable files with no version history, no hashes and no append-only log.

Auto memory works as an index plus one file per memory:
- `MEMORY.md` is the index, "one line per memory", with entries like `- [build-and-test.md](build-and-test.md): npm run build...`.
- Each topic file (e.g. `user_role.md`, `feedback_testing.md`, `debugging.md`) has YAML frontmatter with `name`, `description` and `type` (user|feedback|project|reference), followed by a Markdown body.
- Since v2.1.214, Claude Code stamps an ISO 8601 `modified` field on any file that has frontmatter when Claude writes it. It never adds frontmatter to a file that lacks it.

Claude edits or deletes entries in place, and users can edit or delete them too (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory).

CLAUDE.md model:
- `@path` imports, relative or absolute, recursive up to four hops. Code spans and fences are not parsed for imports.
- Block-level HTML comments are stripped before injection.
- Files are concatenated from the filesystem root down to the working directory, with CLAUDE.local.md after CLAUDE.md at each level. Nothing overrides anything else.
- Rules take YAML `paths:` globs, with a budget of 1,000 expanded patterns and 4 MiB.
- Content reaches the model "as a user message after the system prompt, not as part of the system prompt", and is "context, not enforced configuration".

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.
multi_writer_and_merge:
Auto memory:
- Many writers on one machine share one directory: all worktrees and subdirectories of a repo since v2.1.63 (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
- No locking, CRDT or merge is documented. Claude writes memory with its ordinary file tools. Since v2.1.208 the Edit tool accepts a changed file only when `old_string` still matches the current content exactly; otherwise Claude re-reads the file (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference). Write replaces the whole file.
- The changelog mentions "memory write conflicts" with retried writes in Cowork (v2.1.280), so some conflict detection exists. The internals are undocumented.
- There is no cross-machine merge, because files are never synced.

CLAUDE.md and subagent `project` memory: multiple writers and merging are delegated entirely to git. They are "shared with your team through version control" and merged like any text file. A gitignored CLAUDE.local.md exists only in the worktree that created it, so the docs suggest importing `@~/.claude/...` to share personal notes across worktrees (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents).

Precedence: user rules load before project rules, but neither overrides the other. On a conflict "Claude may follow either one". Managed policy CLAUDE.md cannot be excluded (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory).

Cloud Projects memory: parallel cloud threads share it, but no concurrency semantics are documented. A project belongs to one user and cannot be shared (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects).
realtime:
There is no real-time propagation.
- MEMORY.md is read at the start of each conversation, up to the first 200 lines or 25KB.
- Topic files are read on demand, so a concurrent session on the same machine may pick up newer files, but nothing pushes or notifies it.
- Nothing crosses machines or cloud environments (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory).
- CLAUDE.md changes travel at git push/pull speed.
- Cloud session sharing gives recipients the latest state on open, but "their view doesn't update in real time" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web).

On compaction, the project-root CLAUDE.md, unscoped rules and auto memory are "re-injected from disk", and the plan-mode plan is re-injected too. Path-scoped rules and nested CLAUDE.md files go into message history, so compaction summarizes them away until a matching file is read again. Invoked skills are re-injected with caps of 5,000 tokens each and 25,000 in total (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window). The InstructionsLoaded hook reports `load_reason: "compact"` on these reloads (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks).
search_retrieval:
Retrieval is index-plus-file-reading, with no documented search engine, embeddings or full-text index.
- MEMORY.md, the curated index, is auto-loaded up to 200 lines or 25KB.
- Topic files are not loaded at startup. "Claude reads them on demand using its standard file tools", and the UI shows "Recalled N memories" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory).
- Near the limit, Claude Code reminds Claude to shorten the index. Over the limit, the write still succeeds but returns an error telling Claude to rewrite it. Before v2.1.210 the excess was silently truncated (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
- The changelog mentions memory being "recalled, indexed, or used by memory extraction" (v2.1.273), a background "memory-extraction" writer (v2.1.77), and Claude Tag memory recall that depends on the default Sonnet model (v2.1.286). These hint at model-assisted recall and extraction pipelines that the docs do not describe, so I could not verify them.

CLAUDE.md retrieval is structural:
- ancestors load at launch
- subdirectory CLAUDE.md files load lazily when Claude reads files there
- path-scoped rules load when a matching file is read
- `claudeMdExcludes` skips files
- `/context` and `/memory` show what loaded

Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.
links_sessions_to_code:
Linking is weak and indirect.
- Auto memory is keyed only by repository identity (the project directory) and dated only by the `modified` frontmatter timestamp. It records no session id, prompt, commit SHA or file/line anchor, and it deliberately excludes what "can derive from the code or git history" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory).
- Session transcripts (`<session>.jsonl`) sit next to the memory directory but are not referenced by memory entries. They are deleted after cleanupPeriodDays, default 30, while memory survives the sweep (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory).
- CLAUDE.md and subagent `project` memory are versioned in git with the code, so git history ties instructions to commits but not to the sessions that produced them (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents).
scale:
There are no claims about throughput or number of memories; the published limits are budgets.
- MEMORY.md loads the first 200 lines or 25KB, whichever comes first.
- CLAUDE.md should stay under 200 lines. Files up to 4 MiB load in full; larger ones are skipped. Startup warnings fire per file and for a combined total.
- Imports go at most four hops deep.
- Path-rule brace expansion is capped at 1,000 patterns and 4 MiB.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.

Other limits: project instructions in cloud Projects hold up to 16,000 characters (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects); compaction re-injects up to five recently modified files and caps skills at 5,000 tokens each and 25,000 in total (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window).
privacy_security:
At rest:
- Data under `~/.claude` is plaintext. The docs say transcripts and history "are not encrypted at rest. OS file permissions are the only protection", and a credential that a tool reads or prints lands in the session JSONL (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory). No encryption or secret redaction is documented for memory files; what gets saved depends on the model's judgment.
- Retention: memory files are exempt from the cleanupPeriodDays sweep. `claude project purge` deletes a project's transcripts and auto memory (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory).

Treating stored instructions as hostile:
- An external `@` import in a project CLAUDE.md triggers a one-time approval dialog "to protect you from files other people commit to a shared project".
- Symlinks to network paths (UNC, /net) are not followed.
- In Cowork sessions, out-of-tree imports in user-scope files are skipped.
- A repo-supplied `autoMemoryDirectory` is honored only under workspace trust. With `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories`, memory is neither loaded from nor saved to such a directory.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.

Hardening in the changelog:
- v2.1.284 neutralizes "invisible characters and tags that imitate Claude Code's own markup" in MEMORY.md and recalled notes before they reach Claude.
- v2.1.285 stops auto memory from being turned on from background sessions or sessions that a tool started.

Source: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md.

Enforcement: CLAUDE.md and memory are not an enforcement layer. Permissions and hooks are (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions).

Where it is off or unavailable:
- Self-hosted environments run with auto memory off by default.
- `--bare`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1` and safe mode disable it.

Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars.

License: Claude Code is proprietary ("© Anthropic PBC. All rights reserved", https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/LICENSE.md).
license: Proprietary: "© Anthropic PBC. All rights reserved. Use is subject to Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service" (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/LICENSE.md). The npm package says "SEE LICENSE IN README.md" (https://registry.npmjs.org/@anthropic-ai/claude-code).
lesson_for_parinn:
Claude Code keeps three things in three places:
- what humans write: CLAUDE.md, shared through git, bounded in size, re-injected from disk after compaction
- what the agent writes: auto memory, mutable Markdown that stays on one machine and is never synced or merged
- the raw history: session JSONL, deleted after 30 days

Two parts of this were later fixed in the field. MEMORY.md, which the model writes itself, is injected into every session automatically, so Anthropic had to add sanitization against hidden characters and fake markup in v2.1.284. And over-budget index content was silently dropped until v2.1.210 made it an explicit error.

For ParleyInn this means:
- Let only human-pinned TrustedText enter the restore block that is re-injected after compaction, under a hard line/byte budget. A budget overflow should be an audited, counted error, never a silent truncation (I6).
- Treat anything an agent wrote into memory as recalled, untrusted, enveloped and pull-only content, never auto-loaded (I2).
- Keep the append-only, hash-chained record underneath, so any MEMORY.md-style index stays a rebuildable projection (I10) rather than the mutable, history-free source of truth Claude Code uses.
- Copy Claude Code's keying by git repository so all worktrees share one store, but carry the session, commit and timestamp links Claude Code leaves out.
confidence: high for documented behavior, which comes from current official docs and the changelog as of 2026-10-01. Model-assisted recall, memory extraction and the conflict-detection internals are not described in the docs and could not be verified. GitHub issue search was unavailable from this session, so I found no third-party technical discussion.

name: Claude Code background agents (agent view)
status: beta
what_is_stored: Agent view itself stores only control-plane state. That covers a roster of running background sessions for reconnecting after a restart, per-session state for the agent view row (state, detail, tempo, needs), a per-session scratch dir and a supervisor log (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#where-state-is-stored). The full conversation is the ordinary Claude Code transcript: every message, tool call and tool result. Subagent transcripts, large tool outputs spilled to files and pre-edit file snapshots for checkpoints sit next to it, and prompt history goes to history.jsonl (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory). Row summaries are generated by a Haiku-class model and not kept as history. While a session works, the row updates at most every 15 s from the session's own output. At end of turn a model request writes a fresh summary (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#row-summaries). Code changes are stored as git commits on a per-session worktree branch. When a remote exists, the session pushes that branch and can open a draft PR (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#how-file-edits-are-isolated).
where_stored: Local disk under the Claude config dir (~/.claude, or $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, which gives a separate supervisor instance): ~/.claude/daemon/roster.json, ~/.claude/jobs/<id>/state.json, ~/.claude/jobs/<id>/tmp/ (exported as $CLAUDE_JOB_DIR), ~/.claude/daemon.log, ~/.claude/daemon.lock (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#where-state-is-stored). Transcripts are at ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-project-path>/<session>.jsonl, with subagents/ and tool-results/ subdirectories (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory). Worktrees are at <repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>/ on branch worktree-<name> (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees). The docs say "The conversation transcript always stays on your local machine, available through claude --resume" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#what-deleting-a-session-removes). Nothing goes into git notes, custom refs or a server. The only git artifacts are ordinary branches, commits and PRs.
format_and_model: Transcripts are append-style JSONL, one session per file, kept per project. A transcript that is set aside is renamed (.orphaned-<ts>-<suffix>.jsonl, .jsonl.superseded-<ts>), not overwritten or deleted. That makes it close to append-only, but there is no hash chain or integrity check (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory; v2.1.196 note at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#version-history). state.json and roster.json are JSON documents rewritten in place. The docs say they "are not a stable interface". An older version must keep fields it does not recognize, as a forward-compat rule (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#where-state-is-stored). The stable, read-only interface is `claude agents --json [--all] [--cwd]`. Each entry carries: cwd, kind, startedAt (ms), short id (the jobs dir name), sessionId (UUID), name, pid, state (working/blocked/done/failed/stopped), status (busy/waiting/idle) and waitingFor (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#list-sessions-as-json). The data model is a session-centric job record with a state machine. One supervisor runs one OS process per session, and the code side is a git worktree plus branch.
multi_writer_and_merge: There is one writer per transcript. The docs say "Two processes can't write to the same transcript", and opening a session already held by a live process is refused (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#opening-a-session-says-the-conversation-is-already-open). Code is isolated per session through git worktrees. Inside a git repo, writes to the shared checkout are blocked until the session moves into its worktree. Tool-level checks block Edit/Write to the main checkout, plus git -C, GIT_DIR and cd redirects (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#how-claude-code-enforces-isolation). A git worktree lock is held while a session runs. A stale-lock sweep releases locks of dead processes (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#clean-up-subagent-and-background-session-worktrees). There is no automatic merge. Claude commits, pushes its own branch and may open a draft PR. It never pushes to main/master, never force-pushes and never merges, so humans merge through the forge (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#how-file-edits-are-isolated). Transcripts are never merged across sessions. /fork copies a conversation into a new session (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#copy-the-session-with-fork). Outside git, parallel sessions are not isolated. Other VCSs are covered through WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#how-file-edits-are-isolated).
realtime: Real time on one machine only. A local supervisor process hosts the sessions. It survives terminal close, sleep and auto-update. Processes stop after about 1 h idle, and sessions stop when the machine shuts down (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#the-supervisor-process, #limitations). Row state and summaries update live, at most every 15 s while working. Needs-input, finished and failed events fire notifications and the Notification hook (agent_needs_input / agent_completed) (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#version-history v2.1.198). Sessions can pass short text messages (not history) to each other. On the same machine this goes over a per-session Unix socket or named pipe restricted to the OS user. To other machines or cloud sessions it relays through Anthropic servers over Remote Control (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging). The session history itself is not synced across machines by agent view. Remote Control does store the transcript on Anthropic servers while it is connected (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage).
search_retrieval: Agent view filters live session metadata, not the content of past history: a:<agent>, s:<state>, n:<name or first prompt> (v2.1.287+), o:<text in result>, and #1234 or a URL for a linked PR (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#filter-sessions). There is a peek panel showing the latest output, claude logs <id>, and full resume through `claude --resume <id|name|partial-id>`. A /resume picker in agent view also covers deleted sessions (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view). Prompt history supports Ctrl+R search over history.jsonl (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory). I found no documented full-text or semantic search across transcripts.
links_sessions_to_code: Partly, and only for display. A session is linked to a PR through observed commands: gh pr edit/comment/close/ready output, gh pr checkout, or a push followed by a gh pr view branch lookup, retried for up to five later git/gh/glab/curl commands. The row shows the PR number colored by checks/review/merge status (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#pull-request-status). The worktree branch (worktree-<name>) ties a session to its commits, and the session ends with a report naming path, branch or PR. The docs describe no persisted session-to-commit provenance: no commit trailers, git notes or prompt-to-line attribution. The PR link lives in local state. Because the transcript is local only, a PR reviewer elsewhere cannot get from the code back to the session.
scale: No numeric scale claims. The docs only warn that running ten agents in parallel uses quota about ten times as fast. Sessions are local and limited by machine resources. A possibly-low-memory failure mode is documented (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#limitations, #a-session-fails-before-starting-with-a-possibly-low-memory-note). Transcripts are deleted after cleanupPeriodDays (default 30). The same sweep removes Claude-created worktrees older than that (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees).
privacy_security: The docs say transcripts and history "are not encrypted at rest. OS file permissions are the only protection." Secrets read by tools, such as .env contents or printed credentials, land verbatim in the JSONL. Local transcripts get no redaction. Mitigations are cleanupPeriodDays, CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY and deny rules on credential files (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory#plaintext-storage). Redaction of known API-key and token patterns applies only to the opt-in transcript upload after the feedback survey (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage). Workspace trust is required before dispatch. Permission modes inherit with a permissiveness order: checked-in project settings cannot raise the mode to auto or bypass (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#permission-mode). The supervisor uses the same stored credentials as interactive sessions (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view#the-supervisor-process). Worktree creation refuses symlinked .claude, .claude/worktrees or worktree paths (fixed in v2.1.212) (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees). Messaging sockets are restricted to the OS user, with a /tmp/cc-socks-<uid> fallback, and inbound messages go through crossSessionInbound accept/hold/refuse. Messages arrive as plain text, and @-mentions are not auto-attached, which is a partial guard against injection (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging). I found no integrity protection for the transcript, such as hashing or signing.
lesson_for_parinn: Anthropic's own multi-agent design keeps conversation history and code apart. Transcripts stay as local, single-writer, plaintext JSONL and never enter git. Git carries only code, on a per-session worktree branch with push and a draft PR, never main and never auto-merge. Coordination happens through local supervisor state plus out-of-band, user-scoped socket messages that pass text, not history. ParleyInn should take two parts: one writer per session log, enforced like Claude Code's lock-and-refuse, and a stable read interface (like `claude agents --json`) over private, unstable state files. ParleyInn should add what is missing. That means a hash chain and redaction at write time, because Claude Code admits OS permissions are the only protection. It also means a durable session-to-commit/PR link that can travel with the code, because Claude Code's PR link lives only in local state and dies with the machine and the 30-day cleanup.
license: Proprietary (Anthropic commercial terms); Claude Code is not open source. I did not check the license text on this pass.

name: Claude Code checkpointing (/rewind, file history)
status: shipped
license: Proprietary. The claude-code repo LICENSE.md reads: "(c) Anthropic PBC. All rights reserved. Use is subject to Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service" (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/LICENSE.md).
what_is_stored:
Pre-edit snapshots of files changed by Claude's file-editing tools, taken at each checkpoint. A checkpoint is created for every user prompt that starts a turn (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing). The SDK docs say the tracked tools are Write, Edit and NotebookEdit. On rewind, Claude Code deletes files it created and restores modified files to their checkpoint-time content (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing).

Retention:
- Snapshots are kept for the 100 most recent checkpoints in a session. Snapshot files that no retained checkpoint references are deleted, except each file's first snapshot, which the VS Code extension uses as the baseline for session diffs (checkpointing doc; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory).

The conversation side of a checkpoint is the session transcript. Checkpoints are "saved with the conversation", so /rewind still works after resume. Rewind actions are restore code, restore conversation, restore both, "summarize from here" and "summarize up to here". Summarizing leaves the original messages in the transcript (checkpointing doc).

NOT captured (all from the checkpointing doc):
- changes made by Bash commands (rm, mv, cp)
- most subagent edits; only a foreground forked skill (context: fork) is restorable, and background forks and background /code-review --fix are not
- manual edits outside Claude Code, and edits by other concurrent sessions, unless they touch the same files
- messages queued mid-turn
- symlinked or hard-linked paths, which are skipped on restore

Per the SDK doc, it also does not undo directory create, move or delete, and it does not track remote or network files.

The docs state checkpoints are "not a replacement for version control"; use Git for permanent history.
where_stored:
Local disk only, in the user's config directory (default ~/.claude, movable with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR):
- Backup blobs go in ~/.claude/file-history/<session-id>/.
- Per-checkpoint metadata goes in the session transcript at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl, which also holds every message, tool call and tool result (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions).

It is not git: nothing goes in the working tree, git objects, refs or notes.

A retention sweep deletes file-history/<session>/ and transcripts older than cleanupPeriodDays (default 30, minimum 1, 0 is rejected) (claude-directory doc, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference). The sweep pauses if the retention period cannot be determined safely, and does not run in claude -p --bare (claude-directory doc).

Checkpointing can be turned off with fileCheckpointingEnabled:false or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FILE_CHECKPOINTING=1 (settings-reference, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars). `claude project purge` deletes a project's file-history entries along with its transcripts (claude-directory doc).
format_and_model:
Whole-file copies, not deltas. The on-disk format is not officially documented, and the sessions doc warns that the transcript entry format "is internal to Claude Code and changes between versions".

Observed format (from user bug reports, not official docs):
- Backup files are named <16-hex-id>@v<N>, one id per tracked file and a version counter per backup, for example 456bdc92d4463e15@v1..@v4 (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/20671).
- How the id is derived (likely a path hash) is unverified.
- The transcript holds JSON lines of type "file-history-snapshot" with fields messageId, snapshot.{messageId, trackedFileBackups (a map keyed by file path), timestamp} and isSnapshotUpdate (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/30802, https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/9736).
- Ordinary user and assistant entries carry uuid/parentUuid links (a tree of messages), sessionId, cwd, version and gitBranch (issue 30802).

Model: a checkpoint is identified by the UUID of the user message that started the turn. The SDK exposes it as the checkpoint id for rewindFiles(uuid) / rewind_files(uuid). It needs enableFileCheckpointing plus the replay-user-messages extra arg. A hidden CLI flag works too: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING=true claude -p --resume <session> --rewind-files <uuid> (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing).

There is no hash chain or integrity metadata on snapshots in any source found.
multi_writer_and_merge:
Single writer per session. No merge exists.

- Checkpoints "are tied to the session that created them" (SDK doc).
- Resuming the same session in two terminals without forking makes "messages from both interleave into one transcript" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions).
- Forking (/branch, --fork-session) copies the original session's backups into the fork. If a copy fails, for example on a full disk, that backup is missing in the fork and a later rewind fails (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#no-files-were-restored).
- Edits by other concurrent sessions are normally not captured (checkpointing doc).

A restore overwrites each tracked path with its checkpoint content, or deletes it if Claude created it. There is no three-way merge with concurrent changes. The docs imply this by "restores the files it modified to their content at that point" (SDK doc); it is not stated as a merge policy anywhere.

Bug history in this area:
- Cross-session contamination bugs, where snapshot and message entries landed in the wrong session's JSONL after /resume (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/30802, closed).
- Bash mv of a tracked file followed by auto-restore of the source (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/20671, closed).
realtime:
None. Checkpoints are local, per-session files with no sync or sharing.

Cross-machine handoff exists only for cloud sessions, and it goes the other way:
- `claude --teleport` fetches the session's pushed git branch and loads the conversation history into the terminal.
- The terminal copy then diverges ("new work there stays local") (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web).
- The docs do not say teleport carries file-history checkpoints, so that is unverified. Code moves across machines through git, not through checkpoints.
search_retrieval:
No search. Retrieval works three ways:
- the /rewind menu (or Esc Esc), which lists each prompt in the session and shows per-checkpoint file diff stats (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing; UI example in https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/20201)
- SDK rewindFiles(uuid)
- the hidden --rewind-files CLI flag (SDK doc)

Rewind restores state; it does not query it. For scripting, the docs point to /export, claude -p --resume, hook transcript_path, or the Agent SDK rather than parsing JSONL (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions). Open bugs report the code-restore option sometimes missing or not reverting (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/14002, https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/91733, both open).
links_sessions_to_code:
Yes, tightly but only inside one session. Every checkpoint is keyed to the user-prompt message UUID, and its file backups are the pre-images for edits made after that prompt. So prompt -> file state is recoverable and the menu shows per-prompt diffs (checkpointing doc; SDK doc; issue 20201). The VS Code extension uses each file's first snapshot as the baseline for session diffs (checkpointing doc).

It does not link to git commits. Transcript entries record cwd and gitBranch (issue 30802 sample), but nothing ties a checkpoint to a commit SHA. Everything ages out with the 30-day sweep. Durable session-to-code linkage is left to git.
scale:
No published scale claims. Documented limits are 100 checkpoints per session and about 30-day retention by default (checkpointing doc; claude-directory doc).

Bug reports show unbounded growth before fixes (all closed):
- a 222 MB transcript with 981k empty file-history-snapshot entries at about 31/s, v2.0.14 (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/9736)
