name: Claude Code native OpenTelemetry export (metrics, events/logs, beta traces)
category: first-party session event transport (push telemetry, not a store)
status: shipped (metrics and log events GA; traces are beta behind CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1; "detailed beta tracing" is a further opt-in). The docs reference Claude Code versions up to v2.1.283, so the feature is current as of Oct 2026. The discovery note's "five event types" is out of date: the page now documents about 25 event types.
what_is_stored:
Claude Code stores nothing itself. It emits three OTel signals to a collector the user configures.
(1) Metrics (meter com.anthropic.claude_code): claude_code.session.count (start_type fresh/resume/continue/agents_view), lines_of_code.count (added/removed, model), pull_request.count, commit.count, cost.usage (USD), token.usage (input/output/cacheRead/cacheCreation), code_edit_tool.decision, active_time.total.
(2) Events as OTLP log records: user_prompt, assistant_response, tool_result, tool_decision, api_request, api_error, api_refusal, api_request_body, api_response_body, permission_mode_changed, auth, mcp_server_connection, internal_error, plugin_installed, plugin_loaded, skill_activated, at_mention, api_retries_exhausted, hook_registered, hook_execution_start, hook_execution_complete, hook plugin metrics, compaction (pre_tokens/post_tokens, trigger auto/manual), subagent_completed, feedback survey, retention_sweep and managed_settings_resolved.
(3) Beta traces: a claude_code.interaction root span per prompt, with child spans claude_code.llm_request, claude_code.tool (then tool.blocked_on_user and tool.execution), subagent spans, and claude_code.hook under detailed tracing. With OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=1 a tool.output span event carries file contents, Bash output and MCP/WebFetch results.
Content is redacted by default: only lengths are sent unless opt-in flags are set. With OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES, the full Messages API request and response bodies are emitted. Those bodies hold the whole conversation history, system prompt and tool results. Extended thinking is always redacted.
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage
where_stored:
Wherever the operator's backend puts it. Claude Code pushes over OTLP (grpc, http/protobuf or http/json) to OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, with per-signal overrides. It can also expose a Prometheus scrape or write to the console.
One exception writes to local disk: OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES=file:<dir> writes untruncated .request.json and .response.json files plus an index.jsonl. The index links session_id, request_id, message_uuid and the file names. The events then carry a body_ref path instead of the body.
Known backends: Elastic has a documented integration that indexes events into the logs-claude_code.events.otel-* data stream, fed by managed OTLP, the Elastic Agent OTLP receiver or the EDOT Collector (https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/integrations/claude_code). Anthropic's ROI guide repo ships Prometheus, OTel Collector and Grafana compose files (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-monitoring-guide).
Better Stack and Last9 ingestion was named in the discovery note but not verified in this pass. The session's real transcript store is separate and not covered by this page.
format_and_model:
Standard OpenTelemetry data model: OTLP metrics (delta temporality by default, cumulative optional), OTLP LogRecords with an event.name attribute, and OTLP spans with W3C trace context.
Resource attributes: service.name=claude-code, or claude-code-desktop for the Desktop app.
Standard attributes on every record: session.id, ccr.session.id (cloud sessions; equals CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID), organization.id, user.account_uuid, user.account_id, user.id (installation-scoped random id), user.email (OAuth), terminal.type, and optionally app.version, app.entrypoint and vcs.* repository identity.
Correlation fields:
- prompt.id: a UUIDv4 linking every event produced while handling one user prompt.
- event.sequence: a 0-based counter per process, not per session. Across /clear or a resume it can repeat or go backwards within one session, so the docs say to sort by event.timestamp and break ties with event.sequence.
- interaction.sequence: likewise counted per process.
- tool_use_id, request_id, client_request_id and message.uuid join records to transcript messages.
- trace_id/span_id appear on events when an inbound TRACEPARENT is set (SDK and -p sessions only).
- Some span attributes follow the OTel GenAI conventions (gen_ai.system=anthropic, gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.tool.call.id).
Content attributes are cut at CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH (61440 UTF-16 units by default) with a [TRUNCATED ...] marker and *_truncated / *_original_length companion fields.
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage
multi_writer_and_merge:
No merge semantics. Each Claude Code process is an independent OTLP writer. Combining processes, sessions, users, machines and cloud sandboxes is left to the backend, which joins on session.id, ccr.session.id, user and organization attributes, OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and the optional vcs.* repo identity.
The docs say Claude Code "emits the raw event stream only. Anomaly detection, baselining, correlation across sessions, and alerting are the responsibility of your SIEM or observability backend."
Ordering is not total even within one session (see event.sequence). There is no hash chain, no dedup key beyond the UUIDs, and no causal ordering across writers.
Managed settings can force every writer to one collector. A managed endpoint or credential strips the endpoints a developer set, so credentials cannot leak to another collector.
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage
realtime:
Near-real-time push through batching exporters. Defaults: logs every 5 s (OTEL_LOGS_EXPORT_INTERVAL=5000), traces every 5 s, metrics every 60 s. Cloud sessions export through their own sandbox network, so the collector's domain must be on the environment allowlist.
Delivery is best effort:
- If the otelHeadersHelper fails, "your telemetry backend receives nothing from the session until the helper works again".
- Some background WebFetch/WebSearch results are never recorded.
- Intermediate API retries are not logged as separate events.
The docs give no retry or queue guarantee and no durable local buffer (unverified beyond the doc's silence).
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage
search_retrieval:
None in Claude Code. Search is whatever the backend provides: SIEM or log full-text search, Elastic dashboards with ECS fields, PromQL or Grafana for metrics, trace waterfalls.
The recommended query pattern is to filter by prompt.id, which returns the user_prompt, api_request and tool_result events for that prompt. Recall into the agent is not part of this feature, so there is no pull-back path to the model.
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage
links_sessions_to_code:
Partially, and opt-in. Three links exist:
- Commit SHA on a prompt (v2.1.269+): with OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1, a successful git commit run by the Bash or PowerShell tool adds the commit SHA (vcs.ref.head.revision) and the branch (vcs.ref.head.name, vcs.ref.head.type) to its tool_result event. That joins prompt.id, session.id and the commit.
- Repository identity (v2.1.269+): with OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_REPOSITORY=true, every record carries vcs.repository.url.full, vcs.owner.name, vcs.repository.name and vcs.provider.name (github/gitlab/bitbucket/gitea), taken from the origin remote with credentials stripped. Anthropic's own telemetry drops all vcs.* keys.
- Aggregate counters: commit.count, pull_request.count and lines_of_code.count, without diffs.
Edit diffs and file paths appear only in trace spans and tool_input when OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS and OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT are set.
Nothing is written into git itself: no notes, trailers or refs.
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage
scale:
No throughput or volume claims. The docs only warn about metric cardinality and give switches for it: OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID, _VERSION, _ACCOUNT_UUID, _ENTRYPOINT, _RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and _REPOSITORY. The 60 KB content cap is sized for backends that limit attribute values to 64 KB.
The ROI guide repo had about 370 stars when fetched (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-monitoring-guide). Its fetched summary reported only one commit and no date, so its activity is unclear.
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage
privacy_security:
Telemetry is off unless CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1. Content redaction is on by default, with separate opt-ins per class:
- OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS: prompt text.
- OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES: response text. It falls back to the prompt flag when unset.
- OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS: commands, paths, arguments, real MCP, skill and plugin names, and commit SHAs. Without it, names collapse to "custom", "mcp_tool" or "third-party".
- OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT: raw tool output, in spans only.
- OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES: full conversation history. It implies consent to all the other flags.
- OTEL_LOG_MANAGED_SETTINGS: redacted managed settings plus a SHA-256 digest.
Even with the flags off, user.email and account ids are sent by default when signed in. The docs tell operators to filter these in the backend.
Built-in secret scanning is not claimed. The docs say arguments "may still contain sensitive values, so configure your telemetry backend to filter or redact".
Transport security: TLS and mTLS (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CLIENT_KEY/CERTIFICATE, CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_CERT/KEY), bearer headers, and a dynamic otelHeadersHelper script refreshed every 29 minutes (HTTP protocols only).
Hardening:
- Repository .claude/settings.json and settings.local.json cannot turn telemetry on, change its destination or enable content capture. A repo can only turn a signal off.
- Managed settings lock the endpoint and credentials.
- OTEL_* variables are not passed to Bash, hook, MCP or LSP subprocesses.
- vcs.* and custom attributes never go to Anthropic.
No encryption at rest. That is the backend's responsibility.
Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage
lesson_for_parinn:
Use the OTel stream as a model for correlation and redaction, but not as ParleyInn's record. It is batched, best effort, truncated at 60 KB, has no hash chain, and its per-process event.sequence can repeat or run backwards inside one resumed session. It is also network push, which I4 forbids in ParleyInn's core.
Three things are worth copying:
(1) Give every record a session-scoped, strictly monotonic sequence and a hash link. Keep session.id, prompt.id, tool_use_id and message.uuid as join keys, so a ParleyInn record can be cross-referenced with an organization's OTel or SIEM data.
(2) Copy the trust split. Repository-level settings can only turn capture down, never up, and content capture is opt-in per class (prompts, responses, tool arguments, tool output), recorded so an audit can see it (I2, I6).
(3) Copy the commit-SHA-on-tool_result idea, recording it locally from the PostToolUse hook rather than over the network. That gives a cheap, verifiable link from a prompt to the code it changed.
If integration is wanted, an exporter outside the core can derive OTel from the ParleyInn record, keeping the record the source of truth (I10). Pointing ParleyInn at Claude Code's own stream would not achieve that.
license: Proprietary. OTel export is a built-in feature of Claude Code, which ships under Anthropic's commercial terms; a license text was not checked in this pass. The output format is the open OpenTelemetry/OTLP specification.

name: Claude Code OpenTelemetry Export
status: beta
what_is_stored: OpenTelemetry log events representing every action in Claude Code agentic sessions: tool calls (shell commands, file operations, MCP tool invocations), API requests, user prompts, permission decisions, and lifecycle events (hook registration, plugin loading, skill activation, MCP server connections). Each event is a structured OTLP log record with an event-name attribute identifying its type and event-specific attributes namespaced under claude_code.*. Event types include tool_result, process, tool_decision, iam, api_request, api_error, api_refusal, permission_mode_changed, mcp_server_connection, hook_registered, hook_execution_start, hook_execution_complete, plugin_loaded, and skill_activated. Telemetry verbosity is controlled by four environment variable gates: OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS (controls prompt text inclusion), OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS (controls tool_parameters and tool_input), OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT (controls tool_result content), and OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES (controls raw API body inclusion). When gates are disabled, corresponding fields are absent from the document; the ingest pipeline handles gracefully.
where_stored: Elasticsearch data stream logs-claude_code.events.otel-* (indexed by Elastic Agent, EDOT Collector, or direct managed OTLP ingestion to Elastic Cloud). Events transmitted via OTLP (OpenTelemetry Protocol) HTTP to one of three ingestion paths: (A) managed OTLP endpoint on Elastic Cloud, (B) Elastic Agent's built-in OTLP HTTP receiver (default port 4318), or (C) Elastic Distribution of OpenTelemetry Collector with otlp receiver and elasticsearch exporter. Requires Claude Code CLI version 2.1.0 or later.
format_and_model: OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) log records in JSON, mapped to ECS (Elastic Common Schema) and structured as Elasticsearch documents. Each OTLP log record carries event-name attribute (mapped to event.action in ECS), attributes namespaced under claude_code.*, and body content. Ingest pipeline parses JSON-encoded tool parameters and inputs into structured fields; extracts security-relevant fields (user, command, cost_usd, permission_level); categorizes events using ECS. Final documents indexed with typed fields, allowing SQL and KQL queries. Dashboards provided for visualization of tool invocations, costs, permissions, and MCP server access.
multi_writer_and_merge: Multiple Claude Code sessions (from same or different machines/users) can emit events concurrently to the same Elasticsearch cluster via OTLP. No client-side merge logic; Elasticsearch handles concurrent ingestion. Ingest pipeline applies consistently to all events regardless of source. Fleet can enforce organization-wide verbosity gates via MDM profiles or admin console, ensuring consistent processing. Managed settings cannot be overridden by user environment variables on managed devices. Events are additive/append-only; no modification or deletion of already-indexed events is supported via this transport.
realtime: Push-based, real-time event emission. Claude Code emits OTLP log records during agentic sessions as events occur. Transport is HTTP POST to configured OTLP receiver. Elastic Agent or collector immediately receives and forwards to Elasticsearch. Events appear in logs-claude_code.events.otel-* data stream within seconds (subject to network and indexing latency). Kibana Discover can query events in real-time as they arrive.
search_retrieval: Full-text and structured field search via Elasticsearch KQL (Kibana Query Language) and SQL. Ingest pipeline extracts structured fields: user, command, cost_usd, permission_level, tool_name, MCP server identity, tool_parameters (parsed from JSON). Example use cases: (1) Tool invocation auditing — query all Bash commands by user; (2) Permission analysis — find user_permanent auto-approvals; (3) Cost anomaly detection — aggregate cost_usd per user per day; (4) MCP server access monitoring — track which MCP servers users connect to and tools invoked. Dashboards provided for visualization. Original event preserved on pipeline errors (event.kind: pipeline_error) for inspection.
links_sessions_to_code: Events carry context identifiers (claude_code.session_id or similar, inferred from integration design) linking tool invocations to code changes. Tool call events include command text or tool parameters, allowing correlation with file operations and shell commands executed during a session. MCP server connections and tool invocations are tied to named servers and tools. Permission decisions (permission_mode_changed, tool_decision) include user and tool context. Cost tracking (cost_usd) aggregates per session/user. No explicit code repository or commit hash correlation in the described integration; correlation depends on command content and user context analysis.
privacy_security: Telemetry verbosity controlled by four environment variables (OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT, OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES). By default, prompt text and tool parameters are redacted (absent from documents). Enabling gates includes potentially sensitive content (commands, file contents, prompts). On managed devices, gates enforced fleet-wide via MDM profiles or admin console cannot be overridden locally, ensuring organizational control. Ingest pipeline applies securely; events with malformed JSON preserved with pipeline_error tag for inspection. Integration focuses on tool invocation auditing and permission analysis, inherently supporting security use cases. No encryption mentioned; relies on Elasticsearch cluster security and network TLS for transport via OTLP HTTP.
lesson_for_parinn: Claude Code's OTLP export demonstrates that agent session telemetry can be collected as structured, real-time events without modifying agent core logic: Claude Code emits events via environment variables (OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER, OTEL_LOG_* gates) without internal instrumentation burden. For ParleyInn, the key lesson is that a push-based telemetry protocol (OTLP) with verbosity gates allows fine-grained control over sensitive content (prompts, commands, tool details) at collection time, not indexing time. This aligns with ParleyInn's I2 (untrusted content never reaches the model) and I5 (redaction in logs): sensitive fields can be optional/absent from the transport, and verbosity is policy-controlled, not user-controlled on managed systems. However, OTLP is network-dependent and unsuitable for ParleyInn's I4 invariant (no network in shipped code); ParleyInn would need an offline append-only transport (git, file, or embedded DB) with optional later export to observability systems, not the reverse.

name: Claude Code Projects (redesigned "Projects" in claude.ai/code)
category: Coordinator of parallel cloud agent threads (hosted, single-user, git used for code only)
status: beta
what_is_stored:
Per project, hosted by Anthropic:
(1) The coordinator conversation, a long-running session that "keeps track of every thread it started" but "sees what threads report back, not every step they take".
(2) Thread transcripts. Each thread is a full cloud session with its own context window, and its full results stay in the thread.
(3) Project memory: "Notes Claude keeps about the project, such as requirements, decisions, and pitfalls, stored as files", with an index file MEMORY.md. Claude also saves user preferences, such as thread limits, there "on its own".
(4) Project instructions: human-set text "sent to each new thread and to Claude in the project conversation, up to 16,000 characters".
(5) A Library of uploaded files, folders and Google Drive folders, plus files threads produce, readable under /mnt/project-files.
(6) Settings: goal, models and effort, repositories, cloud environment, plugins, routines, per-thread usage.
Code changes are not stored in the project. They live in GitHub branches and PRs. Deleting a project removes "its threads, its memory, and its files", but "Branches and pull requests the threads pushed to GitHub aren't affected". Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects
where_stored:
Server/cloud (Anthropic-hosted). Transcripts, memory, instructions and Library are kept on Anthropic servers. "Anthropic stores the session transcript so you can return to the session later" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage).
Code goes to GitHub only: each cloud thread clones into an isolated Anthropic VM and pushes a per-thread branch through Anthropic's GitHub proxy.
Project memory is separate from the machine-local auto memory at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/. Local auto memory "is machine-local... not shared across machines or cloud environments" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory).
A thread run on the user's own computer through Remote Control "Starts with the project's instructions, but not with its memory files loaded" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects).
Only github.com repos are supported, not GHES, GitLab or Bitbucket. The Claude GitHub App is required.
format_and_model:
Hierarchy: project → one coordinator conversation → N threads. Each thread is one cloud session that maps to one branch and, optionally, one PR.
Thread states shown in Overview: Ready for review, Waiting on you, Working, Landing, Idle, Resolved. Threads auto-resolve after a week with no activity.
Project memory: the docs say "stored as files", with a MEMORY.md index. "Every cloud thread reads the index file MEMORY.md when it starts and opens the other files when it needs them" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects). This mirrors local auto memory: a Markdown index of one line per memory, plus topic files with YAML frontmatter (`type`: user/feedback/project/reference, and a `modified` ISO-8601 timestamp). Only the first 200 lines or 25KB of the index load at start (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory). Whether project memory uses exactly the same frontmatter schema is not documented: unverified.
Instructions are plain text, at most 16,000 characters.
The coordinator does not keep full history in context. It "works from recent messages, recent threads, and project memory rather than its full history". Threads auto-compact.
No export format, schema, hash chain or append-only guarantee is documented. Memory is a mutable store: users can read, edit and delete files in Project settings > Memory, and Claude can be asked to "forget" an entry.
multi_writer_and_merge:
Code: there is one branch per thread, started from the default branch. Overlaps are resolved through ordinary git and PR merge conflicts. The launch blog says overlapping work "resolves through standard merge conflict processes, treated like any other pull request" (https://claude.com/blog/projects-redesigned). Thread cards offer "Resolve conflicts", "Fix CI", "Address comments" and "Merge it" buttons. Threads watch their PR with auto-fix. GitHub sends no webhook when the base branch moves, so auto-fix cannot react to conflicts on its own (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web).
Memory: any thread or the coordinator may write. "Ask Claude in the project conversation or any cloud thread to remember a requirement, a decision, or a pitfall". "Every thread now adds to and draws from a shared memory" (blog). No concurrency control, locking, merge semantics or per-entry provenance is documented for simultaneous memory writes from parallel threads: unverifiable.
Settings: changes to instructions, repos, plugins and environment "reach new threads, not threads already running".
Writer scope: single user only. "A project belongs to one user. You can't share a project or its threads". You cannot move threads between projects or merge projects. Multi-person steering is pushed to Claude Tag in Slack (Team/Enterprise plans).
Local folders: two local threads in one folder "can overwrite each other's changes". A Worktree toggle or `claude remote-control --spawn worktree` isolates them.
realtime:
Partly real time, for one viewer.
Threads run in parallel and keep running after the laptop closes. They can be watched and steered from web, desktop or mobile.
The Overview pane shows a dot when a thread waits. Desktop notifications fire on coordinator posts, thread errors and input requests, but are desktop-only. Threads report to the coordinator when they finish, not step by step.
Memory and instruction updates are not pushed into running threads: changes reach new threads only. One exception: preferences saved to memory are followed "in later cloud threads".
Shared cloud-session links (outside Projects) "don't update in real time" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web). Project threads cannot be shared at all.
Sandboxes pause between turns. If one cannot resume, "the thread continues from a fresh clone, so uncommitted changes can be lost".
search_retrieval:
No user-facing search over memory or transcripts is documented.
Retrieval is LLM-driven:
- Threads load the MEMORY.md index at start and open topic files on demand with file tools.
- The coordinator can be asked to read threads, for example: "For every open thread, list what you asked it to do, what it assumed or couldn't reach..." (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects).
- Users browse thread transcripts, the Library tab, the Pull requests tab, and memory files in settings.
No API or CLI access to project memory is documented. Projects are unavailable in the terminal CLI and IDE extensions. A cloud session can be pulled to a terminal with `claude --teleport`, which "loads the full conversation history into your terminal" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web). Whether teleport works on project threads is not stated: unverified.
links_sessions_to_code:
Yes, structurally and by convention:
- Each cloud thread is one session working on its own branch, and opens a PR when needed. The Overview and Pull requests tabs map threads to PRs.
- PR review replies are posted under the user's GitHub account but "labeled as coming from Claude Code" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web).
- The session-to-branch link lives in Anthropic's service, not in git. No git notes, trailers or refs carrying transcripts or prompts are documented.
- After a project is deleted, branches and PRs remain but the transcripts and memory are gone. Git-side provenance is therefore lost unless commit or PR text captured it.
- Teleport fetches a cloud session's branch and its conversation together, which shows the service keeps a session↔repo/branch binding.
scale:
Enforced limit: "200 new threads per day across your projects". Otherwise "There's no fixed number" of concurrent threads, and user-stated caps are preferences, not hard limits.
Project instructions: at most 16,000 characters. Memory index: only the first 200 lines or 25KB load, if it matches local auto memory (inferred, not stated for projects).
Library: up to 100 files and 2 GB per pick, 480 MB per file. Folders: first 100 files up to 200 MB, files over 30 MB skipped, at most 10 folders or Drive folders per project.
Usage draws on the same plan limits and uses them faster. Threads that hit limits wait and auto-resume.
Repos: add the one or two repos most tasks need. Threads can add others mid-task, but only from a GitHub owner the project already uses.
All from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects.
Availability: public beta on Pro/Max, rolling out gradually. Not on Team/Enterprise and no org-level controls during beta. Not on Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry. Launched September 17, 2026 (https://claude.com/blog/projects-redesigned).
privacy_security:
Isolation: "each session runs in an isolated, Anthropic-managed VM". Network egress is limited by default through a security proxy "for audit logging and abuse prevention".
Credentials: GitHub credentials and signing keys "stay encrypted on Anthropic's servers and never enter a session's VM". A proxy attaches scoped credentials server-side. API credentials added to an environment are also attached outside the sandbox on Pro/Max. (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage)
Encryption at rest: infrastructure-level AES-256 disk encryption on the Anthropic API side (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage). No end-to-end or customer-key encryption is documented for project memory or transcripts.
Retention: consumer plans keep data 30 days, or 5 years if the user opts into model training. Deleting a cloud session removes its event data. Deleting a project removes threads, memory and files.
Redaction: no redaction of transcripts or project memory is documented. Redaction is mentioned only for feedback uploads and error reports, and for credential-like files left out of local bundle uploads.
Trust model: memory and CLAUDE.md are "context, not enforced configuration". Coordinator-saved preferences are "not enforced settings". Threads run in auto mode, and multi-repo projects apply no repo permission rules or hooks.
No documented defense against prompt injection through project memory, which any thread can write and every later thread reads at start.
Auto-fix warns that Claude's PR comments can trigger comment-driven automation such as Atlantis or Actions.
lesson_for_parinn:
Projects splits the problem the way ParleyInn should: git (branch per thread, PR, normal merge conflicts) carries only code, and a hosted service carries context. But its shared context layer is a mutable, LLM-curated MEMORY.md plus topic files that any parallel thread can write and every new thread auto-loads at start. It has no documented provenance, concurrency control or injection defense, and deleting the project erases all session history while the branches survive.

ParleyInn should take the good half: keep the human-authored brief (pinned constraints, delivered verbatim to every agent) separate from agent-written learnings (recall, pulled on demand and enveloped as untrusted). It should not adopt the bad half. Make every memory write an attributed, append-only, hash-chained event per writer, never an in-place file edit. Then concurrent agents across worktrees and sandboxes merge as a union of events, not as competing edits to a shared index. Store the session↔branch/commit binding where it outlives the hosted service, for example in git refs or notes or a portable record, so code provenance survives deletion of the coordinator.
license: Proprietary hosted service (Anthropic). Not open source.

name: Claude Code Remote Control
category: real-time session mirroring (relay plus server-held transcript mirror for a local agent process)
status: shipped. GA on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise per current docs. Trusted Devices add-on is beta (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control). Timeline: the `claude remote-control` subcommand appeared in CLI 2.1.51 (npm 2026-02-23); 2.1.58 (2026-02-25) says "Expand Remote Control to more users" (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md, https://registry.npmjs.org/@anthropic-ai/claude-code). HN launch thread 2026-02-25 (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47148454). Still actively developed: 213 changelog entries mention it, through 2.1.287 (2026-10-01). Not verified: whether it launched as a "research preview" limited to Max; I ran out of web-search budget.
what_is_stored:
While connected, Anthropic stores "the session transcript, including your messages, Claude's responses, and tool activity". The stored copy "keeps the conversation in sync across your devices and lets the session reconnect after a network drop" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#connection-and-security).

Server-side metadata (all from the remote-control page):
- session ID and title
- online/offline presence
- archived state
- model and effort selections
- a git diff view for the session directory: branch-vs-default-branch plus uncommitted edits

Files and photos attached from phone or web are downloaded to the machine under `~/.claude/uploads/<session>/` (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory).

Locally, Claude Code keeps its normal full transcript at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl`: "every message, tool call, and tool result". It also keeps subagent transcripts under `<session>/subagents/` and pre-edit file snapshots under `file-history/` (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory). Code, files and execution are not uploaded; "execution and filesystem access stay on your machine" (remote-control page).
where_stored:
Server/cloud: Anthropic servers hold the synced transcript, retained under the Data usage policy (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage):
- consumer: 30 days, or 5 years if the user opts in to model training
- commercial: 30 days

The local machine stays authoritative:
- plaintext JSONL under `~/.claude/projects/`, deleted after `cleanupPeriodDays` (default 30)
- attachments in `~/.claude/uploads/`
- Remote Control session bookkeeping in `~/.claude.json` (changelog 2.1.277: "Remote Control session bookkeeping failing when ~/.claude.json holds a malformed placeholder record", https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

Nothing is stored in git: no notes, refs or branches.
format_and_model:
The wire and server format is proprietary and undocumented. The model is a linear conversation of messages, tool activity and subagent/workflow progress, keyed by an opaque session ID (`session_...`, the part of the claude.ai/code URL after `/code/`). Sessions can be renamed, archived, unarchived and deleted (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web).

Evidence on the protocol, partly my inference:
- The server process spawns per-session children with `--sdk-url session_...` (issue https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/28334).
- The changelog mentions duplicate `control_response` messages "from WebSocket reconnects" (2.1.51), "bridge sessions" over WebSocket (2.1.76), and "work items" redelivered after "JWT refresh" (2.1.76) (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
- This suggests the bridge carries the Claude Code SDK message stream (user/assistant/control_request/control_response). This is inferred, not documented.

The cloud-session docs say `--teleport` uses "the same Remote Control session infrastructure that cloud sessions use" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web).

The local transcript is JSONL, one event per line (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory). Nothing indicates hash-chaining or signing anywhere.
multi_writer_and_merge:
There is no merge. One local `claude` process is the only executor; many devices are writers into its input queue. "send messages from your terminal, browser, and phone interchangeably" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control). Inputs are serialized into one linear conversation.

Ownership is exclusive: one host connection holds a session.
- Another host can take it over ("Another connection took over this session").
- A second terminal resuming the same conversation prints "Remote Control not started here" and does not steal the session.
- `/remote-control` moves the session explicitly (remote-control page).

History rewrites are not merged. If compaction rewrote the conversation, or `/resume` switched conversations, before a reconnect, Claude Code archives the old server session and mints a new one. Devices do not receive switched-to or `/teleport`-ed earlier history (remote-control page; changelog 2.1.224).

Delivery-semantics bugs fixed in the changelog (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md):
- duplicate assistant messages after WebSocket reconnect (2.1.51)
- stale work items redelivered after token refresh (2.1.76)
- messages marked read on arrival rather than when Claude started on them, and lost on quit (2.1.285)
- a message arriving during exit marked delivered but never answered (2.1.286)
- prior local history re-uploaded into a recreated server session (2.1.224)
- a teleported session appended to the original (2.1.261)

Concurrent sessions in one directory: server mode `--spawn same-dir` (default) shares the working tree "so they can conflict if editing the same files". `--spawn worktree` gives each on-demand session its own git worktree (remote-control page).
realtime:
Yes, live mirroring. Connection model (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#connection-and-security):
- The local process "makes outbound HTTPS requests only and never opens inbound ports".
- It "registers with the Anthropic API and polls for work".
- When a device connects, "the server routes messages between the web or mobile client and your local session over a streaming connection".

Polling and streaming (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md):
- 2.1.70: the poll rate drops to once per 10 minutes while connected (was 1–2 s), "cutting server load ~300×"; transport loss wakes fast polling.
- 2.1.251: live streaming of a foreground subagent's tool calls; background subagents show status only.

What devices see (remote-control page): progress of compaction and `/clear`, and running subagents and workflows. Stopping a task from a device stops it on the machine.

Timeouts and recovery (remote-control page):
- HTTP 403 is retried for up to 3 minutes.
- Server mode exits after about 10 minutes offline. Interactive mode retries indefinitely.
- Presence heartbeat failure disconnects after about 30 minutes.
- Sessions can be resumed for about 4 hours after the server stops.
- Forwarded dialogs expire after 5 minutes by default.

Push notifications go to the mobile app. Cross-session messages to other machines travel over the same Remote Control connection; an offline target gets its messages queued until it reconnects (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging).
search_retrieval:
No search over session content is documented. Retrieval is navigational:
- find a session by name in the claude.ai/code or mobile session list
- open the session URL or QR code
- filter for archived sessions
(https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web)

Locally, sessions come back with `claude --resume` / `--continue`, or `claude remote-control --continue` / `--session-id <id>` (remote-control page). The server returns a session's history to clients on open; a VS Code fix concerns "the server failed to return its history" (changelog, https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

There is no recall API for agents. For agent-to-agent use, `ListAgents`/`SendMessage` exchange plain-text messages only, "never the sender's conversation history or files" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging).
links_sessions_to_code:
Weakly, and only at runtime. When the directory is a git repo, a connected device's diff pane shows "changes since the branch split" from the default branch plus uncommitted edits, or only uncommitted edits on the default branch (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control).

Server mode can give each session its own git worktree (`--spawn worktree`). `--continue` falls back to the newest session from "this repository's other git worktrees" (remote-control page).

Not documented:
- recording which commits a session produced
- writing session IDs into commits, trailers or notes
- linking prompts to lines of code

The session is tied to a working directory and host, not to git objects.
scale:
Documented limits (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control):
- server mode: `--capacity` default 32 concurrent sessions per process
- interactive process: one remote session each ("one remote session per interactive process")
- auto-connect: each interactive process registers one session

Cross-session messaging limits (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging):
- at most 100 held messages and 50 queued accepted messages per receiver
- same-machine message cap of about 1M characters
- remote session lists read newest-first with bounded paging

Load: the 2.1.70 poll change cut server load "~300×" (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). The server credential lasts about 30 days before re-registration (2.1.267). No user counts or throughput claims were published.
privacy_security:
Transport and credentials:
- Outbound HTTPS only; no inbound ports.
- TLS through the Anthropic API.
- "multiple short-lived credentials, each scoped to a single purpose and expiring independently" to "limit the blast radius" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security).
- Requires a full-scope claude.ai login. API keys, `setup-token` tokens, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry and custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` gateways are refused.

No end-to-end encryption is claimed. The server routes and stores the transcript and serves it to the web and mobile clients, so the operator can read it; this is my inference from the docs. At-rest encryption for the Anthropic API is "infrastructure-level disk encryption (AES-256)" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage). No redaction of the Remote Control transcript is documented. Secret redaction is documented only for feedback/survey uploads and error reports (data-usage page).

The local transcript is "not encrypted at rest. OS file permissions are the only protection"; a credential that a tool prints lands in the JSONL (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory).

Governance (remote-control page):
- Off by default on Team and Enterprise until an Owner enables it.
- `disableRemoteControl` managed setting.
- Zero Data Retention orgs cannot enable it; HIPAA configurations are incompatible.
- A checked-in project `remoteControlAtStartup: true` is ignored, "so a checked-in file can't turn on Remote Control for everyone".
- Workspace-trust prompt and a one-time consent prompt before first use.

Trusted Devices (beta): a per-device credential, sign-in no older than 18 hours, and a biometric or passkey step-up. Only the device public key and metadata are stored (remote-control page).

Inbound peer messages "can't approve anything", can't change configuration, and embedded commands don't run (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging). `/list-agents` withholds working directories and unattributed names while Remote Control is connected (same page).
license: Proprietary: "© Anthropic PBC. All rights reserved. Use is subject to Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service" (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/LICENSE.md). The relay service is closed and hosted by Anthropic, with no self-hosted option.
lesson_for_parinn:
Keep the local record authoritative and make any sharing layer a dumb, idempotent relay of immutable events, run outside the network-free core. Remote Control's history shows what goes wrong when the server mirror is a mutable transcript and messages have weak delivery guarantees. Its changelog fixes duplicate assistant messages after WebSocket reconnects, work items redelivered after token refresh, messages marked read on arrival and then lost, and local history re-uploaded into a recreated session. When compaction rewrites history it has to archive the server session and start a new one.

For ParleyInn, if it ever shares in real time:
- Ship only sealed, hash-chained, content-addressed append-only events, deduplicated by event ID.
- Acknowledge on consume, not on arrival.
- Represent compaction as a new event, never as a rewrite.
- Run the relay as a separate process (I4), and encrypt events client-side, since Remote Control's server can read everything and is barred for Zero Data Retention orgs.

Copy two Remote Control choices directly: outbound-only connections with short-lived, single-purpose credentials, and treating anything that arrives from a peer as non-authoritative plain text (I2).

name: Claude Managed Agents session events
status: beta
what_is_stored: Event-based session records: user messages, agent responses, tool invocations (bash, file operations, web search, MCP tools, custom tools), session status transitions (running, idle, rescheduled, terminated, deleted), error events, span events for model requests and outcome evaluation, thinking progress signals, tool evaluation metadata with permission policy results. Every event has unique ID (sevt_...) and processed_at timestamp. Sessions are stateful: conversation history, sandbox state, and outputs persist server-side until user deletion.
where_stored: Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure (api.anthropic.com) or user-managed self-hosted sandboxes via worker CLI. Session transcripts persisted in Anthropic's primary data store. NOT eligible for Zero Data Retention (ZDR) — session data retained indefinitely until explicitly deleted by user. NOT eligible for HIPAA Business Associate Agreement (BAA) coverage because statefulness requires persistent retention incompatible with HIPAA's more restrictive requirements.
format_and_model: JSON event objects with domain.action naming convention: user.*, agent.*, session.*, span.*, system.*, stream-only event_start/event_delta. Core schema: {id: 'sevt_...', type: 'domain.action', processed_at: RFC3339 timestamp}. Content blocks with type (text, image, document, redacted), streamed via Server-Sent Events (SSE). Optional event_deltas for incremental preview: event_start → event_delta(s) → full event. Stop reasons (end_turn, requires_action, interrupted) classify session.status_idle. Tool evaluation metadata includes evaluated_permission and evaluation.type.
multi_writer_and_merge: Single-writer by design: one session instance at a time, sequential event ordering enforced by processed_at timestamp. No multi-agent writes to same session in primary flow (multiagent orchestration uses separate threads, each sequential). User sends events (user.message, user.interrupt, user.tool_confirmation), agent responds with tool_use/tool_result pairs. Tool results immediately processed (processed_at populated immediately). No explicit merge/conflict resolution: linear event history, deduplication on reconnection by ID matching.
realtime: Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream: client opens stream before sending events to avoid race conditions. Events delivered as processed_at is populated. Reconnection pattern: new stream opened (buffers future), list all history (get past events), deduplicate by ID to merge streams. Event deltas enable incremental text rendering: event_start signals pending event, event_delta(s) deliver preview text, final agent.message event replaces preview. Deltas best-effort (shed under load). Heartbeats in span.outcome_evaluation_ongoing during long evaluations.
search_retrieval: Pull-only via list endpoint: client.beta.sessions.events.list(session_id) with optional type filter. Returns paginated event objects in sequential order. No server-side search; no full-text indexing mentioned. Filtering supports event type parameter (e.g., ['agent.tool_use', 'agent.tool_result']). Retrieval always exhaustive: client responsible for pagination and deduplication if streams interrupted.
links_sessions_to_code: Agent tool_use events capture invoked bash commands, file operation inputs, web search queries, MCP tool calls with inputs. agent.tool_result events carry stdout/stderr and return values. Tool evaluation metadata shows permission policy result (always_ask, approve, deny). Files operations include read/write/edit/glob/grep with content returned in events. Web operations return fetched content. No automatic linkage to repositories; code tracing requires client-side aggregation of bash events and file operations. MCP connector enables external tools (e.g., git integrations) but not built-in.
privacy_security: Session transcripts stored server-side, persisted until user deletion. No automatic expiration; user must call delete endpoint. Data NOT eligible for ZDR (immediate deletion) or HIPAA BAA (implies incompatibility with persistent statefulness). Redacted content blocks appear for model-policy-withheld content (type: 'redacted'). Tool calls gated by permission policies (evaluated_permission visible). No mention of encryption at rest or in transit (standard TLS assumed). Token usage tracked and returned in span.model_request_end. Secrets in tool inputs are visible in events (no built-in redaction). Model requests cached separately from session content under prompt caching. Span events allow audit trail of model calls and outcome evaluation cycles.
lesson_for_parinn: Claude Managed Agents demonstrates a working event-driven session model with append-only semantics (events never modified, only created) and unique IDs + timestamps. However, server-side persistence creates a critical trust boundary: Anthropic retains and controls the authoritative record, contrary to ParleyInn's invariant I2 (no automatic path from untrusted content to model) and I4 (never talks to network). ParleyInn's self-kept, hash-chained record avoids vendor lock-in and enables offline verification. Strengths to reuse: event ID + processed_at timestamp pattern, SSE streaming for real-time feedback, event_delta preview mechanism for incremental rendering, reconnection deduplication by ID. Tool evaluation metadata with permission results aligns with ParleyInn's I6 (audit every dropped/rejected operation). For high-security contexts or open-source multi-agent networks, self-hosted ParleyInn record is preferable to managed service.

name: Claude Squad (smtg-ai/claude-squad)
status: shipped. Active, not archived. Latest tag is v1.0.20 (from `git ls-remote --tags`). The HEAD commit "Bump version to 1.0.20" is dated 2026-08-20. The repo page shows about 8.6k stars and 625 forks. https://github.com/smtg-ai/claude-squad
what_is_stored:
Claude Squad stores no session history: no transcripts, no prompts and no tool calls. It keeps four things.
(1) config.json holds default_program, auto_yes, daemon_poll_interval, branch_prefix (defaults to "<username>/") and a profiles list of {name, program} (config/config.go).
(2) state.json holds a help_screens_seen bitmask and an "instances" array. Each entry has title, path, branch, status (Running/Ready/Loading/Paused), height and width, created_at, updated_at, auto_yes and program. It also has a worktree object {repo_path, worktree_path, session_name, branch_name, base_commit_sha, is_existing_branch} and diff_stats {added, removed, content}. content is the full text of the current diff against the base commit (session/storage.go, session/instance.go).
(3) One git worktree per instance holds the agent's actual code changes on a branch.
(4) A daemon PID file, and a debug log at $TMPDIR/claudesquad.log (log/log.go).
The agent's conversation lives only in Claude Code's own files and in the live tmux pane. The scrollback limit is set to 10000 lines (session/tmux/tmux.go), and that buffer is lost when the session is killed. Claude Squad itself does not keep the prompt that `N` and SendPrompt send. It is only typed into tmux.
where_stored: All local. State files are under ~/.claude-squad/ (config.json, state.json, the PID file). Worktrees are under ~/.claude-squad/worktrees/<sanitized-branch>_<hex-nanotime>, outside the repo. Branches live in the user's repo (refs/heads/<prefix><title>). The log is in os.TempDir(). There is no server, no database and no custom refs. Code reaches a remote only when the user presses `s`. That runs `git add .`, `git commit --no-verify`, then `gh repo sync --source -b <branch>`, falling back to `git push -u origin <branch>` (session/git/worktree_git.go).
format_and_model: The state is plain JSON and is rewritten whole on every save: MarshalIndent, then os.WriteFile. There is no temp-file-and-rename and no fsync. The instances array is embedded in state.json as a json.RawMessage. Instances are keyed by their user-chosen title, and UpdateInstance and DeleteInstance match on title. The model is mutable snapshot state, the opposite of append-only. Nothing is versioned and there is no hash chain. A parse failure silently falls back to the default empty state, which loses the instance list (config/state.go LoadState). The code model is plain git: a branch per session, a recorded base_commit_sha, and diffs computed against that base. Pausing commits the worktree as "[claudesquad] update from '<title>' on <RFC822 time> (paused)", removes the worktree and keeps the branch (session/instance.go). Pushing commits with the same message without "(paused)" (app/app.go).
multi_writer_and_merge: For code, isolation is the whole design. Each agent writes to its own worktree and branch, so agents never conflict while they run, and the README says "Each task gets its own isolated git workspace, so no conflicts". Merging is left entirely to the human through normal git and GitHub PRs. Claude Squad does no merging or conflict resolution. For its own state there is one writer per machine at a time, with no lock. The TUI kills the background daemon on startup, and the daemon is relaunched when the TUI exits (main.go, daemon/daemon.go: "It's expected that the main process kills the daemon when the main process starts"). Both rewrite state.json whole, so two concurrent `cs` processes would overwrite each other's saves. Nothing syncs across machines.
realtime: Local only. The TUI and the AutoYes daemon poll each tmux pane with `tmux capture-pane`. The poll interval is daemon_poll_interval, 1000 ms by default. They SHA-256-hash the pane content to detect changes and spot prompts, and auto-press Enter in AutoYes mode (session/tmux/tmux.go, daemon/daemon.go). Changes do not stream anywhere else. Nothing is shared between machines or users.
search_retrieval: None over history. The TUI shows a live pane preview and a diff tab. The branch picker runs `git fetch --prune` and `git branch -a --sort=-committerdate` and filters branch names (session/git/worktree_git.go). There is no full-text search over transcripts or prompts, and no way to look back at past sessions.
links_sessions_to_code: Only weakly. A session maps 1:1 to a branch and worktree, and state.json records the base_commit_sha. Commits carry the session title and a timestamp in the message ("[claudesquad] update from '<title>' ..."). Prompts, transcript ids and Claude Code session ids are not recorded, in commits or anywhere else. When a session is killed its state.json entry is deleted and the branch is removed unless it already existed (session/git/worktree_ops.go Cleanup), so the link disappears with it.
scale: The project makes no scale claims. The design is single-user and single-machine with a handful of concurrent tmux sessions. Every save rewrites the whole instance list, including each session's full diff text, so the file grows with the size of the diffs. That scaling note is inferred from session/storage.go, not something the project states.
privacy_security:
There is no redaction, no encryption and no secret handling.
- state.json and config.json are written 0644 in a 0755 directory, readable by every local user, and state.json holds full diff content. The log file is opened 0666 in the shared temp dir (config/state.go, log/log.go).
- Both the pause commit and the push commit pass `--no-verify`, which skips pre-commit hooks such as secret scanners. `git add .` then stages everything not ignored and can push it (session/git/worktree_git.go).
- The experimental `-y/--autoyes` mode auto-accepts agent permission prompts by sending Enter to tmux (README; daemon/daemon.go).
- At startup it runs `$SHELL -c "source ~/.zshrc; which claude"` to find the binary (config/config.go).
- The network is reached through gh and git when pushing or fetching.
- The license is AGPL-3.0 with a CLA (LICENSE.md, CLA.md), so ParleyInn could not reuse its code.
lesson_for_parinn: Git branches are a good way to isolate code, but Claude Squad shows that branches alone do not keep session history. Its history amounts to a branch name, a base SHA and a commit message with a title. The prompts and the transcript are thrown away when a tmux session dies, and the state is a mutable JSON snapshot that resets to empty if it ever fails to parse. ParleyInn should key its record by repo and worktree path, branch and base commit, because that is how orchestrators like this create sessions: one worktree each, under ~/.claude-squad/worktrees. Then a ParleyInn record can be joined to the branch that an orchestrator later commits and pushes. The session history itself should stay in ParleyInn's append-only, hash-chained store, not in commits. One trap to design for: orchestrators commit with --no-verify and `git add .`. If ParleyInn ever puts session data in the working tree, or relies on git hooks to redact or gate it, these tools will skip the hooks and push that data anyway. So redaction has to happen in ParleyInn's own write path, and nothing has to depend on hook enforcement.

name: claude-code-log (daaain/claude-code-log)
category: session viewer/exporter (single-user, local, read-side projection of Claude Code JSONL; now also a local archive, search server and live watcher)
status: shipped. Active: v1.6.0 released 2026-08-31 per CHANGELOG, the same version is on PyPI, and the last commit on main is 2026-10-02 (https://github.com/daaain/claude-code-log/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md, https://pypi.org/project/claude-code-log/). Not archived.
what_is_stored:
It does not record sessions itself. It reads the JSONL transcripts Claude Code already writes under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/, including subagent files at <session>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl. From these it derives three things:
(1) Rendered HTML: an index.html, combined_transcripts.html per project, and session-<id>.html per session. Markdown session-<id>.md is made on demand or with --format md.
(2) A SQLite cache, claude-code-log-cache.db. It holds project, session and file aggregates (token totals, summaries, ai-titles, cwd, first user message) and every parsed message, normalised into columns (uuid, parent_uuid, session_id, cwd, version, ...). The full entry is kept as a zlib-compressed JSON BLOB.
(3) A contentless SQLite FTS5 index over extracted text, thinking, tool_input, tool_result, attachment and meta fields.
Sources: README (https://github.com/daaain/claude-code-log/blob/main/README.md), claude_code_log/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql, and the claude_code_log/search.py module docstring.
The cache keeps sessions whose source JSONL has been deleted, by Claude Code's cleanupPeriodDays (30-day default) or by a TUI "archive" action, so they can be restored. That makes the cache a de facto long-term archive (https://github.com/daaain/claude-code-log/blob/main/docs/restoring-archived-sessions.md).
where_stored:
Local disk only, written next to the source:
- HTML and Markdown go into ~/.claude/projects/ and its per-project subdirectories (README).
- The cache is ~/.claude/projects/claude-code-log-cache.db, plus -wal and -shm files (cache.py get_cache_db_path).
- Output can go elsewhere with -o, for example an Obsidian vault (docs/live-updates.md).
There is no cloud, server-side or git storage.
format_and_model:
Input is Claude Code's JSONL entry stream. Entry types include user, assistant, summary, system, attachment, queue-operation and ai-title. The tool parses them with Pydantic models (claude_code_log/models.py). Experimental providers parse Codex CLI (beta) and Antigravity/agy (alpha) transcripts (README note).

Ordering is DAG-based, not timestamp-based:
- Entries are linked through parentUuid -> uuid edges.
- Subagent roots are re-parented onto the Task/Agent tool_use that spawned them.
- When a resumed session replays prefix messages into a new file, the copies are deduplicated by uuid. The instance from the earliest session wins (dev-docs/dag.md, claude_code_log/dag.py).

The cache is SQLite with 14 numbered SQL migrations (claude_code_log/migrations/). Invalidation compares file mtime and size (migration 011). An incremental refresh is accepted only if the old SHA-256 row fingerprints are an exact prefix of the new ones, which is an append-only check (cache.py CachedFileState).

Output is HTML (escaped via html.escape, with a URL sanitiser in html/utils.py) or GitHub-flavoured Markdown. Detail levels run full/high/low/minimal/user-only, and --compact is aimed at feeding history back to an LLM (README).
multi_writer_and_merge:
Not applicable as a sync system. It is a single-user, single-machine reader with no notion of replicas, machines or merging between users.
- The only writer of the source is Claude Code itself.
- Within one machine, duplicate entries across resumed sessions are reconciled by uuid deduplication (dev-docs/dag.md).
- Concurrent access to the SQLite cache is handled with WAL plus per-thread connection leases (cache.py).
- "merge git worktree directories" is still an open TODO in the README, so worktrees of one repo show up as separate projects (https://github.com/daaain/claude-code-log/blob/main/README.md).
realtime:
Local only.
- `claude-code-log watch` polls with scandir: 0.25 s poll, 0.3 s debounce quiet period, 2 s maximum latency. It re-converts only the session that changed. Polling was chosen over inotify/FSEvents to avoid a dependency and to work on network filesystems (claude_code_log/watch.py).
- `serve --watch` makes an open session page grow "roughly a second behind the CLI". The page sends HEAD requests with an X-Content-Revision header and keeps scroll position and folded sections (docs/live-updates.md, claude_code_log/server.py).
- Nothing is shared between machines or users.
search_retrieval:
There are three layers (docs/archive-search.md):
(1) In-page substring or regex search, which works from file://.
(2) Index-page search over titles and first messages.
(3) Full-archive search through `claude-code-log serve` at http://127.0.0.1:8010/search.html.

Archive search uses a contentless SQLite FTS5 index:
- Matching is token-prefix by default, with quoted exact words and phrases.
- Snippets are rebuilt in Python from the zlib BLOBs, because snippet() returns NULL on contentless tables.
- Base64 image payloads are kept out of the index on purpose (search.py docstring).
- Retrieval for LLMs is pull-based: export Markdown with --detail low --format md --compact (README).
- The TUI can resume a session with `claude -r <id>`, and can restore a deleted JSONL from the cache.

There is no semantic or vector search.
links_sessions_to_code:
Weakly, and only for display:
- The session's cwd and Claude Code's gitBranch field are parsed and shown (models.py; sessions.cwd in the schema).
- SHA-shaped tokens in transcript prose become commit links, but only when the SHA is reachable from a local remote-tracking ref. This is checked with one `git rev-list --remotes` per working directory, never `git ls-remote`, so no network call is made. Hosts covered are github.com, gitlab.com and bitbucket.org, plus a --git-link template for self-hosted Gitea, Forgejo or GitLab. Local-only commits stay plain text (README "Linking Commit SHAs"; claude_code_log/git_remote.py).

Nothing is written into git: no notes, refs or commit trailers, and no mapping from session to commit.
scale:
Claims come from the code docstrings (claude_code_log/search.py, server.py, entry_store.py):
- A real cache of 1.29 GB. The contentless FTS index adds 253 MB (+20%), against 1,080 MB (+84%) for a content-stored index. Letting base64 into the index would grow it 28%.
- A project-filtered search takes 2.4 ms with a forced CROSS JOIN versus 2,012 ms without it.
- Session pages reach 27 MB.
- A watch tick on a 39.7 MB session file took about 1.1 s before entry reuse.
These are author measurements and have not been independently verified. The discovery note's star count (1.2k) could not be confirmed, because the anonymous GitHub API returned no data in this session.
privacy_security:
There is no redaction, secret scanning or encryption for Claude transcripts. The cache and the HTML hold the full plaintext of prompts, tool inputs and results, and thinking. They are written next to the source in ~/.claude/projects with default file permissions.

The only redaction-like code is in the Codex provider. It replaces opaque Fernet-token payloads with "[opaque payload redacted]", and that is a rendering cleanup, not secret protection (claude_code_log/providers/codex_tools.py).

Hardening that does exist:
- Rendered content is HTML-escaped and URLs are sanitised (html/utils.py).
- The `serve` server binds to 127.0.0.1 by default and validates the Host header against loopback names to block DNS rebinding. The source states that the read side "already exposes every transcript in the archive" (claude_code_log/server.py).
- There is no authentication on the local server.
- Codex `exec` snippets run in a sandboxed QuickJS engine (CHANGELOG 1.6.0).

Two related observations:
- The TUI "archive" action deletes the source JSONL and keeps the data only in the cache (docs/restoring-archived-sessions.md).
- Exported Markdown meant to be fed back to an LLM is not enveloped or marked untrusted (README).
lesson_for_parinn:
Treat the agent's native JSONL as an input to ingest, and keep ParleyInn's record separate from it, because the native file is neither append-only nor durable:
- Claude Code deletes transcripts after 30 days by default.
- Resumed sessions replay earlier messages under the same uuid with a new sessionId.
- Subagent files have parentUuid null at their root.

claude-code-log copes with this through three techniques that ParleyInn's projection layer should copy:
1. A uuid DAG with earliest-session deduplication and subagent re-parenting.
2. An incremental-ingest guard that accepts new data only when the old row fingerprints are an exact prefix of the new ones. This detects append-only violations, which is the same idea as ParleyInn's hash chain.
3. A contentless FTS5 index that keeps base64 out, giving full-text recall at about 20% overhead without a second plaintext copy.

claude-code-log also shows what ParleyInn must not do:
- It keeps unredacted, unencrypted plaintext in a SQLite file inside ~/.claude.
- It serves the whole archive over unauthenticated loopback HTTP.
- It exports history as raw Markdown "to feed back to an LLM" with no untrusted-content envelope. That is exactly the injection channel that ParleyInn's I2 rules out.

A smaller point: its commit linking checks SHAs against local remote-tracking refs instead of calling ls-remote. That keeps code linkage network-free, which fits I4.
