name: claude-code-sync (perfectra1n)
status: shipped
license: MIT (Cargo.toml license field and LICENSE file: https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/Cargo.toml)
what_is_stored: Claude Code transcripts: every ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-path>/*.jsonl file. That covers the main session file (<uuid>.jsonl) and each subagent sidechain (agent-<hash>.jsonl). The filename stem is the identity, because subagent files carry their parent's sessionId (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/src/parser.rs). It also stores "attachments": non-.jsonl files under projects/, such as images, PDFs and per-project memory/ dirs. --exclude-attachments turns these off. Optional per-category "artifacts" can also be synced: settings.json and keybindings.json, ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, skills/, agents/, commands/, rules/, hooks/ (executable), plugin manifests only, plans/, todos/, and ~/.claude/history.jsonl. All are off for existing configs; the wizard pre-selects all of them except hooks (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/README.md#artifact-sync). It never syncs Claude Code's file-history/ code checkpoints, session-env/, shell-snapshots/, sessions/, caches or credentials (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/src/artifacts/denylist.rs). The tool keeps local metadata outside the repo: ~/.claude-code-sync.toml (config), plus state.json, operation-history.json (last 5 ops), snapshots/ for undo and latest-conflict-report.json, all under ~/.claude-code-sync/. A per-machine deletion record lives at ~/.claude/.claude-code-sync-tracked.json (README "Sync State" and "Deletions that actually propagate").
where_stored: Working-tree files in a separate git repository the user chooses: a local directory with an optional remote (GitHub, any git URL). Mercurial is an alternative backend, and Git LFS is optional (default pattern *.jsonl). Repo layout: .gitignore (managed guard block), .gitattributes, projects/<encoded-path or mapped id>/<session>.jsonl, and artifacts/<category>/. The projects subdirectory can be renamed with sync_subdirectory (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/README.md#sync-repository-layout). Git and hg run as CLI subprocesses, not libraries, so the user's hooks, LFS and credential helpers apply (README "Dependencies" note; https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/src/scm/git.rs). Nothing is put in git notes or custom refs. It does not sit in the code project's own repo.
format_and_model: Transcripts are copied byte for byte. Claude Code's JSONL is kept as is: one event per line with type, uuid, parentUuid, sessionId, timestamp, cwd, gitBranch, message and isSidechain, and unknown fields survive through a serde flatten. Each copy is cut back to the byte offset just past the last fully parsed message, so a line Claude Code is still appending is never copied half-written; it travels on the next sync (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/src/parser.rs). Change detection uses a pinned FNV-1a 64-bit "content hash" (16 hex digits) over the re-serialized entries. It is a cheap equality test, not an integrity or tamper check (parser.rs). Each push makes one commit, by default "Sync N sessions at <UTC time>" (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/src/sync/push.rs). In settings and plugin files, machine paths are replaced with __HOME__ / __CLAUDE_DIR__ placeholders (README "Machine-neutral paths"). A project map stores a project under a stable id and lets each machine map that id to its own absolute path (README "Project map"). There is no event schema of its own: the data model is Claude Code's message tree (uuid/parentUuid) plus git history.
multi_writer_and_merge: Merging happens in two layers. (1) Git layer: pull runs `git fetch` and then `git merge --no-edit FETCH_HEAD`. It merges rather than rebases, because undo records point at commit hashes. A real conflict triggers `merge --abort` and the pull stops (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/src/scm/git.rs). .gitattributes sets `*.jsonl merge=union` and `MEMORY.md merge=union`, so two machines appending to the same file do not stop git. Lines from both sides are kept "in no meaningful order" and put back in order later (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/src/scm/attributes.rs). (2) Application layer: each local transcript is paired with its repo copy by path, never by interior sessionId. Any content-hash difference counts as a "conflict", even a pure append, because there is no common base or ancestor (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/src/conflict.rs). The default resolution is "smart merge" (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/src/merge.rs). It takes the union of entries keyed by uuid and rebuilds the parentUuid tree, keeping divergent branches. If one uuid has different content on the two sides, the newer timestamp wins (last-writer-wins). Entries without a uuid are merged by timestamp. Everything is then sorted by timestamp, re-serialized and written over the local ~/.claude/projects transcript, so the result is not byte-identical to either input. If smart merge fails, the user gets an interactive TUI (smart merge, keep local, keep remote, keep both). Non-interactive runs keep the local file and save the remote as <id>-conflict-<timestamp>.jsonl, with a JSON/Markdown conflict report (README "Conflict Resolution"). On push, the local file overwrites the repo copy; `sync` runs pull and then push. history.jsonl is a grow-only union on both push and pull, deduplicated on (timestamp, project, display) (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/src/artifacts/union_jsonl.rs). Other artifacts are remote-wins on pull, with a snapshot taken first. Deletions of skills, agents, commands, rules and hooks propagate through a per-machine tracked record with guards against fresh-machine wipes (README). `undo push` is `git reset --soft` and tells the user to force-push by hand (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/src/undo/operations.rs).
realtime: None. Sync happens only when someone runs `sync`, `push` or `pull`. The docs suggest cron jobs and a systemd pre-shutdown unit (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/docs/EXAMPLES.md#automated-workflows; README "Automated Backup (Cron)"). I found no daemon, file watcher or Claude Code hook integration in the source (a grep for SessionStart, SessionEnd, watch and notify returned nothing). Live sessions are handled by trimming each copy to the last complete message.
search_retrieval: None beyond plain git and the filesystem. The CLI offers `status` (--show-files, --show-conflicts), `report` (conflicts as JSON, Markdown or text) and `history list|last` (the last 5 sync operations) (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/README.md#commands). It has no index, full-text search or recall API. Claude Code reads the synced transcripts back natively, for example to resume a session on another machine.
links_sessions_to_code: No. Transcripts live in a dedicated sync repo, apart from the code repos they describe, and nothing links a session to a commit in the project repo. The cwd and gitBranch fields Claude Code writes into each line are carried through untouched. The tool uses cwd only to name projects, and its project map ties a project id to a per-machine checkout path (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/src/parser.rs; README "Project map"). Claude Code's file-history/ code checkpoints are explicitly denylisted (denylist.rs).
scale: No formal scale claims or benchmarks. Code comments say summarizing 12k transcripts took 20 s on one core, which is why the work runs in parallel with rayon (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/Cargo.toml). Discovery streams files and keeps only summaries, because "a few gigabytes of history" would otherwise need tens of GB of RAM (parser.rs). Issue #70 (closed 2026-05-27) reported a stack overflow at about 2,078 local and 2,353 remote sessions with about 1,089 conflicts per pull; it was fixed by making tree building and flattening iterative (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/issues/70). Defaults include max_file_size_bytes = 10 MB, and Git LFS is optional for *.jsonl (README "Configuration File"). Adoption as of 2026-10-02 (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync): 97 stars, 19 forks, 171 commits on main, not archived. The latest release, v0.4.0, is dated 2026-09-24 (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). The discovery note's 2026-09-29 push date could not be checked: the unauthenticated API call failed, and the newest commit in my clone is dated 2026-09-24.
privacy_security: Path-based secrets guard only. A hardcoded denylist is applied on every copy in both directions and cannot be overridden. It covers .credentials.json, settings.local.json, .claude.json, stats-cache.json, mcp-needs-auth-cache.json, *.pem, *.key, .env*, daemon*, and any path containing shell-snapshots, session-env, file-history, paste-cache, cache, debug, statsig, backups or sessions. Non-UTF-8 path components are refused. On pull, absolute paths and paths with `..` are refused, so a "poisoned sync repo" cannot plant denied files or escape ~/.claude (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/src/artifacts/denylist.rs). Every push also maintains a managed .gitignore or .hgignore guard block as a second layer. There is NO redaction of transcript contents: files are copied verbatim, so secrets pasted into prompts or shown in tool output end up in git history. A grep for redact, scrub, encrypt and sanitize found nothing. There is no encryption at rest or in transit beyond git's own transport; the README only advises "use private git repositories" and "consider encrypting the git repository" (https://github.com/perfectra1n/claude-code-sync/blob/main/README.md#security-considerations). The hooks category syncs executable code, and the README warns to enable it only for a repo you control. Only the exec bit travels, it is only ever granted, and an interactive pull asks before setting it (README "Artifact Sync"). Purge removes old transcripts from the machine and the repo, but the data stays in git history until that history is rewritten (README "Purging old transcripts"). The binary makes network calls: git push/pull plus `self-update`, which downloads release assets over rustls and checks SHA-256 (README "self-update"; Cargo.toml ureq).
lesson_for_parinn: This project shows that git can carry append-only agent JSONL between machines without textual conflicts: `merge=union` plus rebuilding the uuid/parentUuid tree is enough. It also shows what happens when the sync format is a mutable per-session file with no common base. Every append looks like a conflict. Same-uuid edits are settled by last-writer-wins on timestamp, and merged transcripts are re-serialized and rewritten in place, so history is not lossless and could not hold a hash chain. Also, a path denylist does nothing about secrets inside the content. If ParleyInn uses git as a transport, it should commit immutable, content-addressed, per-writer segment files (one writer per path, never rewritten). Git merges then reduce to disjoint additions, hash chains verify byte for byte, and ordering comes from the record's own causal links, not wall-clock timestamps. Redaction must happen before a segment leaves the machine. ParleyInn should adopt this tool's "poisoned sync repo" stance on pull (refuse traversal and denied paths, never auto-execute) as a baseline. Recalled content should stay untrusted no matter which remote it came from.

name: claude-code-tools / aichat
status: shipped
what_is_stored: Session conversation history (JSONL format) with metadata: session IDs, agent type (Claude/Codex), project path, git branch, working directory, timestamps, first/last messages, custom titles, session derivation type, and full-text searchable conversation content. Tantivy-based search index tracking which files have been indexed and their modification state for incremental updates.
where_stored: Local filesystem: session files in ~/.claude/projects/<project-path>/ (Claude Code) and ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/ (Codex). Search index in ~/.claude/.aichat/index/ or ~/.codex/.aichat/index/ (Tantivy index directory with VERSION file and index_state.json for tracking).
format_and_model: JSONL (JSON Lines) per session file; each line is one JSON object. Metadata in first line carries continue_metadata block: {"parent_session_file": "path", "parent_session_id": "id", "continued_at": "timestamp"}. Tantivy schema defines searchable fields (content), stored metadata fields (session_id, agent, project, branch, cwd, modified_ts, custom_title, is_sidechain, is_exec_run), and fast fields for sorting. Data model: session graph where each session points to its parent via continue_metadata, forming a linked list (abc123 <- def456 <- ghi789 <- jkl012).
multi_writer_and_merge: Single active writer per session (native Claude Code or Codex agent). Multi-agent workflows enabled via session lineage: parent-child relationships tracked in continue_metadata. No merge conflict resolution needed; new sessions (rollover/trim) create fresh children pointing back to parent. Session porting (Codex ↔ Claude) creates new native sessions with full history accessible via lineage chain. No concurrent write conflicts; each session is append-only while active.
realtime: Sessions are live: agents write JSONL lines as messages are exchanged. Indexing is on-demand (incremental): `aichat search` and `aichat resume` auto-index sessions on every command run, checking file modification time and size to skip unchanged files. Index rebuilds when package version or indexing-logic revision changes. No real-time push updates; queries are pull-based (user triggers search/resume).
search_retrieval: Full-text search via Tantivy (Rust library). Schema includes: searchable content field (conversation text), stored metadata (session_id, agent, project, branch, cwd, custom_title, derivation_type). Fast fields for sorting by modification_ts (epoch milliseconds). Incremental indexing: tracks mtime+size in index_state.json; only re-indexes modified files. Search returns: session_id, agent, project, snippet, score, export_path. Results can be filtered by is_sidechain, is_exec_run, claude_home. Index version tracked; auto-rebuild on package upgrade.
links_sessions_to_code: Yes. Sessions store: project (path mapped from ~/.claude/projects/<path-hash>/), branch (git branch if available), cwd (working directory at session start), file_path (JSONL file location). Session metadata extracted from session_meta records includes environment info. Tool calls indexed (flattened to text during Codex→Claude porting). Session lineage (parent_session_file path) allows traversing full history. Searcher can find sessions by project, branch, cwd substring. Rollover sessions auto-inject lineage list into first user message: [SESSION LINEAGE] with chronological ancestor file paths.
scale: Tested on ~13.6k session files (2-30s indexing time, varies on backlog). Incremental indexing after initial build is fast (skips unchanged files). Search queries executed via Tantivy queries (no figures given for query latency). Session porting and lineage traversal are linear in ancestor chain length. No explicit claims about limit; implies thousands of sessions per home are viable.
privacy_security: Local-only storage: no network calls from aichat. Codex encrypted_content fields are stripped during session porting (Codex → Claude conversion) to prevent encrypted content leakage. Session files contain full conversation history including user input; no automatic redaction. Lineage pointers are file paths (absolute paths stored); accessible to any reader with filesystem access. No encryption at rest; sessions in ~/.claude and ~/.codex are readable plaintext. Export format (with YAML front matter) stores same content as JSONL.
lesson_for_parinn: Use lightweight file-based lineage chains with parent pointers rather than deep copying history: continue_metadata block (parent_session_file, parent_session_id, continued_at timestamp) is sufficient for traversal. Incremental search indexing with state tracking (mtime+size) scales to thousands of sessions without full re-indexing. Metadata extraction on-demand (no separate DB) keeps storage model simple. For multi-agent scenarios, session porting shows how to flatten and re-structure content across formats while preserving history chain. Version-controlled indexing logic (INDEX_LOGIC_REVISION) avoids stale index bugs on code changes. Consider: ParleyInn's append-only, hash-chained guarantee is stronger than aichat's file-based pointers (not cryptographically verified); aichat's local-only design avoids network risk, but ParleyInn's untrusted-content handling post-recall should apply to sessions from portable/shared storage.

name: claude-code-transcripts (Simon Willison)
category: exporter + gist share (one-way, read-only renderer of Claude Code session logs)
status: shipped (v0.6, 2026-01-24; latest commit 2026-02-12 notes the `web` commands are broken; not archived, but no release since; effectively in maintenance)
what_is_stored: The tool keeps no store of its own. It reads Claude Code session logs and writes static HTML. Its inputs are local JSONL from ~/.claude/projects, JSON from Claude Code for web (fetched through undocumented Anthropic endpoints, currently broken), or a JSON/JSONL file given by path or URL. It writes index.html, a timeline of prompts and detected git commits, plus page-001.html and onward at 5 prompts per page (PROMPTS_PER_PAGE = 5 in src/claude_code_transcripts/__init__.py). The `all` command adds a master index and per-project indexes. With --json it also copies the original session file next to the HTML. Subagent files (agent-*.jsonl) are skipped by default; `all --include-agents` keeps them. Sources: README https://github.com/simonw/claude-code-transcripts/blob/main/README.md ; code https://github.com/simonw/claude-code-transcripts/blob/main/src/claude_code_transcripts/__init__.py
where_stored: Output goes to a local directory: a temp dir by default, `-o DIR`, or ./claude-archive for `all`. With --gist it also goes to a GitHub Gist, created by shelling out to `gh gist create` with the HTML files only. That gist is secret by default, since `create_gist(output)` is called without public=True. Viewers open it through the third-party static renderer gisthost.github.io/?GIST_ID/index.html; gistpreview.github.io is still supported, and the Dec 2025 blog post names gistpreview. A gist is itself a git repository, but the tool never uses git semantics such as history, branches or merges. It treats the gist as a one-shot file upload. Sources: README "Publishing to GitHub Gist" section; create_gist() in __init__.py; https://simonwillison.net/2025/Dec/25/claude-code-transcripts/
format_and_model: Input is Claude Code's native JSONL, one JSON object per line with types user, assistant and summary, and content blocks text, thinking, tool_use and tool_result. Output is Jinja2-rendered HTML (templates base/index/page/macros/master_index/project_index.html plus search.js) with inline CSS and JS. Markdown in prompts, assistant text and thinking is rendered with Python-Markdown (fenced_code and tables extensions). The model is session → conversation turns (each user prompt with its assistant/tool responses) → pages. There is no schema of its own, no IDs beyond Claude Code's session id, and no hashing or integrity data. Written in Python 3.10+ (click, jinja2, markdown, httpx, questionary) under Apache-2.0. Sources: https://github.com/simonw/claude-code-transcripts/blob/main/pyproject.toml ; __init__.py
multi_writer_and_merge: Not applicable. It is a single-user, one-shot exporter. Each run writes a fresh directory or a new gist. Nothing is appended, deduplicated, merged or reconciled across machines or agents, and re-exporting a session that grew creates a new gist rather than updating the old one. The `all` command just re-renders every JSONL under one ~/.claude/projects tree. Source: README; create_gist() always calls `gh gist create`, never `gh gist edit`.
realtime: None. Export is manual and batch, run by hand on a finished or in-progress session file. There is no watch mode, no hooks and no streaming. Source: README command list (local, web, json, all).
search_retrieval: Search is a client-side, progressive-enhancement box in the generated index (templates/search.js). It fetches every page-NNN.html and highlights substring matches. On gisthost it first calls https://api.github.com/gists/{id} to find the file URLs. It is turned off under file:// because of CORS. The CLI picker lists the 10 most recent local sessions by mtime (--limit), using the JSONL `summary` entry or the first user message as the title. The web picker groups sessions by GitHub repo and can filter with --repo. There is no index, no FTS and no cross-session query. Sources: templates/search.js and find_local_sessions() in the repo; README "Local sessions" and "Web sessions".
links_sessions_to_code: The link runs one way, from session to code, and comes from scraping. A regex, COMMIT_PATTERN `\[[\w\-/]+ ([a-f0-9]{7,})\] (.+?)`, finds `git commit` output inside tool_result text. Matches become commit cards in the index timeline and in the pages. The GitHub repo for the commit URLs is auto-detected by regex from `git push` output (github.com/owner/repo/pull/new/branch), set with --repo, or taken from web-session metadata. Nothing is written back into git: no trailers, notes or refs. The reverse link, commit to session, is a manual habit. Willison pastes the gist/preview transcript URL into his commit messages, and the repo's own commit log shows this. Sources: __init__.py (COMMIT_PATTERN, GITHUB_REPO_PATTERN, detect_github_repo); README --repo option; https://simonwillison.net/2025/Dec/25/claude-code-transcripts/
scale: The project makes no scale claims. Its scale handling is pagination at 5 prompts per page and long tool results truncated behind "Show more" in the UI. The blog post gives no usage numbers. PyPI lists releases 0.3–0.6 (https://pypi.org/pypi/claude-code-transcripts/json). I could not get GitHub star counts through this session's API access.
privacy_security: There is no redaction or secret scanning, and no encryption. The whole transcript (prompts, thinking, tool inputs and outputs, file contents, env dumps) is published as-is. The blog post does not discuss privacy (https://simonwillison.net/2025/Dec/25/claude-code-transcripts/). Gists are secret by default, which means unlisted: anyone with the URL can read them. The preview path also sends viewers through a third-party renderer, gisthost.github.io, which loads the content from the GitHub API. For the `web` command, the tool takes the Claude Code OAuth access token from the macOS keychain (`security find-generic-password -s "Claude Code-credentials"`) and the org UUID from ~/.claude.json. It then calls undocumented endpoints, api.anthropic.com/v1/sessions and /v1/session_ingress/session/{id}. Those stopped working when Anthropic changed them; issue #77, opened 2026-02-12, is unresolved (https://github.com/simonw/claude-code-transcripts/issues/77). Rendering safety: Jinja2 autoescape is on, and tool results are passed through html.escape. Prompts, assistant text and thinking, however, go through Python-Markdown and are inserted with |safe (templates/macros.html). I checked locally that Python-Markdown passes raw HTML through: `markdown.markdown('<script>alert(1)</script>')` returns the script tag unchanged. So HTML or JS inside a transcript, for example an injected payload the model echoed into its reply, would run in the viewer's browser on gisthost. That last point is my own analysis of the code. It is not a documented or reported vulnerability.
lesson_for_parinn: Treat sharing as a separate, explicit export step from a trusted record, and never let rendered or shared history be trusted. The tool shows that a git-backed gist plus a static viewer is a cheap and popular way to share a session. It also shows three failure modes ParleyInn has to design out. (1) Rendered transcripts are an injection channel: model text goes to a browser unescaped through Markdown with |safe, the same class of risk as ParleyInn's I2. Any ParleyInn export or viewer should escape everything and add an allow-listed Markdown/HTML sanitizer, and should never mark recalled content as trusted. (2) Publishing the raw transcript with no redaction leaks secrets, so a ParleyInn export should run the same redaction pipeline as ingest and audit what it removed (I6). (3) The tool depends on undocumented vendor APIs and fragile regex scraping (commit detection from `git commit` stdout), and it breaks silently when either changes. ParleyInn should get session-to-commit links from hooks or git trailers it writes itself, not from parsing tool output. Shipping a gist upload in the core would also break I4. Any `--gist`-style sharing belongs in a separate, opt-in tool outside the no-network core.
license: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file and pyproject.toml)

name: claude-code-viewer (d-kimuson), npm package @kimuson/claude-code-viewer
category: session viewer / web client (single-user, self-hosted, local-first)
status: shipped (active, not archived). The latest release is v0.8.2, published to npm on 2026-08-18. Main HEAD 9367cf0 is dated 2026-08-18. The repo shows about 1.3k stars, 164 forks and about 798 commits (GitHub page fetched 2026-10-02). No commits since mid-August, which is about six weeks.
what_is_stored:
It is a viewer and client. It does not own any session history. The source of truth is Claude Code's own transcripts, `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl` (README "Data Source"). Main session files and agent (sub-agent) session files are both watched. The viewer adds only derived or auxiliary state of its own:
(1) A rebuildable SQLite cache. It holds a `projects` table (id, name, path, session_count, dir_mtime_ms, synced_at) and a `sessions` table (id, project_id, file_path, message_count, first_user_message_json, custom_title, total_cost_usd, cost_breakdown_json, token_usage_json, model_name, pr_links_json, file_mtime_ms, last_modified_at, permission_allowlist_json). It also holds a `sync_state` KV table and an FTS5 table `session_messages_fts` (session_id, project_id, role, content, conversation_index).
(2) `schedules.json` for its cron and one-shot message scheduler.
(3) `vapid-keys.json` for Web Push.
(4) A cache directory.
Per-project session options and chat drafts are also persisted. Their exact store was not checked.
The README says outright that it makes no backups: when Claude Code's default 30-day `cleanupPeriodDays` cleanup deletes a JSONL file, that session disappears from the viewer.
where_stored: Session history stays in Claude Code's local files (`~/.claude/projects`, which `--claude-dir` / `CCV_GLOBAL_CLAUDE_DIR` can change). The viewer's own state goes in a sibling directory, `~/.claude-code-viewer/`: `cache.db` (SQLite in WAL mode), `schedules.json`, `vapid-keys.json` and `cache/`. All of it is local disk on the host running the Node server. Nothing goes to git, and there is no cloud or p2p storage.
format_and_model: The input is Claude Code's JSONL, parsed with strict Zod schemas, one per entry type. The types are user, assistant, system, summary, custom-title, ai-title, agent-name, agent-setting, attachment, bridge-session, file-history-snapshot, last-prompt, mode, permission-mode, pr-link, progress and queue-operation. Each entry has a base of uuid, parentUuid (nullable), cwd and an optional gitBranch, so messages form a parent-linked tree inside each file. A line that fails to parse becomes an `x-error` entry instead of being dropped. The README pitches this as "Zero Information Loss: Strict Zod schema validation". The derived model is relational SQLite built with drizzle-orm on node:sqlite, plus an FTS5 trigram index. If a migration fails, the cache DB and its -wal and -shm files are deleted and recreated. The cache is treated as disposable and rebuildable from the JSONL.
multi_writer_and_merge: There is no multi-writer or merge model. The writer is Claude Code: either a CLI process, or a process the viewer spawns through the Claude Agent SDK. Each session has its own append-only JSONL file. The viewer reads those files and syncs its cache by file mtime: new or changed files are re-indexed, and cache rows for deleted files or projects are removed. Multiple machines, users or sandboxes are not handled at all. The README calls the authentication "a simple single-password authentication mechanism without advanced features like multi-user support". It notes that Claude Code's resume creates a new session file with regenerated logs. The only reconciliation is an optional UI setting, "Unify sessions with same title", which shows just the latest session with a given title.
realtime: Yes, but only on one host. A recursive fs.watch on `~/.claude/projects` maps changed paths to session or agent-session ids. It debounces per file for 100 ms, then emits sessionChanged, sessionListChanged and agentSessionChanged on an in-process EventBus. That bus is pushed to the browser over SSE (`/api/sse`). A terminal runs over WebSocket. On mobile, a PWA receives Web Push notifications when a session completes. Remote use goes through Tailscale or a reverse proxy with `--hostname 0.0.0.0 --password`. History is not replicated between machines.
search_retrieval: Full-text search uses SQLite FTS5 with the trigram tokenizer, ranked by BM25. User-message hits get a 1.2x boost. Search can cover one project or all projects. Only user prompt text, assistant text blocks, and custom or AI titles are indexed; tool calls and results are not. The query is wrapped in double quotes to avoid FTS syntax errors. Snippets are about 150 characters taken around the match. Results point back to (sessionId, conversationIndex). There is also in-page find (Ctrl/Cmd+F). In `--api-only` mode, `/api/search` is exposed for tools such as n8n.
links_sessions_to_code: The links are weak and indirect. Each JSONL entry carries `cwd` and an optional `gitBranch`. `pr-link` log entries (PR title, number, URL) are aggregated into `sessions.pr_links_json` and shown as cards. The Explorer panel summarizes the files a session edited and its tool invocations. A built-in Git panel offers diff (with inline comments), commit, `git push origin HEAD` and branch switching, by shelling out to git. The viewer does not record which commit a session produced, and it writes no session metadata into git (no notes, trailers or refs).
scale: No numeric scale claims were found. Scalability work is visible in the code: mtime-based incremental sync, indexes on sessions(project_id) and sessions(file_mtime_ms), and FTS5 instead of an in-memory index. Its own comment says "FTS5 always reads latest data". The design targets one developer's `~/.claude` directory.
privacy_security:
PRIVACY.md claims localhost-only communication, no telemetry, and that only the Anthropic API is contacted, through the Agent SDK. The code also includes the `web-push` library and calls `webpush.sendNotification` for PWA notifications, which go out to browser push services. This is an inference from the code, not stated in PRIVACY.md.
Access control is a single optional password (`--password` / `CCV_PASSWORD`). It is checked with timingSafeEqual, carried in an httpOnly, SameSite=Lax `ccv-session` cookie or a Bearer header, and authentication is fully off if no password is set. Remote exposure relies on infrastructure such as Tailscale, a VPN or an OAuth proxy.
The in-browser terminal is on by default and uses restricted bash flags unless `--terminal-unrestricted` is set. It can be turned off with `--terminal-disabled`. With a password, it is effectively remote shell access.
No redaction, secret scanning or encryption at rest was found, either in the transcripts or in the SQLite cache. A grep for redact, secret or mask in src/server returned nothing. The FTS index therefore stores a plaintext copy of prompt and response text in `~/.claude-code-viewer/cache.db`.
Recalled content is rendered for a human. It can also be resent to Claude through resume or continue, with no prompt-injection treatment.
Since April 2026, chat sending, resume, permission approval and AskUserQuestion are opt-in, because of Anthropic's terms on Agent SDK use with subscription accounts.
lesson_for_parinn:
ParleyInn should keep the authoritative record separate from the derived index, and should not rely on Claude Code's transcripts surviving. The viewer gets two things right. Its SQLite and FTS5 cache can be thrown away and rebuilt from the JSONL. Lines that fail to parse are kept as `x-error` entries instead of being dropped. Both line up with I6 and I10, and ParleyInn should copy them.
It also shows the failure mode ParleyInn exists to fix. Because it only reads `~/.claude/projects`, history vanishes when Claude Code's 30-day cleanup runs. A rebuildable index also quietly becomes a second plaintext copy of every prompt, with no redaction.
So ParleyInn should do three things:
- copy transcripts into its own append-only, hash-chained record before cleanup can delete them
- run redaction before anything is indexed
- treat the FTS index as a derived projection under the same redaction and encryption policy as the record
For real-time display, a per-host file watcher with a short debounce feeding an event stream is enough. It gives no sharing across machines, so the transport question stays open and must be solved by the record format itself.

name: claude-context-sync (Daniel de Oliveira Trindade; VS Code extension "Claude Context Sync" by DaleuStudio)
category: sync-to-git (git or self-hosted HTTP server as a blob transport for whole Claude Code session snapshots)
status: shipped. It is early-stage, has one maintainer and is inactive. Tags v0.1.0, v0.5.2 and v0.6.0 exist, but there are no GitHub Releases (https://github.com/Daniel-de-Oliveira-Trindade/claude-context-sync/releases). The README says the current version is 0.6.0. A shallow clone shows 21 commits, from 2026-02-26 to 2026-03-25 (last commit df88be8). That means no commits for about 6 months as of 2026-10-02. The repo is not archived. GitHub showed 13 stars, 1 fork and 1 open issue (#1, "[WIP] Auto-sync hooks (hooks-install) not working reliably on Windows", https://github.com/Daniel-de-Oliveira-Trindade/claude-context-sync/issues). The VS Code Marketplace lists v0.6.0 with about 115 installs and no ratings (https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=DaleuStudio.claude-context-sync). These figures came through a page summarizer, and the Marketplace "last updated" date it reported could not be verified.
where_stored:
The source is Claude Code's local files under ~/.claude. Three transports exist:
(a) A separate private git repo, not the code repo. It is cloned to ~/.claude-sync-git. Each bundle is a file at {sanitized-project-name}/{sessionId}_{YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS}.bundle[.gz][.enc] on the default branch, committed with the message "sync: session <8-hex> | <project> | <first 50 chars of first prompt>" (git_sync.py push_bundle, lines ~160-207: https://github.com/Daniel-de-Oliveira-Trindade/claude-context-sync/blob/df88be89cf773c5a7b7de96daab87785b815abdf/src/git_sync.py).
(b) An optional self-hosted FastAPI server (v0.6.0). It writes bundles to {SYNC_DATA_DIR}/sessions/{username}/{project}/{file}, keeps users.json (token hashes) and shares.json on the same disk, and can mirror every upload into a backup git repo set by SYNC_GIT_BACKUP_REPO (claude-sync-server/server/storage.py, auth.py, sharing.py, git_backup.py: https://github.com/Daniel-de-Oliveira-Trindade/claude-context-sync/tree/df88be89cf773c5a7b7de96daab87785b815abdf/claude-sync-server/server). When a server URL is set, the CLI uses HTTP and falls back to git.
(c) Manual file transfer of an exported bundle (USB, Drive).
Every push and pull also writes a local backup to ~/.claude-sync-git/backups/{project}/, which is gitignored. Overwritten sessions are backed up to <project-dir>/backups/ inside ~/.claude/projects.
format_and_model:
Each bundle is one JSON document, indented, holding a snapshot of the whole session:
{version:"1.1.0", exportedAt, sourceDevice, session:{sessionId, messages:[raw JSONL records], metadata, fileHistory:{name: text}, todos:[...]}, checksum}
The checksum is an unkeyed SHA-256 over json.dumps(session, sort_keys=True) (exporter.py line 214, verified in importer.validate_bundle).
Optional layers are gzip (`--compress`) and then an AES-256-GCM envelope, Salt(16)||IV(12)||Tag(16)||Ciphertext (crypto.py https://github.com/Daniel-de-Oliveira-Trindade/claude-context-sync/blob/df88be89cf773c5a7b7de96daab87785b815abdf/src/crypto.py).
There are no deltas and no event log. Every push writes a fresh full copy under a new timestamped filename, and nothing ever prunes old copies, so repo size grows with the sum of all snapshot sizes.
Paths are made portable by prefix substitution with ${PROJECTS}, ${HOME}, ${CLAUDE_DIR} and ${USER}. It is applied only to the `cwd` and `projectPath` fields of each record and to the metadata (exporter.py lines 131-139). Paths inside message text, tool inputs or file-history are not rewritten. denormalize() always converts '/' to '\' (path_transformer.py line ~139), so it is Windows-centric; the README itself says "Fully tested on Windows."
On import it rewrites the JSONL into ~/.claude/projects/<encoded cwd>/, re-creating Claude Code's directory naming, and updates sessions-index.json (importer.py https://github.com/Daniel-de-Oliveira-Trindade/claude-context-sync/blob/df88be89cf773c5a7b7de96daab87785b815abdf/src/importer.py).
multi_writer_and_merge:
There is no merge. The README's Limitations section says: "No conflict resolution — use sessions alternately between devices" (https://github.com/Daniel-de-Oliveira-Trindade/claude-context-sync/blob/df88be89cf773c5a7b7de96daab87785b815abdf/README.md).
At the git level, collisions are rare because every push adds a new uniquely timestamped file. The client runs `git pull --rebase`, then `git add`, `git commit` and `git push` (git_sync.py lines 132, 199-205). It does not retry if the push loses a race; the hook just logs an error.
At the session level the policy is last-writer-wins by overwrite. Import always replaces the local JSONL. In `--auto` mode it forces the overwrite (cli.py line 1105, `force=force or auto`; `--all` uses `force or True` at line 963). Even without --force, importer.py lines 343-344 back up the existing file and then overwrite it. The README says this case gives a "Session already exists" error, so code and docs disagree.
If two devices extend the same session, they diverge, and the most recently pushed snapshot replaces the other on the next pull. Messages are never unioned.
The SessionStart hook runs `sync-pull --latest --auto`. It takes the newest bundle added in git history, from any session or project (get_latest_bundle, `git log --diff-filter=A`), and force-imports it into the current working directory's project. From reading the code, this can drop an unrelated session into the open project; I did not test it.
The server keeps one namespace per user. Sharing is read-only: user B downloads A's latest bundle from an inbox.
realtime:
Not real-time. Three triggers exist:
(1) Manual `sync-push` / `sync-pull`.
(2) Claude Code hooks: SessionEnd runs `sync-push --session $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID --auto` and SessionStart runs `sync-pull --latest --auto` (hooks.py lines 41-56, https://github.com/Daniel-de-Oliveira-Trindade/claude-context-sync/blob/df88be89cf773c5a7b7de96daab87785b815abdf/src/hooks.py). Claude Code's hook docs deliver session_id only as JSON on stdin and document no CLAUDE_SESSION_ID variable (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks). That fits open issue #1, which says the hooks are unreliable.
(3) A `watch` daemon that uses watchdog on ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl. It checks every 5 s and pushes a full snapshot after 30 s without changes (watcher.py https://github.com/Daniel-de-Oliveira-Trindade/claude-context-sync/blob/df88be89cf773c5a7b7de96daab87785b815abdf/src/watcher.py).
Receivers learn of changes only when they pull: at SessionStart, by hand, or through the VS Code tree. The server has no push channel (no websocket or notifications).
search_retrieval: There is no content search. Retrieval works by an 8-hex session-ID prefix substring match on filenames, or by an interactive picker. The picker groups bundles by project folder and session prefix, lists versions by timestamp, and shows git commit messages (project plus first prompt) as labels (git_sync.py list_bundles / get_bundle_labels; cli.py sync-pull and sync-list). `--latest` takes the file most recently added in git; the server lists by mtime and prefix (storage.py). Restoring brings back the whole session for Claude Code's `/resume`. There is no partial recall, full-text index or embeddings. The server's admin dashboard lists users, bundles, sizes and shares.
links_sessions_to_code: Weakly, and only by project name. Bundles sit in a separate sessions repo under a folder named after the sanitized project directory name, derived from Claude Code's encoded cwd or from sessions-index projectPath (git_sync.py sanitize_project_name; cli.py lines ~555-575). They carry no commit SHAs, branch names, git notes or trailers, and nothing is written to the code repo. The VS Code extension warns when a pulled session's project does not match the open workspace (README v0.5.1 roadmap). The bundle does carry Claude Code's file-history snapshots (file contents before edits), so code content travels with the session, but it is not tied to any code commit.
scale: No real scale claims. The README says gzip "reduces bundle size by up to 86%" and shows an example 1,504-message session; the server caps uploads at 500 MB (main.py push_session). From reading the code: export and import load the whole JSONL into memory (read_text().splitlines(), json.load). Every push stores another complete copy in git and nothing prunes old copies. The server scans directories linearly on every list or lookup and resolves tokens by checking every user. Adoption: 13 stars and about 115 Marketplace installs (unverified, via page summarizer).
privacy_security:
Encryption is optional AES-256-GCM with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations, a random salt and nonce per bundle, and the whole bundle encrypted (crypto.py lines 1-30, 52). Weaknesses, all from reading the code at df88be8 and not tested:
(1) The automatic path is plaintext. Encryption runs only when `--encrypt` is passed (cli.py lines 777-801). The installed SessionEnd hook (hooks.py line 45) and the watcher (watcher.py line 95, `--auto --compress`) never pass it. In `--auto`, a missing passphrase skips encryption silently (cli.py line ~785; `_push_single` line ~596). The README says that after crypto-setup "sync-push --auto will encrypt bundles automatically", which the code does not do.
(2) Metadata leaks even when a bundle is encrypted. The git commit message holds the project name and the first 50 characters of the first prompt, and filenames hold session IDs and timestamps.
(3) The saved passphrase is only XOR-obfuscated with a pad derived from a salt file in the same directory. The module itself says this is "NOT cryptographic protection" (crypto.py lines 26-28).
(4) On pull, decrypted bundles are written next to the .enc file inside the clone, and plaintext local backups are kept.
(5) Integrity uses an unkeyed SHA-256, which catches corruption but not tampering. There are no signatures.
(6) Import trusts the bundle. fileHistory keys and sessionId are joined into filesystem paths unchecked (importer.py line 207, `(fh_dir / filename).write_text`), which allows path traversal or arbitrary file writes from a crafted or shared bundle. The server joins the `project` and `filename` form fields into storage paths unchecked (storage.py lines 24-27). The client uses the server's Content-Disposition filename as a local path (server_client.py line 133).
(7) There is no redaction or secret scanning; tool outputs and full file contents are shipped as-is.
(8) Server tokens are secrets.token_urlsafe(32), stored server-side as SHA-256 hashes, but the client keeps the raw token in ~/.claude-context-sync/server.json. docker-compose exposes plain HTTP on port 8000 and leaves TLS to the deployer. The README suggests putting a GitHub PAT in the repo URL.
(9) Prompt-injection channel: the design plan calls for automatically writing a colleague's recent messages into the recipient's CLAUDE.md (memory/plan-central-server.md, https://github.com/Daniel-de-Oliveira-Trindade/claude-context-sync/blob/df88be89cf773c5a7b7de96daab87785b815abdf/memory/plan-central-server.md). The server implements this as POST /api/sharing/{id}/apply (main.py line 250 onward). The v0.6.0 CLI and extension do not call that endpoint (grep), and it looks non-functional because it reads top-level `messages` and `role=="human"`. Shared bundles imported through `inbox --pull` still become resumable context, which is likewise an injection channel.
(10) Unsigned 16 MB Windows binaries are committed into the repo (dist-win32/, vscode-extension/bin/).
lesson_for_parinn:
The automatic path must be the safe path. In claude-context-sync, encryption is a CLI flag the installed hooks and watcher never pass, and `--auto` silently falls back to plaintext. So the default flow commits verbatim transcripts and file contents to a GitHub repo, with commit messages that quote the first prompt. Import then trusts an unkeyed SHA-256 and bundle-supplied paths.

If ParleyInn uses git as a transport, it should:
- seal every object before it leaves the core. Sealing should be on by default and fail closed: refuse the push, audit it and count it (I6), never downgrade.
- keep git-visible metadata (refs, filenames, commit messages) opaque.
- authenticate each event with a keyed MAC or signature chained into the hash chain.
- validate every incoming identifier.
- keep imported history pull-only and enveloped (I2), never auto-written to CLAUDE.md the way the project's planned "team context" injection would do.

Shipping append-only, immutable segments rather than whole-session snapshots also avoids the tool's last-writer-wins overwrite problem when two writers extend the same session.
confidence: high for the code-level facts, which come from reading the full source at commit df88be8. medium for the repo and Marketplace figures (stars, installs, dates), which came through a page summarizer. The security findings come from reading the code and were not exploited or tested.
license: The README says "MIT License". The MIT text is in vscode-extension/LICENSE ("Copyright (c) 2026 claude-context-sync contributors"). The clone has no LICENSE file at the repo root, so licensing of the CLI and server code relies on the README statement (https://github.com/Daniel-de-Oliveira-Trindade/claude-context-sync/blob/df88be89cf773c5a7b7de96daab87785b815abdf/vscode-extension/LICENSE).

name: claude-devtools (matt1398/claude-devtools)
category: session viewer/debugger (read-only, local-first; Electron desktop app or self-hosted Node/Fastify server)
status: shipped. The repo is active and not archived. The latest git tag is v0.5.0, and the HEAD commit 1486f20 is dated 2026-09-26 (seen in a shallow clone and with git ls-remote on 2026-10-02). The GitHub page showed about 4,000+ stars and 302 forks (https://github.com/matt1398/claide-devtools). I could not check the star count through the GitHub API because it was not reachable from this session. package.json still says version 0.1.0, which does not match the tags.
what_is_stored:
It keeps no session history of its own. It reads what Claude Code already writes and rebuilds it into a view.
- Session files: ~/.claude/projects/{encoded-path}/*.jsonl, where the path is encoded as /Users/name/project -> -Users-name-project (https://github.com/matt1398/claude-devtools/blob/main/CLAUDE.md).
- Todo data: ~/.claude/todos/{sessionId}.json (same CLAUDE.md).
- Project memory: ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/MEMORY.md plus one .md file per layer (https://github.com/matt1398/claude-devtools/blob/main/README.md).

From these it derives in memory:
- tool inputs and outputs (Read, Edit diffs, Bash output, search patterns and matches)
- thinking blocks
- per-turn token attribution in 6–7 categories: CLAUDE.md, @-mentioned files, tool output, thinking/text, team coordination, user message
- compaction phases
- subagent and agent-team trees with tokens, duration and cost (README; CLAUDE.md 'Visible Context Tracking').

The only thing it writes is its own config, at ~/.claude/claude-devtools-config.json. That file holds triggers and SSH profiles (https://github.com/matt1398/claude-devtools/blob/main/SECURITY.md). It can also export a session to Markdown, JSON or plain text when the user asks (README).
where_stored: Local files only. The source of truth is Claude Code's own ~/.claude JSONL tree, which the tool only reads. Derived data lives only in process memory: an LRU DataCache (default 50 entries, 10-minute TTL, mtime/size fingerprint) and a SearchTextCache keyed by mtime (default 1000 entries) (src/main/services/infrastructure/DataCache.ts, src/main/services/discovery/SearchTextCache.ts in the repo). There is no database, git storage or cloud store. Remote machines are read live over SSH through an SshFileSystemProvider, with nothing copied or synced (README 'SSH Remote Sessions'; src/main/services/infrastructure/SshFileSystemProvider.ts).
format_and_model:
Input is Claude Code's JSONL, one message per line, parsed by streaming line by line (CLAUDE.md 'Performance'). Messages are classified by the isMeta flag: false means a real user message, true means tool results or system content. They are then built into a timeline of typed chunks: UserChunk, AIChunk (assistant responses plus tool executions plus spawned subagents), SystemChunk and CompactChunk. Each chunk carries a timestamp, a duration and metrics (tokens, cost, tools).

Task tool_use blocks are linked to subagent sessions by a SubagentResolver. Orphaned Task calls are kept so they stay visible. Team membership comes from Task inputs and teammate_spawned results, and from <teammate-message> tags. Context injections form a discriminated union on `category`, and a compaction event resets the running total, tracked as ContextPhaseInfo (https://github.com/matt1398/claude-devtools/blob/main/CLAUDE.md). The whole model is a projection that can be rebuilt at any time from the JSONL record.
multi_writer_and_merge: Does not apply as a write path. The tool is read-only: 'The app does not write to session files', and Docker mounts ~/.claude with :ro (SECURITY.md; docker-compose.yml). Claude Code is the only writer, one JSONL file per session. Sessions from several worktrees are grouped into one repository identity rather than merged. GitIdentityResolver detects a worktree from its .git file pointing to gitdir .../worktrees/<name> and uses the remote URL as the identity. WorktreeGrouper also knows the directory layouts of Conductor, Cursor, vibe-kanban, 21st, ccswitch and auto-claude (src/main/services/parsing/GitIdentityResolver.ts, src/main/services/discovery/WorktreeGrouper.ts, src/main/constants/worktreePatterns). Machines are never merged: you switch the view between a local and an SSH context.
realtime:
Yes, live tailing of a single machine. The vendor docs page frames the tool as retrospective (https://claude-dev.tools/docs/what-is), but the code does more:
- FileWatcher uses fs.watch on the projects and todos directories with a 100 ms debounce.
- A catch-up scan runs every 30 s over files modified in the last hour, to pick up missed fs.watch events.
- Parsing is incremental from the last byte offset (appended lines only).
- In SSH mode it polls every 3 s, comparing file sizes.
- Updates reach browser clients over Server-Sent Events at GET /api/events, and the Electron renderer over IPC.

Sources are src/main/services/infrastructure/FileWatcher.ts and src/main/http/events.ts. It also has 'ongoing session' detection, and notification triggers for .env access, tool errors, token thresholds and custom regexes (README; TriggerManager.ts). There is no sharing between machines or users.
search_retrieval: Cmd+K search across sessions (README). It is a plain substring scan, with no index, embeddings or BM25. SessionSearcher reads the JSONL with a lighter extractor, looks only at user text and the AI's last text output (not tool I/O or thinking), returns surrounding context and stops at 50 results by default. Extracted text is cached in an LRU keyed by mtime. Over SSH it searches in stages of 40/140/320 sessions under a 4.5 s time budget (src/main/services/discovery/SessionSearcher.ts, SearchTextCache.ts). Retrieval is for humans in a UI. Nothing feeds recalled content back to the model, and there is no MCP or recall API.
links_sessions_to_code: Only weakly. Sessions are grouped by project path and by git repository identity across worktrees, using the remote URL and worktree gitdir parsing (GitIdentityResolver.ts). Tool inspectors show the file paths, Edit diffs and line ranges that Claude touched (README). It does not link sessions or prompts to commits, through trailers, notes or blame, and it does not write anything into git.
scale: No numeric scale claims found. It claims to work retroactively over 'every Claude Code session you've ever run' (https://claude-dev.tools/docs/what-is). Performance measures are LRU caches, line-by-line streaming JSONL parsing, virtual scrolling and debounced watching (CLAUDE.md 'Performance'). The search and watch scopes are bounded: catch-up looks back 1 h, search stops at 50 results, and SSH search has a 4.5 s budget. I could not verify any benchmarks.
privacy_security:
Claims:
- No telemetry or analytics.
- Standalone/Docker mode makes 'zero outbound network calls'; auto-update and SSH are disabled there.
- `docker run --network none` with a :ro mount is the documented hardening (SECURITY.md; README).
- The Electron build does contact the GitHub Releases API automatically at launch for electron-updater, and opens SSH connections when the user starts them (SECURITY.md network table).
- IPC and file reads are confined to the project root and ~/.claude with path-traversal checks. A sensitive-path deny list blocks .ssh, .aws, gcloud, .azure, .env*, .git-credentials and similar (src/main/utils/pathValidation.ts).

What it lacks:
- No redaction of secrets inside the transcripts it displays or exports.
- No encryption at rest (it relies on Claude Code's plaintext JSONL).
- No integrity checks or hash chaining on the logs.

Noteworthy, from my own code inspection (not a documented claim): standalone mode defaults to HOST=0.0.0.0 and CORS_ORIGIN='*' (src/main/standalone.ts), and I found no authentication hook on the Fastify routes (src/main/services/infrastructure/HttpServer.ts, src/main/http/*). Anyone who can reach port 3456 can read every transcript. The project relies on Docker or network isolation instead of auth. The vulnerability disclosure process is informal: there is no private contact address yet (SECURITY.md).
license: MIT (Copyright (c) 2026 claude-devtools contributors), https://github.com/matt1398/claude-devtools/blob/main/LICENSE
lesson_for_parinn:
Treat ~/.claude JSONL as a substrate you only read, rebuilt into typed chunks. Claude Code's own JSONL already holds enough to rebuild turns, tool I/O, thinking, compaction phases, subagent and team trees, and per-category token use. claude-devtools does all of it with no writer and no store of its own: byte-offset tailing with fs.watch, a 30 s catch-up scan, and mtime-keyed caches. That backs ParleyInn's I10 design, where the record is the source and every view is a rebuildable projection. ParleyInn's ingest can follow the same pattern: tail by offset, add a periodic catch-up scan for missed watch events, and key any derived cache on (mtime, size).

It also marks where ParleyInn must go further. A pure viewer has no integrity guarantee, because Claude Code can rewrite or delete the JSONL. It does no redaction before display or export. Its standalone server binds 0.0.0.0 with CORS * and no authentication. So 'no outbound calls' is not the same as 'not exposed': ParleyInn should hash-chain on ingest, redact before anything leaves the process, and keep any viewer or MCP surface on loopback or Unix sockets by default.

Grouping worktrees by git remote URL plus .git-file gitdir parsing, with known layouts for Conductor, Cursor and vibe-kanban, is a ready-made heuristic for ParleyInn's cross-worktree session identity.

name: claude-mem (thedotmack)
category: session-capture memory plugin (Claude Code plugin, plus other agent hosts), with an optional paid cloud sync service (cmem.ai)
status: shipped
license: Apache-2.0. The LICENSE file is the Apache License 2.0 text (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/main/LICENSE) and the README says the same (https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem). Earlier releases may have used a different license; I did not check that in this pass. The cmem.ai cloud service is a separate commercial product (https://cmem.ai).
what_is_stored: Distilled memory plus a partial raw backup, not a full transcript. Tables (https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/database): sdk_sessions holds sdk_session_id, claude_session_id, project, status, timestamps and prompt_counter. observations are LLM-compressed records of tool use: tool_name, prompt_number, correlation_id, title/subtitle/narrative/text/facts/concepts, files_read, files_modified, and a type that is one of decision, bugfix, feature, refactor, discovery or change. session_summaries are LLM summaries per prompt with the fields request, investigated, learned, completed, next_steps and notes. user_prompts holds raw prompt text (since v4.2.0). tool_uses (schema v51) is a 'durable backup index' of raw tool_input and tool_response, each capped at 64 KB with a truncation marker, plus cwd, content_hash (computed before truncation), platform_source and OpenRouter spend ids. The privacy docs say Claude's own responses are not captured (https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/private-tags). Settings live in ~/.claude-mem/settings.json (README).
where_stored: Local DB. SQLite at ~/.claude-mem/claude-mem.db through bun:sqlite, plus a Chroma vector store 'alongside' it (https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/database, https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem). The exact Chroma path is not documented on the pages I read. Optionally the observations DB is mirrored to the cmem.ai cloud: 'the worker syncs on write' (README; https://cmem.ai). Nothing goes into git or the working tree.
format_and_model: A mutable relational SQLite schema with numbered migrations (src/services/sqlite/migrations.ts, now past migration 051). Two FTS5 virtual tables, observations_fts and session_summaries_fts, are kept in sync by triggers. WAL mode is on and the API is synchronous (https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/database). Data flow: the Setup hook plus the SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop and SessionEnd hooks call bun-runner.js, which spawns worker-service.cjs, 'the single dispatcher for all hook logic'. A local HTTP worker on port 37700 + (uid % 100) compresses tool events into observations asynchronously with the Claude Agent SDK (https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview). The summarizing model is selectable: the claude-mem hosted 'observer' (free for 14 days), your own OpenRouter or Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan (README). There is no hash chain, no signatures and no append-only guarantee. Rows are derived by an LLM, so the record is lossy and not reproducible.
multi_writer_and_merge: On one machine there is one worker per OS user, and concurrent sessions share one SQLite file through WAL (https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/database, https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview). Sessions are keyed by sdk_session_id plus claude_session_id and grouped by a 'project' text key. I found no documentation of how project is derived (cwd, git root or worktree). tool_uses is idempotent through UNIQUE(content_session_id, tool_use_id). There is no merge model across machines in the open-source core. Cross-device sharing goes through the cmem.ai cloud mirror, and its Team plan ($333/seat/month) advertises 'per-project scopes & isolation' and 'roles, access control & audit' (https://cmem.ai). The conflict and merge semantics of that sync are not documented and cannot be verified.
realtime: Locally yes. A web viewer served by the worker shows a 'real-time memory stream via Server-Sent Events' (https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview). Cloud sync happens on write, and cmem.ai advertises live 'brainbeats' pushed to your phone (https://cmem.ai). There is no peer-to-peer or git-based real-time sharing.
search_retrieval: Push and pull. Push: SessionStart automatically injects observations from earlier sessions, with a configurable count. The ranking is not documented (https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview). The README also mentions an 'Include all sources at session start' setting. Pull: MCP tools follow a '3-layer workflow'. search returns a compact index, timeline gives chronological context, and get_observations returns full details, which the README claims saves about 10x tokens. Search combines FTS5 keyword search with Chroma semantic search (README). user_prompts has no FTS index and is searched with LIKE (database docs).
links_sessions_to_code: Only loosely. Observations record files_read, files_modified and a type such as bugfix or refactor, and tool_uses records cwd. There are no git commit, branch or diff fields: 'No direct git commit fields; code references via files_read/files_modified' (https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/database).
scale: The README shows version 13.28.0 and about 95.2k GitHub stars (https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem; both read from the page on 2026-10-02 and may change). Raw tool payloads are capped at 64 KB each (database docs). The README makes no benchmarks or capacity claims. cmem.ai claims sync across '31+ devices and agent types' (https://cmem.ai). The README lists many hosts: Claude Code, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, Grok and others.
privacy_security: Text the user wraps in <private> tags is stripped at the hook layer before it reaches the worker or the DB. This applies to UserPromptSubmit prompts and to the serialized tool_input and tool_response in PostToolUse. There is also an opt-in 'Auto-Redaction' feature, 'regex-based detection for accidental token leaks' (https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/private-tags). Environment variables can turn capture off (README). The pages I read do not document encryption at rest. Stored content goes to a third-party LLM to be summarized (the hosted observer, OpenRouter, Gemini or Anthropic), so data leaves the machine by default unless you run your own provider setup (README). Recalled summaries are injected automatically at SessionStart with no documented untrusted-content envelope. That is exactly the stored-content-to-prompt path ParleyInn's I2 forbids. cmem.ai says 'End-to-end private — your link, your keys' but does not specify the cryptography (https://cmem.ai). The README also mentions a 'CMEM' crypto token tied to the project, separate from the code. The OSS core is not network-silent: it runs a localhost HTTP worker, calls an LLM provider and can sync to the cloud.
lesson_for_parinn: claude-mem shows that the market wants a cheap index-first recall API: a compact search result, then a timeline, then full details on demand, which it claims saves about 10x tokens. It also shows the price of its design. LLM-summarized rows are mutable and lossy, and they are pushed into the prompt at SessionStart without an untrusted-content envelope. Data goes off-box to summarizers and a cloud mirror, and there is no merge model across machines. ParleyInn should copy two things: the three-layer pull interface over its own exact, hash-chained record, and redaction at the hook edge before anything is persisted, as claude-mem does with <private>. It should keep summaries as rebuildable derived projections (I10) that never auto-inject (I2). Its UNIQUE(content_session_id, tool_use_id) idempotency key plus a pre-truncation content_hash is a ready-made dedupe key for replaying hook events from many writers.

name: claude-nomad
category: Claude Code session sync via git (single-user, multi-machine config and transcript sync through a private git repo)
status: shipped
what_is_stored:
A private git "sync repo" (default remote name claude-nomad-config, local checkout ~/claude-nomad/) holds the user's Claude Code setup and history. It does not hold the tool's own code (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/how-it-works/).

What it holds:
- shared/CLAUDE.md, commands/, rules/, my-statusline.cjs. These are symlinked into ~/.claude/.
- shared/skills/, as a filtered copy. gsd-* skills and Claude Code's skills/synced, .trash and .staging folders are excluded.
- shared/settings.base.json plus hosts/<HOST>.json. Each pull deep-merges these into a generated ~/.claude/settings.json.
- path-map.json.
- Session transcripts under shared/projects/<logical>/. These are <session-id>.jsonl files plus a <session-id>/ subtree for subagent transcripts and tool results, and memory/*.md notes. Only projects listed in path-map.json are synced; a fresh init maps none (README: https://github.com/funkadelic/claude-nomad/blob/main/README.md).
- Opt-in per-project extras: .planning, a root CLAUDE.md, and a project's own .claude/. These land under shared/extras/<logical>/.
- Opt-in sharedDirs.
- .gitleaksignore and .gitleaks.overlay.toml (allow-list in src/core/config.ts: https://github.com/funkadelic/claude-nomad/blob/main/src/core/config.ts).

Never synced, by a hard-coded NEVER_SYNC list (how-it-works):
- ~/.claude.json and .credentials.json (OAuth and MCP state)
- history.jsonl (prompt history)
- settings.local.json
- todos/, shell-snapshots/, file-history/, plans/, session-env/, statsig/, telemetry/, caches, sessions/ and tasks/
- hooks/ and agents/, which @opengsd/gsd-core owns per host

Host-local state lives under ~/.cache/claude-nomad/ and is not synced:
- a push manifest
- the lock file
- timestamped backups
- crash reports

Correction to the discovery note: nomad does not rewrite paths inside transcripts. It translates only the session directory name, which Claude Code builds from the absolute cwd, using path-map.json. Transcript bytes are copied unchanged ("transcript byte-equality invariant" in src/sync/resume.ts: https://github.com/funkadelic/claude-nomad/blob/main/src/sync/resume.ts). The cwd recorded inside a transcript keeps the source host's path. `nomad doctor --resume-cmd <id>` prints a host-local `cd ... && claude --resume` line instead (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/usage/). The README and who-is-this-for pages say it "rewrites the machine-specific file paths Claude Code embeds in every transcript". That wording overstates what the code does (src/sync/remap.ts: https://github.com/funkadelic/claude-nomad/blob/main/src/sync/remap.ts).
where_stored: A separate private git repo that the user owns. `nomad init` creates it on GitHub through the gh CLI. Every other host clones it to ~/claude-nomad, or to a path set by NOMAD_REPO (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/how-it-works/). Live files sit in ~/.claude/, as symlinks into the checkout, or as real copies on native Windows. Host-local caches, backups, the lock and the per-host push manifest sit in ~/.cache/claude-nomad/. The project runs no server or backend (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/privacy/). Non-GitHub remotes appear possible, since a recent commit stops treating a remote as GitHub unless its host is github.com. I could not verify any documented Forgejo or GitLab path.
format_and_model:
Files in a git tree, no database.

Transcripts:
- Claude Code's native JSONL, stored byte for byte as shared/projects/<logical>/<session-id>.jsonl plus the <session-id>/ subtree.
- On push, only *.jsonl files at the top of a project directory are copied. Subdirectories copy in full.
- `.gitattributes` is `* -text`, so git does no line-ending conversion (src/commands/init/init.ts: https://github.com/funkadelic/claude-nomad/blob/main/src/commands/init/init.ts).

Project identity:
- A logical project name maps to one absolute path per host label (NOMAD_HOST) in path-map.json. "TBD" marks a host not yet set up.
- Push fails closed if two paths encode to the same directory name, or if two logical names share a path (src/sync/remap.ts).

Settings:
- settings.base.json is deep-merged with hosts/<HOST>.json. Scalars override, objects merge recursively, arrays replace, and null overrides (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/faq/).

Per-host push manifest (src/sync/manifest.ts: https://github.com/funkadelic/claude-nomad/blob/main/src/sync/manifest.ts):
- Stored in ~/.cache as push-manifest-<HOST>.json.
- Shape: {schema:1, scannerVersion, configHash, files:{absPath:{size, mtime, sha256}}}.
- It drives incremental copy and scan.

Commits:
- One commit per push, message "chore: sync from <HOST>" (src/commands/push/steps.ts: https://github.com/funkadelic/claude-nomad/blob/main/src/commands/push/steps.ts).
- There is no per-event structure, hash chain or signing beyond git itself.
multi_writer_and_merge:
The writers are one person's several machines. The threat model calls it "a single-user tool" (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/security/).

Concurrency:
- A per-HOME exclusive lock file at ~/.cache/claude-nomad/nomad.lock. It uses stale-pid recovery, and a run that finds the lock held skips with exit 0.
- The lock is machine-local. Nothing coordinates across machines except git (src/core/utils.lockfile.ts: https://github.com/funkadelic/claude-nomad/blob/main/src/core/utils.lockfile.ts).

Push:
1. Rebases the checkout on the remote with git pull --rebase --autostash.
2. Copies local state over the repo tree, so local wins.
3. Runs git add -A, checks the allow-list, runs the gitleaks scan, then commits and pushes (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/faq/).

Pull:
- A "retain-merge overlay". Repo files are force-copied over local files with the same name, after a backup to ~/.cache/claude-nomad/backup/<ts>/.
- Local-only transcripts, subagent directories and memory files survive (src/sync/remap.ts).

What is not merged:
- There is no line-level or event-level merge of JSONL. The docs say "Last-write-wins on conflicts. Git surfaces them on merge; no field-level JSON merging" (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/how-it-works/).
- If the same file changed on two hosts, "the host that pushes last clobbers the other's version in the sync repo (the older copy survives only in git history)" (FAQ).
- `nomad sync` runs pull, then push, under one lock.

Recovery:
- `nomad pull --force-remote` recovers a repo stuck mid-rebase or with an unmerged index. It parks stranded commits on nomad/stranded-<ts>.
- It refuses if those commits touch synced config.
- A separate guard catches a conflicted autostash pop and exits 4 (FAQ; README).

Settings drift:
- Tracked through per-key fingerprints of values nomad itself wrote.
- `nomad capture-settings` promotes keys that other tools added locally (README).
realtime:
None. Sync is manual: "Manual push/pull. No file watcher. Shell hooks recommended" (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/how-it-works/). Users run `nomad sync`, or call it from shell-rc or cron. Skipping on a held lock makes concurrent runs harmless (README).

The optional Claude Code plugin's SessionStart hook does not sync. It runs a read-only `nomad doctor` and injects only the WARN/FAIL lines into the session context, always exiting 0 (https://github.com/funkadelic/claude-nomad/blob/main/.claude-plugin/nomad-plugin/hooks/session-start.sh). Its /nomad:sync and /nomad:push commands only preview (README).
search_retrieval:
No search or index of its own. Retrieval means Claude Code's native `claude --resume` over the transcripts nomad puts in place.

Helpers:
- `nomad doctor --resume-cmd <id>` reads a transcript's recorded cwd, looks up the logical project in path-map.json, and prints a host-local resume command (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/usage/).
- `nomad diff` and `--dry-run` preview changes.
- `nomad doctor --check-shared` re-scans already-synced memory notes and skills for secrets.

Version history is plain git history.
links_sessions_to_code:
No. Sessions are keyed only by logical project, mapped to a per-host path, and by session id. Nothing links a session or prompt to commits, branches or diffs in the project's own repo. Sync commits say only "chore: sync from <HOST>" (src/commands/push/steps.ts).

Two indirect ties exist:
- Claude Code's own cwd field inside each transcript, read by --resume-cmd (src/sync/resume.ts).
- Opt-in "extras", which carry project-local, git-ignored files (.planning/, a root CLAUDE.md, the project's .claude/) beside the sessions.

The docs warn against syncing extras that the project repo already tracks, because nomad's last-write-wins copy can revert committed files (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/how-it-works/).
scale:
There are no formal scale claims. It is single-user by design (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/security/).

Data points:
- A source comment says "a real ~420MB tree measured at roughly 5 minutes" for a gitleaks scan. The scan timeout is set to 15 minutes for that reason (src/core/config.ts).
- The per-host manifest makes routine pushes copy and scan only changed transcripts (README).

Inference, not documented: each push stores a whole new git blob for every grown JSONL file, so repo history grows with transcript churn.

Adoption:
- npm reports 1,696 downloads for September 2026 (https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-month/claude-nomad).
- The GitHub page showed 5 stars and 2 forks at fetch time (https://github.com/funkadelic/claude-nomad).
- First release v0.2.0 on 2026-05-14; latest v0.69.5 on 2026-09-25 (https://github.com/funkadelic/claude-nomad/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
privacy_security:
Gates, in the order a push meets them:

1. A push allow-list. It contains PUSH_ALLOWED_STATIC plus the shared/projects/<logical>/ directories, whitelisted extras and valid sharedDirs that path-map.json names. Any staged path that is off the list or in NEVER_SYNC aborts the push (src/commands/push/allowlist.ts: https://github.com/funkadelic/claude-nomad/blob/main/src/commands/push/allowlist.ts).
2. A hard block on credential file names, applied even inside opted-in extras. It is case-insensitive and ignores trailing dots and whitespace, and covers .env*, *.pem, *.key, .netrc and .npmrc. Pulled path-map values are checked against path traversal (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/security/).
3. gitleaks, pinned to 8.30.1. It runs as `gitleaks protect --staged --redact` over the exact staged tree, so secret values are never printed. A finding aborts the push with exit code 5 (src/commands/push/gitleaks.scan.ts: https://github.com/funkadelic/claude-nomad/blob/main/src/commands/push/gitleaks.scan.ts; src/core/config.ts).

The interactive menu offers one prompt per distinct secret (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/recovery/):
- Redact: rewrites the local source transcript in place to `[REDACTED:<rule>]`, after a backup. It refuses if the session was modified in the last 5 minutes.
- Allow: appends a `file:rule:line` fingerprint to .gitleaksignore. The entry is held back while another secret sharing that fingerprint is unresolved, and rolled back if the re-scan fails.
- Drop: unstages the session. This is not durable, because the next push copies it again from local.
- Skip.
- Non-interactive flags: --redact-all, --allow <rule>, --allow-all, --full-scan.
- Every allow path re-scans afterwards.

Known gaps:
- The scan lives in the `nomad push` wrapper, not in a git hook or on the server. A manual `git push` from the checkout "bypasses the scan entirely" (security page; README).
- The scan configuration (.gitleaks.toml, .gitleaksignore) rides in the synced repo, so anyone with write access can weaken detection. Only the overlay file is forced to be path-scoped.
- Pulling hosts "still trust whatever the repo contains". Pulled transcripts are replayed to the model on --resume without vetting (security page).
- A secret that was already pushed needs credential rotation plus git filter-repo and a force-push (recovery page).

Encryption: none at rest or in transit beyond git and the host's own. Confidentiality depends on the repo staying private. `nomad init` disables GitHub Actions on the new repo so no CI can echo transcripts into logs, and the docs warn that a public repo exposes every conversation (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/quickstart/).

Other privacy facts:
- No telemetry.
- `nomad doctor` makes only a GET to registry.npmjs.org, plus json.schemastore.org with --check-schema.
- Crash reports stay local at mode 0600, with home and hostname scrubbed and a gitleaks pass (https://funkadelic.github.io/claude-nomad/privacy/).
- The project is MIT licensed.
lesson_for_parinn:
Main lesson: put the secret and redaction gate on the record, not on the transport command. claude-nomad scans inside `nomad push`, so a plain `git push` skips it. Its scan policy (.gitleaksignore, .gitleaks.toml) travels in the same writable repo that it protects. Pulling hosts trust whatever comes down and replay it to the model.

For ParleyInn, if git (GitHub or Forgejo) ever carries session history:
- Redact and audit at ingest, before an event is hash-chained (I6). The pushable bytes are then already clean, whatever command moves them.
- Keep redaction policy and allow-lists out of the synced channel. A peer must not be able to weaken them.
- Treat every pulled object as untrusted. Verify the chain and re-run redaction on receipt, and let it reach the model only through enveloped, pull-only recall (I2).

Secondary point: nomad merges whole JSONL files by last-write-wins and keys projects by absolute path. A session resumed on two machines therefore loses one side in the repo. ParleyInn should sync per-event, content-addressed objects so that merging is a set union. It should also keep raw bytes immutable and translate paths only when building a view. nomad already does the second part: its byte-equality invariant plus the --resume-cmd sidecar fits ParleyInn's I10.
