The Artifacts docs I read do not mention encryption at rest, customer-managed keys, redaction, secret scanning, or treating stored content as untrusted. All content is visible to Cloudflare. Tokens embedded in remote URLs can leak into agent transcripts and shell history.
scale: Marketing: "create tens of millions of repos", "millions (or tens of millions+)" of Durable Object instances (blog, product page). The roughly 50k new repos a day figure is not in the launch post. It comes from an X post by Cloudflare's Dillon Mulroy ("nearing 50,000 new repositories per day"), as relayed by https://flaviocopes.com/cloudflare-artifacts/, and I could not check it at the original source. Pricing: first 10k ops per month free, then $0.15 per 1k ops; first 1 GB free, then $0.50 per GB-month; replication is included (https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/platform/pricing/).
license: Proprietary hosted service. ArtifactFS is Apache-2.0 (https://github.com/cloudflare/artifact-fs). The Zig/Wasm git engine is not open source as far as I could verify.
confidence: high for the architecture, APIs, limits, pricing and dates, which come from official docs and the official blog. Medium for the session-history-in-repo encoding and the 50k repos a day figure, which come from the blog only or second-hand. Low for concurrency, merge and encryption behaviour, which is not documented.

name: clync
category: sync-to-git (encrypted): a single-user backup and multi-machine sync tool for ~/.claude
status: shipped. Early alpha: v0.4.2 on crates.io dated 2026-08-19, MIT license (https://docs.rs/crate/clync/latest). There have been 17 releases since the first on 2026-07-04, with 401 crates.io downloads in total (https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/clync). On GitHub it has 0 stars, 0 forks and 54 commits from one author, and is not archived (https://github.com/Saturate/clync). The last commit was the v0.4.2 release on 2026-08-19, so there has been no activity for about 6 weeks as of 2026-10-02.
what_is_stored:
Copies of Claude Code's local state from ~/.claude:
- Whole per-session transcripts (projects/<encoded-path>/<session-uuid>.jsonl), copied unchanged when pushed.
- Optional per-session "companion" directories, stored as tar.gz files.
- Per-project memory/ directories, including MEMORY.md.
- settings.json and settings.local.json.
- commands/, skills/ and the global CLAUDE.md (README "What it does", "Sync repo structure": https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/README.md; https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/sync.rs#L113-L137; https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/extras.rs).

It also keeps a manifest mapping session UUID to project path (relative to $HOME), mtime, size, a 64-bit FNV-1a content hash, the hostname that last pushed, and the project's `git remote get-url origin` with credentials stripped (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/manifest.rs; https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/scanner.rs; https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/resolver.rs#L92-L118).

A plaintext sync log records timestamp, hostname, operation and counts, capped at 500 lines. Its per-session merge-record field is defined but never filled in (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/synclog.rs#L7-L73).

There is no event model of its own: clync mirrors files and does not record anything Claude Code did not already write.
where_stored:
A separate git repo per user, by default ~/.clync/data. `clync init` can create a private GitHub repo for it via the gh CLI, and pushes are plain `git push`. Alternatives are a local or network folder (NAS, Dropbox, USB) or an S3-compatible bucket, built with `--features s3` (README "Storage backends": https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/README.md).

With S3, only sessions sync. Memories, settings, commands and skills print "not supported with S3 storage" (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/extras.rs; https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/memories.rs#L22-L35).

The config file moved to ~/.clync/config.toml in v0.4.1, but the README still says ~/.config/clync/ (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/CHANGELOG.md).

Repo layout:
- Plaintext: clync.toml, README.md and sync.log.jsonl.
- Encrypted: manifest.json.age and sessions/<uuid>.jsonl.age (plus <uuid>.dir.tar.gz.age).
- extras/*.age and memories/<normalized-project>/*.age. The directory and file names here stay readable.

Nothing is written to the code repos themselves: no git notes, no custom refs, no branches.
format_and_model:
Files are mirrored one-to-one and each is age-encrypted as a whole (binary age format; the age crate is built with the armor feature). A changed session is re-read and re-encrypted in full, then overwrites sessions/<uuid>.jsonl.age (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/sync.rs#L50-L137).

Change detection compares the 64-bit FNV-1a hash of the local file with the manifest's value; FNV-1a is not a cryptographic hash (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/parser.rs#L76-L88).

For merging, a session is parsed as JSONL into a struct. Its named fields are uuid, parentUuid, sessionId, timestamp (an untyped JSON value), type and cwd; everything else is captured in a flattened `extra` value (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/parser.rs#L6-L26).

My own reading of the code, inferred from serde/serde_json semantics and not executed (running the crate was not permitted here): a merge rewrites the transcript by re-serializing it. Named fields that are null are dropped, so a root message's "parentUuid":null disappears. Keys in `extra` come out alphabetically sorted, because serde_json is used without preserve_order (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/Cargo.toml).

There is no hash chain, no signature and no history beyond what git commits keep.
multi_writer_and_merge:
Merging happens in two layers.

**1. Session-level "smart merge"**, run only on pull, between the local ~/.claude copy and the decrypted remote copy (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/merge.rs):
- Entries are unioned by uuid.
- If the same uuid has different content, the remote entry wins only when its timestamp is strictly greater; otherwise local wins. The losing version is discarded, despite the README's "No data is lost" (L32-L50).
- Entries without a uuid are deduplicated by content hash and moved to the end, sorted by timestamp, so their original position is lost (L59-L83).
- uuid entries are written out depth-first along the parentUuid tree, with siblings ordered by timestamp (L93-L157).

**Likely defect (my code reading, not executed).** `timestamp_millis` only accepts a JSON number or a numeric string (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/parser.rs#L34-L40). Real Claude Code transcripts carry ISO-8601 strings such as "2025-07-03T15:50:07.874907Z" (fixture: https://github.com/daaain/claude-code-log/blob/main/test/test_data/representative_messages.jsonl). Every timestamp would then parse as 0. "Newer wins" would collapse to "local wins", and sibling order would follow HashMap iteration order. clync's tests use only numeric timestamps.

**Merge only runs on pull.** Push uploads the local file without merging, and `sync` is pull-then-push. The merged result is written back into ~/.claude/projects with a non-atomic fs::write, with no coordination with a Claude Code process that may still be appending to the file (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/sync.rs#L337-L358; https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/cmd/sync_cmd.rs).

Memory files, settings and other extras use per-file mtime last-writer-wins. MEMORY.md gets a line-union merge of its "- [..](target)" entries, where the longer line wins (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/fileutil.rs#L39-L74; https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/memories.rs#L220-L294).

**2. Transport level.** The git backend runs `git add -A`, `git commit` and `git push`, and pulls with `git pull --ff-only`. If two machines have both pushed, clync stops and tells the user to run `git pull --rebase` by hand (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/store/git.rs#L93-L143). That rebase would conflict on the binary manifest.json.age, which every push rewrites.

There is only a local file lock (.clync.lock via fs2), so two clync processes on one machine are serialized but machines are not. The README warns that S3 has no locking and concurrent writes can conflict.

The design assumes a single human moving between machines, not many agents writing concurrently.
realtime: None. Syncing happens only when someone runs `clync sync`, `push` or `pull` by hand, or when the agent calls the MCP tools sync_push or sync_pull (README "Sync", "MCP server": https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/README.md). The source has no daemon, file watcher, timer or Claude Code hook integration; a grep for hook, watch, daemon, interval and cron finds nothing in src/ at v0.4.2. Latency is whatever the user's push and pull cadence is.
search_retrieval:
Search is minimal and works only on local plaintext. `clync list [query]` and the MCP list_sessions tool do a case-insensitive substring match on three things: the normalized project path, the session UUID, and the first user message cut to 120 characters. The README says "search ... content", but this is not full-text search and there is no index (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/list.rs#L18-L80).

The MCP tool session_detail(uuid prefix, tail N) returns counts plus the last N user and assistant messages, each cut to 500 characters (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/mcp.rs#L268-L340).

The encrypted remote store cannot be searched without pulling and decrypting it first. There is no semantic or BM25 retrieval, and no re-injection into context.
links_sessions_to_code:
Only loosely, and at project level:
- Each session's manifest entry holds its project path (relative to $HOME) and the project repo's origin remote URL with credentials stripped (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/scanner.rs; https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/resolver.rs#L92-L118).
- On another machine, the resolver uses those to map a session to the matching local checkout by path suffix or repo name.
- `clync checkout` (v0.4.1) offers a TUI that clones repos whose sessions were pulled but which are not checked out locally.
- `clync mv` moves sessions between projects (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/CHANGELOG.md).

There is no link from a commit SHA, branch, diff or file to a prompt or message, and nothing is written into the code repo.
scale:
No performance or size claims are made. What the project does say:
- Session files of 99 MB or more (103809024 bytes, configurable, 0 disables) are auto-tracked with git-lfs.
- Encryption and decryption run in parallel via rayon.
- The README warns against concurrent S3 writers.
- The sync log keeps at most 500 entries.
(README: https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/README.md; https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/sync.rs#L81-L101; https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/synclog.rs#L56.)

My inference from the design: any change to a session re-encrypts the whole file. age output is randomized, so each push adds a full-size, uncompressible, non-deltifiable blob to git history, and the repo grows roughly with the sum of all pushed versions of every session. Adoption is effectively zero: 0 stars and 401 total downloads.
privacy_security:
**Encryption.** age, in three modes (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/crypto.rs; https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/secret.rs):
- X25519: one shared identity. Every machine holds the same secret key and encrypts to its own public key.
- Passphrase: scrypt, passphrase taken from an environment variable.
- Plaintext: `--no-encrypt`, which relies on the repo being private.

The secret key comes from a key file or from the op, bw or pass CLIs, and is never stored in the sync repo (README "Encryption"). There are no per-machine or per-user recipients, no key rotation command, and no signing: anyone holding the key can write valid ciphertext, so writers are not authenticated.

**Plaintext metadata in the repo.**
- clync.toml holds the encryption method plus a "hint": the 1Password reference, Bitwarden item id or pass entry name (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/repo_meta.rs#L58-L70).
- sync.log.jsonl records hostnames, timestamps and counts.
- Commit messages read "clync push (N sessions) from <hostname>" (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/cmd/sync_cmd.rs#L56-L64).
- File names reveal session UUIDs and sizes, normalized project names (memories/<project>/) and command and skill file names.

**No redaction.** Transcripts are encrypted exactly as written; there is no secret scanning or scrubbing. Only the S3 keys are masked in the config's Debug output (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/src/config.rs#L75-L85). Git remote URLs have embedded credentials stripped.

**Path safety on pull.** Traversal checks are applied to session UUIDs, project paths and memory directory names. v0.4.2 made the stricter component validation opt-in, so it no longer silently skips sessions (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/CHANGELOG.md).

**External programs.** clync shells out to git, gh, op, bw and pass.

**Recalled content is not treated as untrusted.** The MCP server returns transcript text as plain tool output, with no envelope or marking. That includes text merged in from other machines. This is the kind of channel ParleyInn's I2 forbids.
license: MIT (https://github.com/Saturate/clync/blob/v0.4.2/Cargo.toml; https://docs.rs/crate/clync/latest)
lesson_for_parinn:
Do not move history between machines by encrypting and merging the tool's own mutable transcript file. clync encrypts each ~/.claude JSONL file as a whole, which leaves git unable to diff, delta-compress or merge it. Divergence then means a hand-run `git pull --rebase` on binary blobs and a single shared manifest. The UUID-tree merge rewrites the source transcript: last-writer-wins on edits, metadata entries reordered, null keys dropped, and a timestamp parser that does not appear to accept Claude Code's ISO-8601 strings.

For ParleyInn:
- Give each writer (machine, worktree or sandbox) its own append-only, hash-chained event log, and make the shared view a set-union of immutable, content-addressed events. Merging then never conflicts and never rewrites the raw record.
- When encrypting for git or object-store transport, encrypt per event or per append segment, so an append adds new objects instead of re-encrypting a growing file.
- Keep hostnames, session ids, project names and key-manager hints out of plaintext transport metadata. Use per-device recipients or signatures so writers are authenticated.
- Never expose synced content back to the model without an untrusted-content envelope.
confidence: high for what is stored, where, encryption and the transport design: read directly from the v0.4.2 source (commit 2f4f3c2) and the crates.io metadata. medium for the inferred merge defects (ISO timestamps parsing as 0, null keys dropped, key reordering): these come from reading the code and serde semantics, because executing the crate's tests was not permitted. No independent technical discussions could be found or checked; the web search budget was exhausted.

name: Code.Storage (The Pierre Computer Company)
category: Git hosting for machine-generated artifacts (headless, API-first managed git backend for agent platforms)
status: shipped
what_is_stored: Plain git repositories holding whatever the customer's product writes. The homepage lists "generated code, memory files, design artifacts, legal documents, and other product files and resources that change over time" for Lovable, Poke, Bolt, Anything, Amp and Parahelp (https://code.storage). Bolt and Amp appear only as names on the homepage. I found no case study or technical detail for either. The case studies that exist describe real use. Lovable creates "one or many git repositories" per user project (https://code.storage/changelog/lovable-case-study). Poke stores "general memory, recipes, integrations, sandbox workspaces, generated changes, and long-running agent workflows" (https://code.storage/changelog/poke-case-study). The official guides show four patterns: agent memory files (https://code.storage/docs/guides/agent-memory.md), per-session agent state captured as commits (https://code.storage/docs/guides/capture-agent-state.md), parallel agent attempts as branches (https://code.storage/docs/guides/parallel-attempts.md), and per-commit metadata such as "build status, review state, an agent's verdict on a change, a reward graded on one commit" kept in git notes (https://code.storage/docs/repos/git-notes.md). Code.Storage has no native concept of a transcript, prompt or session record. The guides tell customers to keep the repo ID, branch and head SHA in their own session database.
where_stored: On a server, in the cloud. Pierre hosts the git repositories, multi-tenant by default. Single-tenant and VPC/private networking are offered on the Scale and Enterprise plans (https://code.storage/pricing). The listed sub-processors are all in the US: AWS for "data hosting, storage infrastructure", Google for "data hosting", and PlanetScale for "data hosting" (https://code.storage/legal/sub-processors). Pierre's founder said on Hacker News that the design is "Github's spoke architecture with a few modern twists + object store for cold storage" (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46957629). Repositories untouched for more than 7 days move automatically to a compressed cold tier (https://code.storage/pricing). Mirroring to GitHub is optional. GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea, Forgejo, Codeberg and SourceHut are supported through generic HTTPS sync (https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt).
format_and_model:
Standard git object model: commits, trees, blobs, tags and refs, plus Git LFS (https://code.storage/docs/repos/git-lfs.md). Access is over git smart HTTPS for clone, fetch and push, or through an HTTP/OpenAPI API with TS, Python and Go SDKs (https://code.storage/docs/openapi.json, https://code.storage/changelog). There are three ref spaces:
(1) The default namespace holds branches and tags. These are mirrored to GitHub when sync is on.
(2) The ephemeral namespace lives at refs/namespaces/ephemeral/refs/heads/* and is reached as repo-id+ephemeral.git. A normal clone does not show it. Code.Storage "never mirrors an ephemeral ref to an upstream host". Its branches stay until they are deleted or promoted into the default namespace with createBranch(baseIsEphemeral) (https://code.storage/docs/repos/ephemeral-branches.md, https://code.storage/docs/repos/ref-policies.md).
(3) Notes live at refs/notes/commits plus custom refs/notes/* streams such as reviews, ci or agents/verdicts. Custom streams arrived on Sep 23, 2026 (https://code.storage/changelog/custom-notes-refs).
Commits can be written without a clone. createCommit takes a streamed commit pack, and createCommitFromDiff applies a patch (https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt). Content format and path layout are up to the customer: "Your product chooses the paths and file format" (https://code.storage/docs/guides/agent-memory.md). Agent state is modelled as one ephemeral session branch per session, one commit per state, and a "pointer" of {repositoryId, sha, path} passed between services (https://code.storage/docs/guides/capture-agent-state.md).
multi_writer_and_merge:
Concurrency is optimistic, with compare-and-swap on refs.
- Commit writes take expectedHeadSha. A stale head returns a conflict, and the guide says to reload the current files and re-apply the change: "Do not send the old file content again" (https://code.storage/docs/guides/agent-memory.md).
- Notes writes take expectedRefSha (https://code.storage/docs/repos/git-notes.md).
- Merges run on the server, with strategies including squash, and previewMerge reports conflicts without committing (https://code.storage/changelog). Without expectedTargetSha, a merge retries stale target updates internally. Each retry merges the same pinned source commit against the latest target tip. Responses carry conflict_type (merge_conflict, target_moved or repo_changed), conflict_paths and merge_base_sha. Real conflicts return 409. Automatic retry applies only to native targets, not GitHub-backed ones (https://code.storage/changelog/concurrent-merge-retries).
The recommended pattern is a writer-per-branch split: sessions/{sessionId} or one ephemeral branch per attempt, each sandbox holding a short-lived token whose ref policy lets it fast-forward only its own branch (https://code.storage/docs/guides/capture-agent-state.md, https://code.storage/docs/guides/parallel-attempts.md). If a second sandbox wrote first, the restore guide says to stop the old sandbox rather than retry (https://code.storage/docs/guides/restore-agent-state.md). Marketing claims "30+ concurrent writes" per repo (https://code.storage). With two-way GitHub sync, "Code Storage sends all pushes directly to GitHub. It then copies all changes back", and it "treats GitHub as the source of truth" (https://code.storage/docs/repos/github-sync.md).
realtime: Near real time, through push notification by webhook. There is no streaming or subscription protocol. Webhook events are push, repo.sync.started, repo.sync.succeeded and repo.sync.failed. Each is signed with HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp + "." + payload and sent in the X-Pierre-Signature header. The docs mention "automatic retries" but give no delivery guarantee, retry count or latency figure (https://code.storage/docs/repos/webhooks.md). The "live diffs" guide renders a branch as a diff "with refresh capability", which reads as polling or re-fetching rather than a push stream; I only saw that guide through the docs index, not in full (https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt). GitHub sync is asynchronous, and reads may be stale until repo.sync.succeeded fires (https://code.storage/docs/repos/github-sync.md). Poke reports 90 ms p95 push latency (https://code.storage/changelog/poke-case-study).
search_retrieval:
Search is pattern search on the server, without a clone. There is no semantic or full-text index.
- repos.grep runs a regex or literal pattern at one ref, with path prefixes, include/exclude globs, extension filters, case sensitivity and context lines. Output is capped at 2000 lines and 200 matches per file, flagged with incomplete_results, paginated by cursor, and cached (X-Cache HIT/MISS). The docs name no regex engine and no index (https://code.storage/docs/api/repos/grep.md).
- "Repository Search" is only a case-insensitive substring match on repository URLs (https://code.storage/changelog/repo-search).
- Other retrieval tools: getFileStream (range and conditional requests), getArchiveStream with file patterns (tar.gz), listFiles and listFilesWithMetadata, listCommits with a path filter, getCommitDiff, getBranchDiff, blame, and notes get / refs list (https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt).
Agent memory is loaded by pinning a SHA and then using getArchiveStream with globs such as notes/** (https://code.storage/docs/guides/agent-memory.md). I found no cross-repo content search or ranking documented.
links_sessions_to_code:
Only by convention. Nothing is built in for prompts or transcripts. The guides tie a session to code state in four ways:
(a) Pin the branch's commit SHA "with the agent session" before reading memory (https://code.storage/docs/guides/agent-memory.md).
(b) Give each session its own branch, sessions/{sessionId} or an ephemeral one, with one commit per state.
(c) Store the repo ID, branch and head SHA in the customer's own backend session record (https://code.storage/docs/guides/capture-agent-state.md, https://code.storage/docs/guides/restore-agent-state.md).
(d) Attach agent verdicts, review state or rewards to a commit as git notes in custom refs/notes/* streams (https://code.storage/docs/repos/git-notes.md, https://code.storage/changelog/custom-notes-refs).
Commit messages in the examples are generic, for example 'Save session state' (https://code.storage/docs/guides/capture-agent-state.md). The service does not model prompt-to-commit provenance.
scale:
All of these are vendor claims; I found no independent verification.
- Service: unlimited storage, repos and request rates; "500+/s/repo" git requests; "15k+/s" API requests observed; 32 TB maximum repo size; "30+ concurrent writes"; 99.99% SLA (https://code.storage).
- Launch post: "Millions of new repos a day" and read/write "~60x faster than similar S3/R2 based solutions" (https://code.storage/changelog/introducing-code-storage).
- Lovable: 8M new repos a week, 250/s peak repo creation, 15k/s peak operations, and claimed improvements of 230% in p50 fetch latency and 160% in push latency (https://code.storage/changelog/lovable-case-study).
- Poke: 40k/min peak git operations, 2k/min peak repo creation, 90 ms p95 push (https://code.storage/changelog/poke-case-study).
- A Hacker News commenter noted CDN presence only in us-east and eu-central (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46957629).
- Funding: $22M Series A from CRV and 01A, announced Nov 12, 2025 (https://code.storage/changelog/funding).
privacy_security:
Auth uses JWTs signed by the customer. The browser generates an ECDSA P-256 key pair, Pierre keeps only the public key, and ES256, ES384, ES512 and RS256 are accepted. "Anyone with the private key can sign tokens for your organization." Restricted keys enforce a scope allowlist and a maximum token lifetime of 3600 s. Deleting a key revokes every token it signed (https://code.storage/docs/platform/authentication.md). Scopes are git:read, git:write, repo:write and org:read, and git:write does not imply read (https://code.storage/docs/repos/access.md). Ref policies sit in an ordered `refs` JWT claim and support no-push, no-force-push and verify-sig per ref pattern, covering branches, tags, notes and ephemeral refs (https://code.storage/docs/repos/ref-policies.md). Commit signatures (OpenPGP or SSH) can be verified (https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt). Webhooks are HMAC-SHA256 signed (https://code.storage/docs/repos/webhooks.md). The homepage claims SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, per-tenant deployments, "encryption", fine-grained audit logs and annual penetration tests (https://code.storage). The changelog lists SOC 2 improvements as still upcoming (https://code.storage/changelog). Neither the homepage nor the DPA names an encryption algorithm, and the DPA says only "data encryption" (https://code.storage/legal/dpa).
Gaps I could find:
- No redaction, secret scanning or client-side / end-to-end encryption is documented anywhere in the docs index (https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt).
- The service reads plaintext: grep, diff, blame and merge all run on its servers.
- Git URLs carry the JWT in userinfo (https://t:JWT@org.code.storage/repo.git), so credentials can leak through logs and process listings (https://code.storage/docs/repos/ephemeral-branches.md).
- Deleting a ref does not purge objects: "Git objects remain available while another ref can reach them" (https://code.storage/docs/guides/parallel-attempts.md). The docs therefore advise a separate repo when data "needs its own access rules, storage lifetime, or delete boundary" (https://code.storage/docs/guides/agent-memory.md).
license: The hosted service is proprietary and commercial. Plans: Starter from $20/mo, Scale from $200/mo, Enterprise custom. Storage costs $0.005/GB/hr hot and $0.0002/GB/hr cold, plus $0.06/GB ingress and $0.15/GB egress (https://code.storage/pricing). The SDKs (github.com/pierrecomputer/sdk) and Pierre's open-source repos are Apache-2.0 (https://github.com/pierrecomputer).
lesson_for_parinn:
Code.Storage confirms that git works as the storage and transport backend for agent state at very large scale. What it sells beyond plain git is a set of server-side rules that a plain git host cannot express for custom refs:
- Compare-and-swap on every ref update (expectedHeadSha / expectedRefSha).
- Exactly one writer per ref: one session branch per session, written only by a sandbox token whose ref policy allows fast-forwarding its own branch and nothing else.
- A hidden ref namespace (refs/namespaces/ephemeral/*) that never syncs to GitHub.
- Separate notes streams (refs/notes/<stream>) for metadata about a commit.
ParleyInn can copy that shape without the service and without a network dependency in its core:
- Give each agent session's hash-chained log its own fast-forward-only ref in a private namespace, such as refs/parinn/<agent>/<session>. Then concurrent writers never contend, and an append-only chain maps directly onto no-force-push, enforced on the server or by a verifying receiver.
- Link code to sessions with a dedicated refs/notes/parinn stream rather than commit trailers.
- Follow Code.Storage's own deletion advice: keep session history in a separate repo or object store from the code. In git, the delete or redaction boundary is the repository, because objects stay reachable from other refs.
The counter-lesson: Code.Storage is a provider that reads plaintext (grep, diff and merge all run on its servers) and offers no redaction or client-side encryption. Under ParleyInn's I2/I4 model, any such forge can only be an optional, out-of-core transport. ParleyInn would have to redact and, ideally, encrypt records before they leave the machine, and would have to treat anything fetched back as untrusted.

name: Coder Agents (successor to Coder Tasks), the Chats API and chatd inside coderd
category: Self-hosted agent platform (the agent loop runs in the control plane, workspaces are only compute)
status: shipped. The docs labelled Coder Agents 'early access' in v2.32 and v2.33 and 'beta' in v2.34 to v2.36. From v2.37 the label is gone, and the latest tag is v2.37.3 (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/v2.34.0/docs/manifest.json, https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/v2.37.3/docs/manifest.json, https://github.com/coder/coder/tags). The older 'Coder Tasks' is superseded and archived. In Tasks the agent ran inside the workspace through AgentAPI, and its state lived in a workspace state file. The v2.37.3 docs say Tasks is 'deprecated as of Coder v2.36 and is no longer available by default'. Docs on main say 'deprecated in Coder v2.34 and has been removed, including the Tasks API', so the two sources disagree on the version. On main, migration 000594 drops the tasks, task_snapshots and task_workspace_apps tables. That migration is not yet in tag v2.37.0, so it is unreleased as of 2026-10-02 (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/tasks-to-chats-migration.md, https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/database/migrations/000594_drop_task_tables.up.sql). The old URL https://coder.com/docs/ai-coder/tasks now serves Coder Agents content. The chatd code still lives under coderd/x/, Coder's experimental package path.
what_is_stored:
Conversations ('chats') and everything around them (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/database/dump.sql):
- **Chat metadata** (table chats): owner, organization, workspace_id, build or agent id, parent_chat_id and root_chat_id for sub-agents, status, title, labels, project, pin order, plan mode, model config, sharing ACLs (user_acl, group_acl), last_error, retry_state, the summary of the last turn, and versioning fields (snapshot_version, history_version, queue_version, generation_attempt).
- **Messages** (chat_messages): one row per user, assistant, system or tool message. Each row has a role, JSONB content (typed parts: text, reasoning, tool-call, tool-result, file, file-reference, skill, source, context-file, hook-context, hook-notice, workspace-file-reference), a visibility of user, model or both, token counts (input, output, reasoning, cache), cost in micros, runtime_ms, provider_response_id, reasoning effort, a compressed flag, a deleted flag, created_by, revision, and a tsvector for full-text search (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/reference/api/schemas.md).
- **Queued follow-ups** (chat_queued_messages).
- **Uploaded files as bytea blobs** (chat_files, chat_file_links).
- **Pinned copies of workspace context** (chat_context_resources): instruction files, skills and MCP config, each with a sha256 content_hash. The chat also stores an aggregate hash so drift can be detected.
- **Git/PR status per chat** (chat_diff_statuses): remote origin, branch, PR URL, number, title, state, additions and deletions, commits, approval.
- **Optional debug traces** (chat_debug_runs and chat_debug_steps): the normalized LLM request and response, usage, retries and errors.
- **Runner leases** (chat_heartbeats).

Compaction summaries are stored as new messages with compressed=true. Earlier messages 'remain in the database and are still visible to users' but are left out of the model's context (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/architecture.md). Code itself is not stored: 'The workspace file system is the source of truth for code' (same source).
where_stored: Server/cloud, self-hosted: the PostgreSQL database of the Coder control plane (coderd), not the workspace. The docs say 'All chat state is stored in the Coder database, not in the workspace', so history survives when a workspace is stopped, rebuilt or deleted (https://coder.com/docs/ai-coder/tasks, https://coder.com/docs/ai-coder/agents/architecture). The schema enforces this: chats.workspace_id is a foreign key with ON DELETE SET NULL, while messages, files and diff statuses are ON DELETE CASCADE from chats (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/database/dump.sql). Streaming partial output is held only in an in-memory buffer on each replica, capped at 1 MB per 'episode' and garbage-collected about 15 s after the episode closes (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/x/chatd/ARCHITECTURE.md). Neither git nor the workspace filesystem holds any history.
format_and_model:
Relational rows plus JSONB. No files and no log format (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/database/dump.sql).
- **Message identity:** a global bigint sequence, chat_messages.id.
- **Fencing by state machine:** chatd defines one 'core state machine' (chatstate/machine.go) that every write must go through (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/x/chatd/ARCHITECTURE.md). Each transition locks the chat row and allocates a new chats.snapshot_version. Database triggers then stamp chat_messages.revision with that version and set chats.history_version, and they raise an exception if application code assigns revision or changes chat_id.
- **Episodes:** generation work is identified by the tuple (chat_id, history_version, generation_attempt), so stale work can be rejected.
- **Not append-only:** EditMessage 'marks the truncated active-history suffix as deleted, inserts the replacement turn', a soft delete through the deleted flag. Retention later hard-deletes archived chats.
- **No hash chain or signatures.** Content hashes exist only for pinned context resources (sha256), not for messages.
- **Interchange:** the REST/WebSocket Chats API at /api/v2/chats. Debug runs export as JSON (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/platform-controls/chat-debug-logging.md).
multi_writer_and_merge:
There is one durable writer per chat and no merge (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/x/chatd/ARCHITECTURE.md, https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/chat-sharing.md, https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/tasks-to-chats-migration.md).
- **Ownership:** each chat has one owner. The Chats API has 'no owner override'.
- **Sharing is read-only:** viewers 'cannot send or edit messages'. Only top-level chats can be shared, and admins can disable sharing.
- **Concurrency between replicas:** every coderd replica runs a chat worker. Workers race to acquire runnable chats using row locks. Leases are rows in an UNLOGGED chat_heartbeats table, renewed every 9 s and stale after 30 s, so a crashed replica's chats are re-acquired. Stale leases are never revived.
- **Owner input while busy:** follow-ups from the owner during a running turn are queued with a position and promoted in order.
- **Conflicts:** a conflicting state is rejected through snapshot_version fencing, never merged.
- **Sub-agents** are child chats (parent_chat_id, root_chat_id), each with its own context window. Their results come back through tools (wait_agent, message_agent), not through merging history (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/architecture.md).
- **Code changes** reach the shared state only through git operations inside the workspace (commit, push, PR). Coder does not merge code itself.
realtime:
Yes, for clients of one deployment (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/tasks-to-chats-migration.md, https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/x/chatd/ARCHITECTURE.md).
- **WebSocket stream:** GET /api/v2/chats/{chat}/stream sends events of type message_part, message, status, error, retry and queue_update. Clients reconnect with after_id to skip what they already have. GET /api/v2/chats/watch pushes events for all of a user's chats. The old Tasks API used HTTP polling instead.
- **Notifications:** internally, Postgres pubsub (pg_notify, https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/database/pubsub/pubsub.go) carries a global chat:ownership channel and a per-chat chat:update:{chat_id} channel. Notifications are 'post-commit, best-effort, and versioned via the snapshot_version field'. Receivers 'must tolerate duplicates, drops, and reordering' and discard anything at or below their per-chat watermark, then re-read the database.
- **Cross-replica relay:** when the stream endpoint and the owning worker sit on different replicas, the endpoint connects to the owner's /stream/parts endpoint and relays live parts. Parts are numbered by seq within an episode.
- **Shared viewers** can also 'stream live updates' (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/chat-sharing.md).
- **Not cross-deployment:** there is no federation or sync between deployments.
search_retrieval:
Search covers chat lists only (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/chat-search-syntax.md, https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/database/dump.sql).
- **Filters:** the q parameter on GET /api/v2/chats takes key:value filters: title, archived, has_unread, status, pr_status, pr, diff_url, repo, pr_title, source (created_by_me or shared_with_me), and search.
- **Full-text search:** search: uses PostgreSQL full-text search through websearch_to_tsquery. Message content gets English stemming; titles get none. There is no fuzzy, semantic or prefix matching, and results have no snippets. Message content becomes searchable 'usually within 10 minutes', because a background job fills chat_messages.search_tsv over a partial GIN index. Only user and assistant text parts that are user-visible and not deleted are indexed; tool calls and results are not.
- **Retrieval:** GET /api/v2/chats/{chat}/messages returns the whole history. Debug runs are listed per chat, up to the 100 newest.
- **The agent cannot search past chats:** there is no tool that pulls cross-chat history into the model. Context within a chat is managed by automatic and manual compaction (/compact) and by /clear (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/architecture.md).
links_sessions_to_code:
Sessions are linked at the level of remote, branch and PR, not commits. No commit trailers or notes are written.
- **Storage:** the table chat_diff_statuses is keyed by (chat_id, git_remote_origin, git_branch). It holds the PR URL, number, title, state, draft flag, author, base and head branch, additions and deletions, changed files, commit count, approval and reviewer count (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/database/dump.sql).
- **Capture through the credential request:** when git in the workspace asks the control plane for an external-auth token (GET /api/v2/workspaceagents/me/external-auth), the agent passes the query parameters git_branch, git_remote_origin and optionally chat_id. coderd then calls gitSyncWorker.MarkStale to record the ref (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/workspaceagents.go).
- **Refresh:** a gitsync worker resolves the PR through the GitHub or GitLab API, using the chat owner's linked OAuth token, with a TTL of 120 s and short backoff right after a push (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/x/gitsync/gitsync.go, https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/x/gitsync/worker.go, https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/platform-controls/git-providers.md).
- **Uses:** the link powers GET /chats/{chat}/diff, the diff viewer, and the search filters pr:, repo: and pr_status:.
- **Attribution:** 'Every action the agent takes — PRs opened, code committed, commands executed — is tied to the user who submitted the prompt… There is no shared bot account', because pushes use the user's Coder external auth (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/architecture.md).
- **Not verified:** whether commit messages carry any chat identifier. A grep of chatd for 'co-authored' and 'trailer' found nothing.
scale:
No numbers are published for chat volume or database size. The architecture doc only says control-plane overhead is 'minimal', because inference runs at the provider and builds run in workspaces (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/architecture.md). Concrete limits:
- **Licensing:** a Community license allows 5 concurrently active agents per deployment, and more are queued. Premium is metered in 'Agent Time', which is reported hourly to tallyman-prod.coder.com (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/licensing-usage.md).
- **Attachments:** 50 per chat by default (CODER_CHAT_MAX_ATTACHMENTS_PER_CHAT), and the oldest are evicted. The streaming part buffer holds 1 MB per episode (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/x/chatd/ARCHITECTURE.md). Image uploads go up to 10 MB (https://coder.com/docs/ai-coder/tasks).
- **Hooks:** at most 256 concurrent hook dispatches per replica (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/admin/setup/chat-lifecycle-hooks.md).
- **Cleanup:** retention and auto-archive run in batches of 1,000 rows or root chats per tick.
- **Availability:** multiple replicas, with lease failover at 30 s.
privacy_security:
**Credentials and isolation:**
- LLM provider keys live only in the control plane: 'The workspace never sees them'. Workspaces can be cut off from the network except for the control plane and the git host (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/architecture.md).
- The workspace daemon only dials out. Tools run over the existing Tailnet tunnel through the workspace daemon's HTTP API.
- The agent has exactly the prompting user's permissions and can only touch workspaces that user owns.
- Admins set models, the system prompt and the tool configuration centrally.

**Encryption at rest:**
- dbcrypt (AES-256-GCM) covers only OAuth tokens, user_secrets, git SSH keys and crypto keys (https://coder.com/docs/admin/security/database-encryption). It does not cover chat_messages or chat_files content. The schema has no key_id column for them, so it is inferred that conversation content sits in plaintext Postgres.
- MCP server headers attached to a chat are encrypted with dbcrypt when a key is set (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/database/dump.sql).

**Redaction:**
- Redaction exists only for debug traces. It removes Authorization, Cookie and API-key headers and JSON keys matching secret, password, credential or token-like names (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/coderd/x/chatd/chatdebug/redaction.go). Debug logging is off by default, its data is kept 30 days, and the docs warn that it 'may contain sensitive content' (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/platform-controls/chat-debug-logging.md).
- Chat messages themselves are not redacted.

**Access and audit:**
- The architecture doc says 'An administrator can inspect any chat for audit or debugging'. The debug-logging doc, however, says admins get no blanket access to other users' debug data.
- Audit logs track chat metadata (title, owner, workspace, ACLs, archived) but not message content (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/admin/security/audit-logs.md).

**Retention:** archived chats are purged after 30 days by default, and 0 keeps them forever. Auto-archive is off by default (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/platform-controls/chat-retention.md).

**Experimental lifecycle hooks:**
- Hooks send HS256-JWT-signed webhooks that are body-bound with sha256 and fail closed. A policy can deny or rewrite prompts and tool inputs, and rewritten calls are marked 'Modified by policy'.
- Coder rejects tool input with duplicate or case-varying keys, to block policy-bypass parsing tricks.
- Hook model_context is stored with model-only visibility (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/admin/setup/chat-lifecycle-hooks.md).

**Prompt-injection exposure:** workspace instruction files, skills and .mcp.json are automatically hydrated into context, with only their hashes pinned. No trust labelling of recalled or repository content is documented.
license: AGPL-3.0 for the coder/coder repository, which includes coderd/x/chatd (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/LICENSE). Some features, such as Agent Firewall, are premium. Coder Agents itself runs on a Community license with a limit of 5 concurrent agents. Premium buys pooled Agent Time and requires usage reporting to Coder's Tallyman server and Metronome (https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/docs/ai-coder/agents/licensing-usage.md).
lesson_for_parinn:
Keep the durable record and the real-time channel separate. Treat notifications as lossy hints, never as the source of truth.

**How Coder does it:** chatd advances a monotonic per-chat snapshot_version inside each committed transition and publishes only that version. Notifications are post-commit and best-effort, and receivers 'must tolerate duplicates, drops, and reordering'. Each receiver keeps a watermark and re-reads the durable rows when it sees a newer version. Clients resume with after_id.

**For ParleyInn:** the record can stay local, append-only and hash-chained. Any sharing transport — a git push or fetch of the record, a p2p log, or a relay — then only has to carry '(session, head seq or hash)' hints that peers can drop or duplicate safely. That fits I4 (the core never talks to the network) and I10 (everything derived can be rebuilt from the record).

**A second, cheap idea:** Coder links sessions to code by piggy-backing on the git credential request. That request already carries the remote, branch and chat_id, and the PR is resolved later. A local credential-helper or pre-push hook in ParleyInn could record the same (session, remote, branch, HEAD) event without opening a network path.

**What ParleyInn should do better:**
- Coder's history is mutable: edits soft-delete a suffix, retention hard-deletes chats, there is no hash chain, and content is not encrypted.
- It lives only in a central database, so it does not help with offline or ephemeral sandboxes, which can be offline.
- Workspace instruction files flow into the prompt with no trust boundary. ParleyInn's I2 envelope (recalled content is always wrapped as untrusted) would be the differentiator.

name: Cognee (topoteretes/cognee)
status: shipped. Actively developed: v1.6.1 was released 2026-09-24, pyproject.toml on main reads 1.6.2, and the newest commit I cloned is dated 2026-10-01. The repo is not archived and has about 31.3k stars (https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee). One correction to the discovery note: Kuzu is no longer the default graph store. Commit 1cd7bc55b 'feat(graph): replace kuzu with ladybug' (2026-05-02) made Ladybug the default. Ladybug is MIT-licensed and says it was 'formerly known as Kuzu' (https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug). Kuzu itself was archived on 2025-10-10 (https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu).
what_is_stored: Cognee stores four kinds of data. (1) Ingested data and its metadata: documents, chunks, summaries, extracted entities and relationships. Each is a Pydantic 'DataPoint', and every graph node has a matching embedding (https://www.cognee.ai/blog/fundamentals/how-cognee-builds-ai-memory). (2) Session memory: one SessionQAEntry per turn, keyed by (user_id, session_id). Its fields are time, qa_id, question, context, answer, feedback_score and used_graph_element_ids. Agent traces and usage logs are kept too (https://docs.cognee.ai/core-concepts/sessions-and-caching). (3) Provenance, which has three independent mechanisms: per-node source_* stamps (default 'lightweight'), an edge-evidence table linking each edge to the chunk that supports it (on by default), and an opt-in 'append-only, hash-chained provenance_entries' audit ledger (PROVENANCE_TRACKING=false by default). Ledger rows follow PROV-O and carry checksum, previous_checksum, sequence_id, source_quote, agent_id and lineage fields (.env.template and cognee/modules/provenance/models/ProvenanceEntryRow.py in the repo). (4) From the Claude Code plugin: user prompts, tool traces (Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Agent) and assistant responses. At SessionEnd these are synced into the permanent graph (https://docs.cognee.ai/integrations/claude-code).
where_stored: A local DB by default; server or cloud storage is optional. All defaults are embedded files under <system_root>/databases. The graph default is 'ladybug' (cognee/infrastructure/databases/graph/config.py). It keeps using an existing cognee_graph_kuzu directory, so upgrading users do not silently get an empty graph. Vectors default to 'lancedb' and relational data to 'sqlite' (vector/config.py, relational/config.py). The session cache defaults to SQLite cache.db, with Postgres, Redis, filesystem (diskcache) and 'tapes' as alternatives (.env.template). The tapes backend mirrors each QA to an external append-only Merkle-DAG ingest server, papercomputeco/tapes. Server-backed options include Neo4j (including one Docker container per dataset for Community edition), Neptune, Postgres graph and pgvector, Turso/libSQL, plus community adapters for Qdrant, Weaviate, Milvus and Chroma (.env.template). In local mode the Claude Code plugin buffers data in ~/.cognee-plugin/claude-code/ and syncs it to a local Cognee API on localhost:8011. In cloud mode it posts over HTTP to a managed endpoint, Cognee Cloud (https://docs.cognee.ai/integrations/claude-code). Code-graph snapshots go into <repo>/.enola/ (https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee-integrations/tree/main/integrations/claude-code). Git is not used to store or transport memory.
format_and_model: The data model has three parts: a property graph (Cypher on Ladybug, Kuzu or Neo4j), a vector index with one embedding per node, and relational tables managed through SQLAlchemy and Alembic. The unit of data is the DataPoint, a Pydantic model that declares which fields get embedded (https://www.cognee.ai/blog/fundamentals/how-cognee-builds-ai-memory). The pipeline runs add → cognify → memify/improve. Cognify chunks the input and runs LLM structured extraction, or a local GLiNER2 'demo' extractor, to produce entities and edges. It can optionally ground them against an OWL ontology (.env.template). Session cache rows hold a JSON or JSONB payload with seq, user_id, session_id, qa_id, created_at and expires_at (cognee/infrastructure/databases/cache/sql/tables.py). The provenance ledger uses ISO-8601 strings for all timestamps so that recomputed hashes stay stable across dialects (ProvenanceEntryRow.py). The graph is derived by LLM extraction, so it is not a lossless transcript.
multi_writer_and_merge: Cognee does not merge histories the way a VCS does. Concurrency comes from database locking and a central API server. Opening embedded Ladybug takes an exclusive on-disk file lock. Cognee runs the graph and LanceDB in subprocess workers held in an LRU cache, and documents a known limitation: a worker holding the lock blocks a new one (cognee/infrastructure/databases/graph/get_graph_engine.py). Two optional flags, SHARED_KUZU_LOCK and SHARED_LADYBUG_LOCK, add cross-process locks for the embedded graph (.env.template). A semaphore-backed dataset queue limits how many datasets are processed at once. For real multi-writer, multi-machine use, the docs point to server databases (Postgres, Neo4j, Redis) behind the Cognee API. Logical merging works through deterministic entity IDs: entity ids are 'globally deterministic (name-derived uuid5s)', so the same entity name upserts into one node. The ledger prefixes ids with the dataset id so tenants cannot overwrite each other (cognee/tasks/provenance/record_provenance.py). Conflicting facts are not resolved. When the opt-in CONTRADICTION_DETECTION is on, an LLM check records them as 'contradicts' edges. A memify stage consolidates entity descriptions (.env.template). Multi-tenancy is on by default (ENABLE_BACKEND_ACCESS_CONTROL=True), which creates one isolated database per user and dataset (.env.template).
realtime: Partly real-time. A session write is visible to the next query in the same session, and the last 10 entries are injected into prompts. The Redis and Postgres cache backends are shared across processes and machines, while SQLite and filesystem stay local to one instance (https://docs.cognee.ai/core-concepts/sessions-and-caching). Moving data into the permanent graph is batch work: cognify, improve() or distill_session run after remember() or at the plugin's SessionEnd hook, with debounce knobs IMPROVE_DEBOUNCE_ENTRIES and IMPROVE_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS and 'no timer' (.env.template). I found no documented pub/sub or change feed for other agents. Not verified beyond the docs.
search_retrieval: Retrieval is hybrid: vector similarity combined with graph traversal. Search types include CHUNKS, RAG_COMPLETION, graph-completion and session-aware completion. With no LLM key, recall() falls back to CHUNKS (.env.template; docs/recall-vs-search.md in the repo). Optional extras include triplet embeddings, edge-evidence citations (include_references), per-user preference personalization and feedback-weighted ranking. The Claude Code plugin recalls dataset-scoped context on every UserPromptSubmit and injects it under an '=== Cognee memory ===' header. On PreToolUse it injects deterministic code-graph facts about the file being read: symbols with line numbers, calls and imports (https://docs.cognee.ai/integrations/claude-code). The default local embedding model is fastembed BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (.env.template).
links_sessions_to_code: Only weakly. The Claude Code plugin keys sessions to the Claude Code conversation ID by default; COGNEE_SESSION_ID overrides it (https://docs.cognee.ai/integrations/claude-code). The plugin also offers a COGNEE_SESSION_STRATEGY of per-directory, git-branch or static. It indexes the repository into a separate deterministic code graph, a 'codebase-<repo>-<digest>' dataset built by the enola pipeline with no LLM calls, and re-indexes after any turn that changed the working tree (https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee-integrations/tree/main/integrations/claude-code). It uses that graph to inject file context before Reads. I found no documentation that it records commit SHAs, links turns to commits, or writes anything into git. Unverified beyond those docs.
scale: No concrete scale figures were found (no event counts, sizes or throughput numbers). The README points to a BEAM evaluation of conversational memory on synthetic long-context conversations scored by an LLM judge. It notes that the runs use benchmark-specific formatting, prompts and retrieval settings (README.md, cognee/eval_framework/beam/REPORT.md). The scaling levers it describes are server databases, per-dataset engines with an LRU cache (DATABASE_MAX_LRU_CACHE_SIZE=6 by default), a dataset queue, and a 'distributed' deployment directory (.env.template, repo tree). Cognee Cloud is the managed option (https://docs.cognee.ai/cognee-cloud/overview).
privacy_security:
Redaction. The Claude Code plugin skips credential paths (.env, .pem, .key, SSH, AWS and npm files). It redacts private keys, database URLs, Bearer tokens, API keys and password assignments to '[redacted:<kind>]' before storing anything. This is configurable through COGNEE_CAPTURE_DENY_PATHS and COGNEE_CAPTURE_REDACT_PATTERNS and can be switched off with COGNEE_CAPTURE_REDACT=false. Tool allow and deny lists control which tool calls are captured (https://docs.cognee.ai/integrations/claude-code).

Access control. Multi-tenant access control and per-dataset database isolation are on by default. REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATION is set to False in .env.template but is ignored while access control is on (.env.template).

Encryption. Only specific secrets are encrypted at rest: generated per-dataset Neo4j passwords (NEO4J_ENCRYPTION_KEY) and integration DSNs (AES-256-GCM). I found no at-rest encryption of the memory stores themselves (.env.template).

Prompt injection. Recalled memory is injected automatically on every prompt. The one place I found 'untrusted' framing in the core is a single label in the session-aware prompt: 'Prior assistant (untrusted retrieval guidance)' (cognee/modules/retrieval/session_aware_completion.py). The plugin docs say nothing about trust framing.

Network and telemetry. Extraction calls cloud LLMs unless local models are configured. Telemetry is on unless TELEMETRY_DISABLED is set (.env.template; cognee/shared/utils.py). The plugin's cloud mode sends captured sessions to a remote endpoint.

Integrity. The hash-chained ledger is opt-in and 'swallows all of its own errors — provenance can never break ingestion' (record_provenance.py).
license: The core is Apache-2.0 (https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee). The graph store Ladybug is MIT (https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug). The production GLiNER extractor needs an enterprise licence; the open-source one is a 'demo' (.env.template). I could not verify the cognee-integrations plugin's license from the page I fetched.

name: CommitLore
category: git-native decision records (agent decision memory built on commit trailers and git notes)
status: shipped. v1.7.2 is the latest release named in the README. The newest commit on the default branch is 2d54398, dated 2026-09-30, so the project is active. The README says "Protocol 2.0 Stable". The repo is not archived. Star counts and the repo creation date could not be fetched (the GitHub API was blocked from this session). ADR-0029 gives the creation date as 2026-07-26. The package is marked private on npm and is distributed as a pinned git checkout plus a Claude Code and Codex plugin.
what_is_stored: It stores curated decision records, not sessions. A record is a block of git trailers using a 16-key vocabulary. Decision-context keys: Limit, Ruled-out ("alternative | reason"), Warn, Blast (local/module/system), Undo (easy/costly/permanent), Certainty (firm/tentative/guess), Verified, Unverified. Identity and lifecycle keys: Record-Id (r-[a-z0-9]{6,}, random and stable across rebase or squash), Follows, Supersedes, Expires (a date or a free-text condition), Evidence (a path, path#anchor or URL), Provenance (authored/drafted/inherited <sha>/reconstructed/unknown), CommitLore-Version, plus X-<Name> extensions. The README says "Most commits should carry no record". Session transcripts and staged diffs are only read during capture. The pending-transaction file keeps their sha256 hashes (source_hashes.transcript and .diff, staged_diff_hash) and the drafted record. It does not keep the transcript itself.
where_stored: The record has two homes, both inside git: (1) the trailer block of the commit message; (2) the git notes ref refs/notes/commitlore, which mirrors records so they survive squash, amend and rebase, and receives records inherited across a squash or reconstructed from history. The spec says nothing else is authoritative. Derived and local-only state: a SQLite index at $(git rev-parse --git-path commitlore/index.db) (in practice .git/commitlore/index.db), and capture transactions under .git/commitlore/pending. A repository-wide policy lives in .commitlore-policy.json, which is committed, with an optional per-machine override in .commitlore-policy.local.json. There is no hosted backend.
format_and_model: Records use plain git trailer syntax. Parsing must go through `git interpret-trailers --parse` or an exact reimplementation of it; the spec lists 8 verified boundary cases, e.g. a paragraph mixing trailers and prose yields no trailers. Records are written in a canonical order with 2-space continuation lines, and a parse-serialize-parse round trip must give the same result. Protocol 2.0 lets one message carry several record blocks: an earlier paragraph counts as a record only if every line is a trailer and it declares a Record-Id. Note bodies use the same canonical trailer block byte for byte ("There is no second format"). The data model is a lifecycle fold over Record-Id. Supersedes retires a record from that commit onward; Expires retires it after a date, or flags it for review when the value is a condition. Follows builds decision chains. Records are graded on two axes: provenance and lifecycle (active/superseded/expired). Delivery labels them directive, claim or blocked. The SQLite index (schema v6) has three tables: trailers(key, value, value_lc, commit_sha, source, block, seq, committed_ts...); commit_paths(commit_sha, path), filled only for commits that carry records; and meta/scan_pending. An optional FTS5 trigram table serves only as a prefilter. A JSON Schema (spec/schema/record.schema.json) and fixture and contract-case suites define conformance.
multi_writer_and_merge:
Commit trailers merge the way code does: they branch, merge and clone with the commits. Squash merges lose trailers. A local `git merge --squash` is handled by the prepare-commit-msg hook, which reads SQUASH_MSG. GitHub's squash button needs a separate GitHub Action (action/preserve, run on pull_request_target), which writes Provenance: inherited records into refs/notes/commitlore under a concurrency group. Notes sync (`commitlore sync`, also run from the pre-push hook) works like this:
- It fetches the remote notes into a scratch ref, refs/notes/commitlore-remote, never onto the working ref.
- It fast-forwards when it can.
- When both sides have moved, it runs `git notes merge -s cat_sort_uniq` ("the only merge that cannot lose one") and pushes with --no-verify.
- If git refuses the merge, it writes nothing and reports 'diverged'.

The notes fetch refspec is deliberately not forced (refs/notes/*:refs/notes/*). A forced '+' refspec used to destroy unpublished local records silently (issue #417). A note merged from several writers is graded against every identity that wrote it and keeps the lowest grade. A note may not add or replace content under a Record-Id already declared in a commit message. That counts as an identity collision ('duplicate-id'), and the payload is withheld.
realtime: No. Records spread through ordinary git push and fetch of commits and refs/notes/commitlore, and the pre-push hook triggers sync. Reads are deliberately offline. Per sync.ts, nothing on the injection path or in the PreToolUse hook fetches, because "a fetch on the injection path would be felt on every edit". A fresh clone does not see notes until `commitlore init` or `doctor --fix` configures the fetch refspec.
search_retrieval: Retrieval is scoped by file path and lifecycle, not by semantic similarity. `commitlore context <path>` and the limits / ruled-out / warnings routes return only active records for commits that touched that path. A Claude Code PreToolUse hook on Read|Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit injects these records before each tool call, capped at 800 tokens by default (--budget changes it). An MCP server offers the same routes to other hosts. A Bash PreToolUse hook runs commit-guard. Text search is a case-insensitive substring match, with an optional FTS5 trigram prefilter. When the index is missing, a scan-only fallback (`--no-index`) must return the same answers. `commitlore guard` matches proposals against Ruled-out alternatives, but the project calls it an experimental advisory with 44.8% precision and 22.0% recall. `commitlore stale` lists superseded and expired records. Answers report their coverage; exit code 3 means a partial view, such as unfetched notes or a shallow clone.
links_sessions_to_code: Only indirectly, and without keeping the session. In the capture flow (`commitlore capture`, harvest, harvest-verify) an agent drafts a record from the session transcript (JSONL) and the staged diff. CommitLore then checks that every quoted piece of evidence appears character for character in the transcript or the diff. The capture doc admits this proves the quote exists, not that it supports the claim. A pending transaction binds the record to the sha256 of the transcript, the staged diff and the policy. The commit-msg hook validates the record, and it is attached to the commit. The final record keeps no session ID, prompt or transcript text, only the Evidence citations and a Provenance value. Records staged without a human reading them are stamped Provenance: drafted and can never be delivered as directives (ADR-0030).
scale: From the README and docs/evidence.md: indexed `context` lookup takes 496 ms p50 at 100k commits; the no-index scan is reported as roughly 36x slower at 10k and 175x slower at 100k. On a corpus of 10,002 records, path scoping put 2 records (335 tokens) in front of the model, against 1,004,554 tokens for injecting everything, and found both relevant records where top-k lexical search found 1 of 2. Index build time grows with the number of records, not commits. Hook overhead: 185.85 ms p50 for commit-msg and 102.40 ms p50 for the injection hook. A registered agent study measured re-proposal of rejected ideas at 2.8% (16/580) with CommitLore against 18.8% (109/579) without, using one model on constructed tasks. The project publishes its negative results too (e.g. VERDICT-M1 p=0.748, VERDICT-M4 withdrawn).
privacy_security:
- **Secrets:** a commit-msg hook scans the whole message for credential shapes and blocks the commit, because "a credential that reaches a commit message is permanent". Findings show only a redacted 4-character excerpt and the raw match is never printed. Comment lines and the scissors section are skipped to keep false positives down.
- **Injection:** records count as untrusted until graded. Content matching INJECTION_PATTERNS is withheld and served as [blocked]. The project calls this "a speed bump", not a boundary.
- **Trust modes:** in the default mode, [directive] only means the commit author string matched a repo allowlist, which anyone who can commit can forge, and the docs say so openly. Opt-in commitlore.requireSignedDirective=true also requires git signature status G plus a %GF fingerprint listed in commitlore.trustedSigner. An absent or unreadable allowlist authorizes nobody (fails closed). Drafted records are capped at claim.
- **Data flow:** no hosted backend, no encryption. Records are plaintext in git and travel with every clone or push. Once context is handed to the host agent, CommitLore no longer controls it. The squash Action runs on pull_request_target and must never execute fork code.
- **Disclosure:** private reporting through GitHub Security Advisories; only the latest release is supported.
lesson_for_parinn:
If ParleyInn ever stores or moves records through git refs, it should copy CommitLore's handling of the notes ref.
- **Fetch safely:** never use a forced '+' refspec. CommitLore's forced refspec silently destroyed unpublished records with exit code 0 (#417). Fetch the remote side into a scratch ref instead.
- **Merge conservatively:** fast-forward, or union-merge with `git notes merge -s cat_sort_uniq`. If git will not merge cleanly, write nothing and report 'diverged'.
- **Keep network off the read path:** do all sync in a separate step that cannot fail the push it runs inside, and keep the read and inject path free of network calls. This maps onto I4 (the core never talks to the network) and I9 (hooks fail open).
- **Trust after a merge:** grade a merged blob at the lowest trust of all its writers.
- **Duplicate IDs:** treat a second channel re-declaring an existing ID as a withheld collision, not an update.

Two more ideas transfer, both matching I2. Records an agent drafted and no human read can never be served as instructions. Content checked against a transcript is bound to the transcript's hash, not to its text.
license: MIT (LICENSE file; package.json "license": "MIT")

name: Conductor (Melty Labs)
category: Parallel agent workbench: a Mac app with local git-worktree workspaces, plus Conductor Cloud (shared Vercel-sandbox workspaces, multiplayer, an HTTP API and an MCP server)
status: shipped. The Mac app is at v0.89.1, released Sep 29 2026 (https://www.conductor.build/changelog.md). Conductor Cloud became generally available in 0.78.0 on Jul 30 2026 (https://www.conductor.build/changelog/0.78.0-introducing-conductor-cloud). The API and hosted MCP server are still labelled beta: "Request and response shapes may change" (https://www.conductor.build/docs/api, https://www.conductor.build/docs/api/mcp). The OpenAPI file marks its endpoints x-conductor-stability "experimental" (https://api.conductor.build/v0/openapi.json).
license: Proprietary and closed source. The vendor is Melty Labs (footer of https://www.conductor.build/blog/series-a). The Customer Terms define "Conductor IP" that customers must return or destroy on termination (https://www.conductor.build/markdown/terms). HN users complain that it is not open source (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44594584). I could not confirm that no source repository exists, because GitHub code search was blocked in this environment. Pricing: Free (local only), Pro $50/mo, Teams $60/user/mo, Enterprise custom (https://www.conductor.build/markdown/pricing).
what_is_stored:
(1) Code. Each workspace is one git worktree on one branch. The branch is what gets reviewed and turned into a PR (https://www.conductor.build/docs/concepts/workspaces-and-branches, https://www.conductor.build/docs/concepts/git-worktrees).
(2) Chat and session history: user prompts, agent output, tool calls and metadata. Each AI response shows its duration, start and end time, model name and the files it changed (https://www.conductor.build/changelog/0.25.0-workspace-storage-improvements-ai-response-metadata-and-slash-commands, https://www.conductor.build/changelog/0.28.0-workspaces-page-claude-s-context-interactive-planning-keyboard-nav-and-more).
(3) Per-turn checkpoints. "Before each supported agent responds to a user message, Conductor captures the working branch state in a private Git ref" (https://www.conductor.build/docs/reference/checkpoints).
(4) A per-workspace .context directory. "Attachments, plans, and notes are automatically stored here" (https://www.conductor.build/changelog/0.28.1-context-directory-set-working-directories). It is meant for context "you want to share with multiple agents but don't want to check into git" (0.28.0 changelog), and the docs say to "Put uncommitted handoffs in .context" (https://www.conductor.build/llms-full.txt, first-workspace page). A per-workspace Notes scratchpad is shared with agents via <notes> (https://www.conductor.build/changelog/0.27.0-notes-tab-gpt-5-2-codex-more-fonts).
(5) Repository settings. .conductor/settings.toml is committed. .conductor/settings.local.toml holds machine-local values and secrets and is gitignored (https://www.conductor.build/docs/reference/scripts/share-with-teammates, https://www.conductor.build/docs/reference/environment-variables).
(6) On archive, git state is saved, including uncommitted files: "Archiving a workspace now saves uncommitted changes as a commit" (https://www.conductor.build/changelog/0.33.5-better-archiving, https://www.conductor.build/changelog/0.44.0-new-sidebar-rebuilt-composer-codex-checkpoints).
(7) Cloud only: session inputs and outputs, "the workspace state needed to run and synchronize the workspace", account data and GitHub installation data (https://www.conductor.build/docs/reference/privacy).
(8) Analytics events in PostHog, including error messages and stack traces (same privacy page).
where_stored:
It is split by plane.
Local workspaces:
- Worktrees live under ~/conductor/workspaces/<repo>/<workspace>. This location became the default in 0.25.0, replacing an in-repo .conductor directory (https://www.conductor.build/docs/concepts/git-worktrees, 0.25.0 changelog).
- Local chat history is in ~/Library/Application Support/com.conductor.app (https://www.conductor.build/docs/reference/privacy).
- Bundled Claude Code and Codex binaries are in .../com.conductor.app/bin. The underlying Claude Code and Codex transcripts stay in ~/.claude and ~/.codex, which the FAQ says to copy when migrating machines (https://www.conductor.build/docs/faq).
- Checkpoints are private git refs in the shared repository's ref store, "stored locally, separate from your working branch's Git history" (https://www.conductor.build/docs/reference/checkpoints).
- .context is an uncommitted, gitignored directory inside each worktree.
Cloud workspaces:
- Agents run in Vercel Sandbox microVMs in us-east-1 (https://www.conductor.build/docs/cloud/faq).
- Chat history and session data live on Conductor's servers (https://www.conductor.build/docs/reference/privacy). Files are mirrored to the Mac by one-way sync (https://www.conductor.build/docs/cloud/working-with-cloud-workspaces).
- The backend database is not documented. However, the /v0/sql endpoint says "Errors come back as 400s carrying the Postgres error message" and uses timestamptz columns (https://api.conductor.build/v0/openapi.json). So at least the transcript query surface is PostgreSQL.
Git hosting: GitHub only for Cloud (https://www.conductor.build/docs/cloud/faq). Session history is never written to the git remote.
format_and_model:
The local on-disk format is undocumented. I could not verify whether ~/Library/Application Support/com.conductor.app holds SQLite, JSON or something else. The checkpoint ref namespace and the commands used to build it are also undocumented. The engineering post that likely describes them (https://blog.conductor.build/checkpointing/, linked from HN at https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search?query=conductor.build) no longer resolves, and the Wayback copy could not be reached from here.
Hosted data model, from the OpenAPI document titled "Roundhouse public API" v0.0.1 (https://api.conductor.build/v0/openapi.json):
- Organization → Project (one project contains one repository) → Workspace → Session → Message.
- Workspace: {id, projectId, name, state (initializing/ready/sleeping/archived), lifecycleStep, repoUrl, createdAt, lastActivityAt, creatorId, creatorName, deepLink}. On creation it also takes branch, env map, agent (claude/codex/cursor/acp), model, effort and access.restricted (private workspace).
- Session (one chat): {id, name, model, resolvedModel, effort, fastMode, archivedAt, deepLink}.
- Message: {id, sessionId, sessionIndex (a monotonically ordered number), type (free-form string), content (untyped JSON), receivedAt}. POST accepts an optional client-supplied UUID messageId and an optional source {kind:'slack', url, label}.
- SQL view session_transcripts_view: session_id, workspace_id, transcript (described as "concise plain-text transcript of the session's conversation", i.e. a lossy derived rendering), session_title, agent_type, model, workspace_name, workspace_state, repo_url, session_created_at, transcript_updated_at, workspace_created_at, workspace_creator_id, workspace_creator_name.
- Lists paginate with limit/offset and return {data, offset, hasMore}. Transcripts are polled with after=<last message id> (https://www.conductor.build/docs/api).
Nothing describes hashing, signing or append-only guarantees. Checkpoint revert "will permanently delete all user and AI messages from the selected turn and later" (https://www.conductor.build/docs/reference/checkpoints). History is therefore mutable and destructively truncatable.
multi_writer_and_merge:
Code side:
- Plain git rules apply. Git allows a branch in only one worktree at a time, so one branch maps to one workspace. Integration happens through GitHub PRs. Conflicts are resolved by asking an agent to fix them, guided by configurable "Resolve conflicts preferences" (https://www.conductor.build/docs/concepts/git-worktrees, https://www.conductor.build/docs/reference/agent-behavior, https://www.conductor.build/docs/concepts/workflow).
- Several chats can share one workspace and branch. The checkpoint docs warn: "Exercise caution when using checkpoints if multiple chats are running in the same workspace" (https://www.conductor.build/docs/reference/checkpoints).
History side:
- Local history is never merged. It is per Mac, and moving machines means copying directories or using Migration Assistant (https://www.conductor.build/docs/faq).
- In Cloud, the server is the single source of truth. Many org members can prompt the same chat. Messages sent while the agent works are queued or "steered into the running turn" (https://www.conductor.build/docs/api). Messages are ordered by server-assigned sessionIndex (OpenAPI).
- Handoff means "Reassign to" a teammate rather than merging histories (https://www.conductor.build/docs/cloud/collaboration).
- File sync is one-way, cloud to Mac: "local changes don't sync back and may be overwritten" (https://www.conductor.build/docs/cloud/working-with-cloud-workspaces).
- Since 0.85.0, .context plans, screenshots and attachments also sync one way, cloud to Mac (https://www.conductor.build/changelog/0.85.0-sections-routines-and-a-new-model-picker).
- Workspace creation over the API is "not idempotent" (OpenAPI). The changelog records fixes for duplicate message ingestion: "Fixed a message sent to a busy cloud agent being ingested more than once" (https://www.conductor.build/changelog/0.77.0-early-access-multiplayer-api-background-tasks-performance).
There is no CRDT or offline multi-writer merge.
realtime:
Cloud: yes, for humans in the app. "The transcript and new agent output update live for everyone", with presence avatars and typing indicators (https://www.conductor.build/docs/cloud/collaboration). Agents keep running after the laptop closes, until the sandbox sleeps after 4 hours idle or hits its hard lifetime of 23h50m. "Files and chat history survive sleep" (https://www.conductor.build/docs/cloud/working-with-cloud-workspaces).
API and MCP: no push or streaming of transcripts is documented. Clients poll session status and fetch new messages with ?after=<last id>. The docs suggest polling about every 15 s (https://www.conductor.build/docs/api).
Local: there is no sharing or sync at all. History stays on one Mac.
search_retrieval:
Local app:
- In-chat search with ⌘F (https://www.conductor.build/changelog/0.31.0-search-chats-add-scripts-in-the-ui-and-view-setup-script-logs).
- Workspace search by branch, repo or PR number (https://www.conductor.build/changelog/0.26.0-search-workspaces-view-files-from-chat).
