(d) If anything goes into git itself, keep it small, like Cursor's opt-out `Made with Cursor` trailer, and keep the rich record elsewhere.
license: Proprietary, closed-source commercial feature of Cursor, Enterprise plan only (https://cursor.com/docs/integrations/cursor-blame.md).
scale: Cursor makes no scale claims. The only documented limits are API paging (pageSize max 1000, CSV streamed in pages of 10,000) and the single top-level repo per workspace (https://cursor.com/docs/account/teams/ai-code-tracking-api.md).

name: Cursor Cloud Agents (formerly Background Agents)
status: shipped. Announced as "Cloud Agents" on 2025-10-30 (https://cursor.com/blog/cloud-agents). They were formerly called Background Agents (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent). Some parts are not GA. The Cloud Agents API v1 is a "public beta", and the v0 API is legacy but still available (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints). The in-VM agent metadata API is in "preview" (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/metadata). Custom retention windows are "early access for select Enterprise teams" (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network). Cursor's own git forge, Origin, which cloud agents can push to, is in "early beta" (https://cursor.com/docs/origin). The project is active: a public PR with the Cloud Agent footer was created on 2026-10-02 (https://github.com/ketheridge7/sideline/pull/78).
what_is_stored:
Cursor's security docs list four classes of data (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security):
(1) Runtime workspace: the checked-out repo, build artifacts and tool-execution context, held on the live VM.
(2) VM snapshots: point-in-time disk copies that include the cloned code.
(3) Conversation state: "Prompts, model responses, tool calls, diff context, and demo artifacts that make up the transcript".
(4) Secrets and tokens: Cloud Agent secrets, OAuth tokens and API credentials.
Other stored data:
- Per-run metadata: run ID, URL, repo, branch, model, owner, lifecycle status and source (Cursor, Slack, GitHub, API).
- Dashboard events: setup_started/completed/failed, pr_created, pr_creation_failed, artifact_created, mcp_auth_error.
- Diff metadata, environment config/version and effective egress policy, and raw setup/build logs. All of these are exposed through the built-in Cursor Cloud MCP (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities).
- Artifacts: screenshots, videos and log references, per agent (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints).
- Caller-supplied string tags (cloud.metadata) are persisted with the agent (https://cursor.com/docs/sdk/typescript).
Retention is in fact documented, contrary to the discovery note:
- Conversation history is "kept indefinitely by default".
- Snapshots are deleted after 90 days of inactivity, and each start or resume extends that window.
- The Delete Agent API removes the transcript and artifacts but not snapshots.
- Enterprise can choose "Indefinite" or "90 days" for conversations (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network).
- SSE stream backlog has its own short retention, given by the X-Cursor-Stream-Retention-Seconds header (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints).
where_stored:
server/cloud (Cursor-managed). Locations by data type:
- Transcripts and conversation state: the "Cursor backend, encrypted with per-agent keys". Snapshots: an encrypted "snapshot and cache layer outside the active VM". Secrets: "encrypted credential stores in Cursor's backend". Live workspaces: Firecracker-based microVMs in an AWS account kept apart from the rest of Cursor production (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security).
- Artifacts: S3 at cloud-agent-artifacts.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com, served by 15-minute presigned URLs (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network, https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints).
- Git (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud, Azure DevOps, or Cursor's Origin forge) holds only the code output: a pushed branch (default `cursor/...`), commits and a PR (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints, https://cursor.com/docs/origin/integrations). It does not hold the transcript.
- Self-Hosted Machines move tool execution and the checkout onto customer hardware. Cursor still runs the agent loop, and the worker sends Cursor file contents, terminal output, diffs and screenshots (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/self-hosted). It is not documented that transcripts ever stay off Cursor's servers.
- Data residency can be US-only for Cloud Agents (https://cursor.com/docs/enterprise/privacy-and-data-governance).
- By contrast, the Cursor SDK's local agents persist to on-disk SQLite or to four NDJSON files (agents, runs, run_events, checkpoints). Per the docs, "Cloud agents persist server-side" (https://cursor.com/docs/sdk/typescript).
format_and_model:
Proprietary server-side model. Only API shapes are public; the storage format is not documented.
- Entities: a durable Agent (`bc-<uuid>`, status ACTIVE/IDLE/ARCHIVED) owns many per-prompt Runs (`run-<uuid>`, status CREATING/RUNNING/FINISHED/ERROR/CANCELLED/EXPIRED). The git state `{repoUrl, branch?, prUrl?}[]` belongs to the agent, not to a run (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints).
- Transcript via the SDK: `run.conversation()` returns ConversationTurn[]. Each turn is either an agent turn (a userMessage plus steps of assistantMessage, toolCall or thinkingMessage) or a shell turn (command, stdout, stderr, exitCode). The ToolCall shape is "internal-facing" (https://cursor.com/docs/sdk/typescript).
- Transcript via the legacy REST v0: GET /v0/agents/{id}/conversation returns a flat messages[] list of {id, type: user_message|assistant_message, text} (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/v0).
- Live events are SSE: status, assistant, thinking, tool_call {callId, name, status, args?, result?, truncated?}, interaction_update, heartbeat, result, error, done. Oversized args or results are omitted and flagged as truncated (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints).
- Inside the VM, a plain-text key/value metadata tree (agent/, owner/, turn/, workspace/) is served over a Unix socket (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/metadata).
- None of this is append-only or hash-chained as far as the docs show. Transcripts can be deleted, and retention jobs remove old conversations.
multi_writer_and_merge:
The conversation is a single server-owned linear log. Concurrent writes are serialized, never merged.
- Only one run can be active per agent. A second POST /runs returns `409 agent_busy`, and a cancelled run is terminal (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints).
- Several humans can write to one conversation through admin-enabled "team follow-ups" (Disabled / Service accounts only / All). The submitter of each turn is recorded as `turn/user-id`, which can differ from `owner/user-id` (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/settings, https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/metadata).
- Cursor warns that team follow-ups let one user steer an agent that holds another user's secrets ("lateral movement and secret exposure") (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/settings).
- Subscriptions on GitHub PR or CI, Slack, Linear or timers inject events as follow-ups into the same conversation. Bursts coalesce, and a subscription lasts at most 180 days (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities).
- Code concurrency goes through git branches. The default is a new `cursor/...` branch; `workOnCurrentBranch` pushes to the given ref, and stacked agents produce several branches (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints).
- Auto-fix of CI stops when a human pushes to the branch or sends a follow-up (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities).
- Parallelism is many separate agents, each in its own VM. A conversation can also move between local and cloud: CLI messages prefixed with `&` hand off to the cloud, and the Agents Window can move an agent "from cloud to local … and back" (https://cursor.com/docs/cli/using, https://cursor.com/docs/agent/agents-window).
- No transcript merge or fork semantics are documented.
realtime:
Yes, centrally brokered by Cursor.
- Runs "stream progress, output, and artifacts back to the user" (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security).
- A per-run SSE stream resumes with Last-Event-ID; the leading status event is re-sent on every reconnect. Once the stream retention window passes, it returns `410 stream_expired`, and clients fall back to GET run (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints).
- The SDK notes that the cloud SSE backlog lets several subscribers attach late. For long runs, it suggests polling `run.conversation()` (https://cursor.com/docs/sdk/typescript).
- Teammates can open the run URL to watch the conversation, code changes and artifacts, read-only unless team follow-ups are enabled (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent).
- Remote desktop takeover is live (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities).
- Webhooks exist only in the legacy v0 API. They fire statusChange for FINISHED or ERROR and are signed with HMAC-SHA256. v1 webhooks are "coming soon" (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/webhooks, https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints).
- There is no offline or peer-to-peer mode. A 2026-05-19 forum thread reports cloud agents failing to start during an incident; Cursor staff pointed to the status page (https://forum.cursor.com/t/cloud-agents-broken-ii/161036).
search_retrieval:
Retrieval is structured by ID and filter. No full-text search over transcripts is documented.
- REST: list agents (paginated, filterable by `prUrl` and `includeArchived`), list runs, get run, list and download artifacts. Legacy v0 has GET conversation (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints, https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/v0).
- Cursor Cloud MCP, built in and on by default: `list-cloud-agents` filters by source, status, date, code changes, PR creation and archived state. `batch-fetch-details` pulls transcripts, diff metadata, setup logs, environment info and events for up to 50 runs per batch. "Related runs" are other runs in the same environment or repo.
- MCP access rules: team admins can fetch any team member's transcripts for repos and environments they can access. Non-admins see only their own (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities).
- Web UI viewing is broader than MCP access. Any team member with their own repo access can open a run URL (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent).
- Origin offers code search, not transcript search (https://cursor.com/docs/origin).
links_sessions_to_code:
Yes, but only at the PR level, and the link is a URL pointing back into Cursor.
- Agent-opened PR bodies are wrapped in `<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN/END -->` markers. A footer carries "Open in Web" (`https://cursor.com/agents/bc-<uuid>`) and "Open in Cursor" (`https://cursor.com/background-agent?bcId=bc-<uuid>`) links.
- Commits are authored `Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>`, with a `Co-authored-by:` trailer for the human. The commit message carries no run-ID trailer. I checked this on a public PR created 2026-10-02 (https://github.com/ketheridge7/sideline/pull/78 and its .patch).
- Every agent commit is signed with an HSM-backed Ed25519 key, which gives GitHub/GitLab "Verified" badges (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network).
- Reverse lookup: the API's list agents `?prUrl=` and run `git.branches[].prUrl` map a PR to its agent (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints).
- Inside the VM, `workspace/repo-url(s)` and `branch-name` tie the run to its repos (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/metadata).
- Repo `.cursor/hooks.json` hooks run in the cloud VM and receive `conversation_id`/`generation_id`, so a repo-defined recorder could capture turns there. Exceptions: sessionStart, sessionEnd and the MCP hooks do not run in the cloud, and hooks skip early read-only turns (https://cursor.com/docs/hooks). Whether `transcript_path` is populated in cloud VMs is not documented, so I could not verify it.
- Separately, Cursor publishes Agent Trace v0.1.0 (RFC, January 2026, CC BY 4.0). It is a JSON spec attributing file line ranges to a conversation URL, a model_id and a VCS revision, and it leaves storage open ("local files, git notes, a database") (https://agent-trace.dev). I could not verify that Cloud Agents emit Agent Trace records.
scale:
The docs make no volume claims. The announcement offers only qualitative scale ("run many agents at once") (https://cursor.com/blog/cloud-agents).
Documented limits:
- "as many agents as you want in parallel" (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent).
- Up to 20 repos per agent; one active run per agent; at most 5 images of 15 MB each per prompt; envVars capped at 50 (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints).
- batch-fetch-details handles 50 runs per batch; subscriptions last at most 180 days; up to 10 CI-failure follow-ups per PR (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities).
- The metadata socket allows 120 requests per minute per VM and 8 concurrent connections (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/metadata).
My own observation, not a vendor claim: a GitHub search for public PRs whose body contains "cursor.com/agents" returned total_count 1,343,797 on 2026-10-02 (https://github.com/search?q=%22cursor.com%2Fagents%22+in%3Abody+is%3Apr&type=pullrequests). That is a rough lower bound for public agent PRs carrying the footer.
privacy_security:
Encryption and isolation:
- TLS 1.2+ in transit. AES-256 at rest with per-agent keys for session data. Optional customer-managed KMS key (CMEK/BYOK) on Enterprise.
- Firecracker microVM per agent, in a separate AWS account. "Cursor employees do not have access to the code inside Cloud Agent VMs"; SOC 2 Type 2 (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security).
Secrets:
- Three types: Environment Variable (visible to the agent), Runtime Secret (loaded as an env var but replaced with `[REDACTED]` in tool results, transcript, commits and commit messages, though still visible to a human using the VM terminal) and Build Secret (Docker build only) (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network).
- MCP configs are encrypted at rest. `env`, `headers` and `CLIENT_SECRET` are write-only. HTTP MCP credentials never enter the VM because calls are proxied, whereas stdio MCP config is visible to the agent (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities).
- OIDC JWTs minted from a local socket replace long-lived cloud keys (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/identity).
- The docs admit "Cloud Agent conversations can include prompts, code, tool output, and secrets" (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities).
- Snapshots can freeze tokens, for example an .npmrc captured in a snapshot (https://infisical.com/blog/secure-secrets-management-for-cursor-cloud-agents). The docs also confirm `.env.local` is saved if present at snapshot time (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent).
Prompt injection:
- Acknowledged: agents auto-run all terminal commands. Mitigations are egress modes (allow-all, default+allowlist, allowlist-only; lockable on Enterprise), `.cursorignore`, draft PRs and hooks (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security).
- Recalled transcripts returned by Cloud MCP are ACL-checked, but no untrusted-content marking is documented (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities).
Exposure and model data:
- Opt-in artifact embedding in GitHub PRs uses "long, unguessable URLs that are viewable without authentication" (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities).
- Privacy Mode is required, and legacy Privacy Mode is not supported. Most models run under zero-data-retention agreements, with listed exceptions (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network, https://cursor.com/docs/enterprise/privacy-and-data-governance).
Audit: authentication and admin events go to audit logs, which can be streamed to a SIEM (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security).
license: Proprietary commercial SaaS. It needs a paid Cursor plan (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent) and is governed by Cursor's MSA and DPA (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security). The related Agent Trace spec is CC BY 4.0 (https://agent-trace.dev).
lesson_for_parinn:
Cursor keeps transcripts out of git, and ParleyInn probably should too. At more than a million public agent PRs, Cursor puts only a pointer in git and keeps the transcript where it can be deleted:
- Git gets signed commits authored "Cursor Agent", a Co-authored-by trailer and a PR-footer link to `bc-<uuid>`.
- The transcript sits in a backend encrypted under per-agent AES-256 keys, with a Delete Agent API and a 90-day retention option.
What ParleyInn can take from that:
- **Pointer.** Write a commit trailer carrying the session ID and the chain-head hash. Cursor's link lives only in the PR description on one forge, while a commit trailer stays with the commit.
- **Storage.** Keep the hash-chained record itself outside git.
- **Deletion.** Encrypt each session's payloads under its own key, so a delete or retention request becomes key destruction and the chain stays verifiable. This is my inference: Cursor does not document crypto-shredding.
Cursor also shows two things ParleyInn should do the other way round:
- Redact secrets when the record is written, as Runtime Secrets do, because Cursor admits transcripts carry secrets.
- Envelope recalled sessions as untrusted (I2). Cursor's Cloud MCP hands prior runs' raw transcripts back to an auto-executing agent with ACL checks only.

name: Cursor Cloud Agents (formerly Background Agents): PR artifacts (videos, screenshots, logs)
status: shipped. Cloud agents with computer use and artifacts launched on 2026-02-24 (https://cursor.com/changelog/02-24-26, https://cursor.com/blog/agent-computer-use). Posting artifacts into GitHub PRs did not work at first: a Cursor staff member said "posting artifact screenshots to GitHub is not yet supported". It shipped as an opt-in around late March 2026 (https://forum.cursor.com/t/cursor-cloud-agents-do-not-post-their-screenshots-or-videos-to-pr/152974). Related newer product: Cursor Origin, Cursor's own git forge, has been in early beta since 2026-08-17 (https://cursor.com/changelog/origin-code-hosting, https://cursor.com/docs/origin).
what_is_stored:
There are three kinds of data.
(1) Code changes go into a normal git branch and pull request on GitHub or GitLab, with commits signed by Cursor (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network).
(2) Artifacts: the agent tests its own change and produces "screenshots, videos, and log references" (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities). The help page says they are attached "to the pull request, so you can validate the work without checking out the branch" (https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/background-agents).
(3) Conversation history ("prompts, responses, tool calls") and encrypted VM disk snapshots. These stay on Cursor's side and do not go to the forge (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network).
Only the artifacts and the diff reach the PR. No primary source says the full transcript, or the prompt, is written into the PR or into git.
where_stored:
Cursor's own servers and cloud, on AWS.
- Inside the VM, the agent writes artifacts to /opt/cursor/artifacts/ (forum thread above).
- They are uploaded to Cursor-owned S3. The allowlist host is cloud-agent-artifacts.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network).
- The forge PR description holds only links to those objects, not copies.
- Conversations and environment snapshots stay in Cursor's AWS infrastructure. Code is "stored on VM disks while the agent is accessible" (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network).
- The git branch and PR live on GitHub or GitLab, or on Cursor Origin (beta).
format_and_model:
Data model, from the API (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints):
- Agent: durable metadata with id, name, status, repos, workOnCurrentBranch, autoCreatePR and latestRunId. One agent has many runs.
- Run: id, agentId, status, createdAt, updatedAt, durationMs, result, and a git object holding the branches.
- Run stream: Server-Sent Events of type status, assistant, thinking, tool_call, result, error and done.
- Artifacts: a flat list of {path, sizeBytes, updatedAt}, with paths such as artifacts/screenshot.png. A download returns a presigned S3 URL that expires after 15 minutes.

In the PR, artifacts are embedded as Markdown images or links in the PR description. They use "long, unguessable URLs that are viewable without authentication" because "GitHub's image proxy requires public URLs" (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities). Exact file formats (mp4, png and so on) and the layout of the PR body are not documented. Unverified.
multi_writer_and_merge:
Each agent runs on its own dedicated, isolated VM and branch, so many agents work in parallel without sharing state (https://cursor.com/blog/agent-computer-use, https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/background-agents). Merging is ordinary git and PR merging on the forge. Session data has no merge model: each agent's conversation is a separate, server-owned log.

Artifact embedding has a single-writer limit (forum thread above):
- URL rewriting happens only when the agent creates the PR through Cursor's ManagePullRequest tool.
- Agents cannot edit an existing PR description to add artifacts.
- Artifacts posted in PR comments, or through direct GitHub API calls, do not render.
Staff said fixing comments was planned. Whether that has shipped is unverified.

You can also aim an agent at an existing PR with prUrl, or ask for follow-ups through new runs (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints).
realtime:
Yes for live viewing on Cursor's side:
- Run events stream over Server-Sent Events (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints).
- Users can take over the agent's remote desktop (https://cursor.com/blog/agent-computer-use).
- Agents can be watched and steered from web, desktop, mobile, Slack, GitHub and Linear (https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/background-agents).
- A third-party comparison says "You see the terminal live" (https://startdebugging.net/2026/07/cursor-cloud-agents-vs-github-copilot-coding-agent-for-background-prs/).
The PR itself is not real time: artifacts are embedded once, when the PR is created. Origin is described as syncing PR comments with GitHub both ways in real time (https://cursor.com/changelog/origin-code-hosting).
search_retrieval:
You retrieve data by ID through Cursor's API:
- list runs, get a run, stream a run
- list artifacts, download an artifact through a presigned URL
(https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints)
No full-text search over agent conversations or artifacts is documented. On the forge, the artifacts are just links in the PR body, so they are only as searchable as the PR text. Origin offers code browsing and search, but no documented search over agent sessions (https://cursor.com/docs/origin).
links_sessions_to_code:
Only loosely and one way.
- The PR carries evidence (artifacts) and the diff. The docs reviewed do not say a link to the full agent conversation goes into the PR or commits.
- Cursor's side holds the forward link: a run's git object records branches, and an agent can target a prUrl (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints).
- Slack-triggered agents post the PR link back into the Slack thread (startdebugging article above). The web UI offers "Open in Cursor" handoff (https://docs.cursor.com/background-agent/web-and-mobile).
- Commits are signed with HSM-backed Ed25519 keys and show as verified (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network). That shows Cursor made the commit, but it does not bind the commit to a transcript hash.
- Origin docs do not describe linking sessions to PRs (https://cursor.com/docs/origin).
Whether PR bodies carry a back-link to the agent session could not be confirmed: GitHub-wide search was not available from this sandbox.
scale:
From Cursor's own posts:
- "More than 30% of the PRs we merge at Cursor are now created by agents operating autonomously in cloud sandboxes" (https://cursor.com/blog/agent-computer-use).
- Secondary coverage cites 35% (https://devops.com/?p=182790).
No documented numbers for artifact size or count limits, or for throughput.
privacy_security:
Source for all items unless noted: https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network.
- Secret redaction: runtime secrets are redacted to [REDACTED] from agent outputs, transcripts, commits and messages, but stay visible to someone using the terminal directly. Build secrets exist only as Docker build secret mounts. Secrets are encrypted at rest and in transit.
- Retention: conversation history is kept indefinitely by default, and you delete it with the Delete Agent API. Enterprise teams can choose "Indefinite" or "90 days". Encrypted VM snapshots are kept for 90 days of inactivity. Privacy Mode means no training on your code and code kept only while the agent runs. Legacy Privacy Mode is not supported.
- Network: four egress modes, from unrestricted to allowlist-only, plus self-hosted machines. The docs warn that the artifact upload host must be allowlisted exactly, because wildcards create an exfiltration risk.
- GitHub access: read-write via the GitHub app.
- Key weakness: artifacts embedded in PRs are public bearer URLs. "Long, unguessable URLs that are viewable without authentication" means anyone who gets the PR body, a fork, a notification email or a log can view the screenshots, videos and logs. That includes private-repo UI and data. The setting is opt-in for this reason: "Allow posting artifacts to GitHub" (https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities).
- No documented redaction pass over screenshot or video content.
lesson_for_parinn:
Treat forge PR attachments as a publishing channel, not as storage. Cursor keeps the authoritative record (transcript, tool calls, artifacts) in its own store. The PR carries only small evidence links. Because forge image proxies need public URLs, those links become unauthenticated bearer URLs, and the upload host becomes something network policy must allowlist exactly.

For ParleyInn:
- Keep the hash-chained session record off the forge.
- If anything is ever pushed to a PR, push only a content-addressed reference, such as the chain head hash and session id. Never push transcript content or a viewable URL.
- Do it through an explicit, audited, opt-in export, never automatically. This fits I2, I4 and I6.
- Make the PR reference checkable against the local record, which Cursor's signed-commit-only approach cannot do.

Cursor's limits show the fragility of the PR-body route. Only the PR's creator can embed artifacts, comments do not render them, and description edits fail. Do not build session-to-code linkage on mutable PR text. Anchor it in git objects (trailers or notes holding the hash) or in ParleyInn's own record.
confidence: medium-high for storage location, URL model, retention and redaction, which come from official docs. Medium for the details of the artifact-to-PR mechanism, which come from a staff forum post in March 2026 that may have changed since. Low for whether PR bodies link back to the agent session: not documented, and not checkable from here.
license: Proprietary commercial SaaS (Anysphere/Cursor). There is no open-source component for this feature.

name: Cursor shared transcripts and local chat store
status: shipped
what_is_stored: Full conversation history including code snippets, tool calls, results, and metadata about composer/agent sessions. Does not include local files, authentication credentials, or user identity. Shared transcripts contain redacted conversation text (best-effort pattern-based redaction of API keys, tokens, passwords). Local storage maintains session metadata (tab IDs, open/closed state, last-opened composer IDs, workspace-to-conversation mappings).
where_stored: Two-tier storage: (1) Local SQLite state.vscdb files in workspaceStorage/{id}/ (per-workspace metadata) and globalStorage/ (all message content). Platform-specific paths: macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/; Linux: ~/.config/Cursor/User/; Windows: %APPDATA%/Cursor/User/. (2) Hosted: Read-only shared transcript links on cursor.com (Teams and Enterprise plans only); can be public or team-only; users can fork shared transcripts to continue locally in their own editor.
format_and_model: SQLite database with generic key-value table (ItemTable and cursorDiskKV). Messages stored as individual large JSON objects (~40+ fields per message), keyed by pattern bubbleId:{composerId}:{bubbleId}. Metadata keys follow pattern composerData:{id}. Chronological order tracked in fullConversationHeadersOnly array within composerData, not by row order. Database size can reach 1.2GB per user. No formal schema; key naming conventions establish structure. Shared transcripts exported as JSON/text with secrets redacted.
multi_writer_and_merge: No cross-machine sync. Chat history is siloed per-workspace; each machine maintains independent state.vscdb files. No built-in multi-writer merge strategy. Shared transcripts are read-only links; users can fork to create a local copy that starts a new conversation. Community-developed workarounds include cursaves (export to git repo) and manual file synchronization. No conflict resolution or operational transformation; each workspace is independent.
realtime: Local storage updates synchronously to state.vscdb on each message. Shared transcripts are static snapshots; no real-time updates to published links. Cursor 3.11+ includes local search index across agent transcripts that scales to thousands of conversations with index maintained locally. No real-time sync between devices.
search_retrieval: Cursor 3.11 (July 2026) added Agent Transcript Search: local FTS-style index searchable via Cmd+K in Agents window, searching actual message content beyond conversation names. Cmd+F searches within single open transcript. Third-party tools (cursor-history, cursor-view) implement SQLite FTS5 for full-text search across all stored conversations. Built-in search is keyword-based; third-party tools support stemming and phrase queries. No API endpoint for remote search; all search local to client.
links_sessions_to_code: composerId uniquely identifies an agent/composer session. workspaceStorage/{id}/ establishes workspace-to-session mapping. fullConversationHeadersOnly array tracks message order within a session. Cursor indexes entire codebase semantically via Turbopuffer embeddings (vector store, not source code); chat/agent calls pull semantically relevant chunks. .cursor/rules/ directory scopes context by file glob patterns. Sessions are scoped across multiple repositories (as of Cursor 2026) and can be reused across sessions. No direct git commit or branch linking in transcript; context is semantic and file-pattern based.
privacy_security: Best-effort pattern-based secret redaction applied before sharing, covering: common API key prefixes (sk-, sk-ant-, ghp_, AKIA), Bearer tokens, password assignments, PEM private keys, JWT tokens. Redaction is not guaranteed; custom secret formats and values without recognizable prefixes may leak. Local storage: TLS 1.2+ encryption for connections to Cursor services, certificate pinning for critical services. End-to-end encryption claimed for code and chat. Privacy Mode processes code locally only, zero-retention logging, no long-term storage. Shared transcripts mask user identity but require manual review before publication (redaction is supplementary, not primary defense).
lesson_for_parinn: Cursor uses local-first SQLite with hosted read-only snapshot links—no built-in multi-agent sync or cross-device merge story. The lesson for ParleyInn: (1) pattern-based redaction has security gaps; structure trusted/untrusted boundaries instead of relying on redaction heuristics (I2). (2) No inherent hash-chaining or audit trail; Cursor cannot prove transcript integrity or detect tampering—ParleyInn's append-only hash-chained record is architecturally superior for security review (I6). (3) Local-first storage avoids network calls (I4) but requires users to manually fork and sync; ParleyInn should design multi-agent, cross-machine durability from the start if targeting distributed agents (I9). (4) bubbleId:{composerId}:{bubbleId} linking is opaque; ParleyInn's explicit session/step/event model with verifiable derivation (I10) would enable better auditability and recovery.

name: DEV Agent Sessions (Forem)
status: beta
what_is_stored: JSON/JSONL transcripts from agent coding tools (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Antigravity CLI). Each session contains an array of messages with fields: sessionId, messageId, type (user/assistant), message content, timestamp. Messages can include tool calls, file attachments, and metadata. Sessions are curated client-side before upload, allowing users to include/exclude specific message ranges.
where_stored: Forem platform (open-source community software powering dev.to), backed by PostgreSQL database. Agent sessions stored in agent_session model with curated_data JSON column containing standardized message structure. File attachments and transcript data persisted in PostgreSQL with JSONL structure within agent_session.curated_data['messages'] array.
format_and_model: JSON/JSONL with standardized message schema: {sessionId: UUID, messageId: integer (auto-assigned if missing), type: string, message: string, timestamp: ISO8601}. Messages stored as array in agent_session.curated_data JSON field. Tool type auto-detected from transcript content (tool_name: 'auto'). Rendering uses Redcarpet markdown parser via AgentSessionRenderers::MarkdownRenderer for display within ltag-agent-session DOM elements. Public URL pattern: dev.to/agent_sessions/{slug}.
multi_writer_and_merge: No multi-user editing or collaborative write support. Sessions are individually owned by uploaders. Curation workflow (client-side selection of message ranges) happens during initial upload, not continuously. API-based submissions via POST /api/agent_sessions include before_validation hook that auto-assigns message indices for sessions lacking them. No conflict resolution or merge strategy; sessions are append-only from upload perspective but curated selections are static.
realtime: No real-time collaboration or live session streaming. Sessions are static post-upload. Curation and slicing happen client-side before submission. No WebSocket or push-based updates mentioned. Embedding in articles happens after session publication (via {% agent_session <id> %} Liquid tag), but no live synchronization between embedded sessions and article content.
search_retrieval: No full-text search mechanism documented. Discovery via: (1) public URLs (dev.to/agent_sessions/{slug}), (2) dev.to article embeds that reference sessions, (3) DEV Community feed/discovery. Sessions default to private/unlisted until explicitly made public via 'Make Public' button. Client-side curation interface allows filtering during upload. Fragment linking within transcripts broken due to sanitizer stripping id attributes from headers (GitHub issue #23850). No indexing, tagging, or advanced retrieval documented.
links_sessions_to_code: No bidirectional linking to GitHub repositories, pull requests, or commits. Sessions can be embedded in DEV articles via {% agent_session <id> %} Liquid tag syntax, creating unidirectional reference. No mechanism to track which agent session produced which code change or to link discrete code modifications to their corresponding agent interactions. Users must manually curate and slurp relevant exchanges for embedding.
privacy_security: Sessions private (unlisted) by default; explicit 'Make Public' button enables sharing. Built-in redaction layer in transcript parser targets common secrets (API keys, tokens, credentials), but acknowledged as incomplete: 'will not catch every edge case.' Users bear responsibility for reviewing sensitive data before upload and not uploading data they don't own. No encryption in transit or at rest mentioned in documentation. No data deletion/retention policy specified. Sanitizer whitelist restricts attributes to 'class href target rel', stripping id, data-*, and other attributes from rendered HTML.
lesson_for_parinn: Three key insights: (1) Tool standardization essential—multiple incompatible log formats (Gemini, Claude Code, Copilot, etc.) demand unified parsing before users can interact with records; DEV's multi-parser approach shows this is necessary infrastructure, not optional polish. (2) Client-side filtering beats server limits—DEV's 10MB upload constraint forced them to move curation to browser; ParleyInn should let users filter what matters before transmission, not constrain transmission size. (3) Granular sharing is real; full sessions are not—users want to slice specific exchanges for embedding/sharing, not manage monolithic transcripts; design access controls at conversation-fragment level from start, not session level. (4) Honest redaction > false confidence—DEV's transparent acknowledgment that redaction won't catch every edge case is more trustworthy than claiming perfect secrets filtering; ParleyInn should design assuming sensitive content will slip through and focus on detection/audit rather than prevention.
sources: https://dev.to/devteam/share-embed-and-curate-agent-sessions-on-dev-beta-5bj6 — Original announcement, feature description, and use case documentation
https://github.com/forem/forem/pull/23919 — Support for Antigravity CLI agent sessions: message indexing, curated_data JSON structure, validation hooks
https://github.com/forem/forem/pull/23256 — Add OpenCode agent sessions: parser implementation, auto-detection, curation workflow, database storage approach
https://github.com/forem/forem/issues/23850 — Agent session transcripts table-of-contents fragment links: rendering architecture, sanitizer configuration, schema details
https://github.com/forem/forem — Primary source for Forem/DEV platform codebase, model definitions, migrations, and architectural decisions

name: Devin (Cognition): Devin Cloud sessions, Devin CLI /handoff and /pickup, Session Insights
category: Hosted autonomous agent (proprietary SaaS; the session record lives on the server, code goes back through git PRs)
status: shipped
license: Proprietary, closed-source SaaS. Customers own Devin's output, but may not use it to train competing models (https://docs.devin.ai/admin/security.md). The cross-agent Devin Handoff plugin/skill (works in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) is MIT (https://github.com/club-cog/devin-handoff). Cognition also publishes an open-source Outposts Kubernetes operator, devin-outpost-k8s (https://docs.devin.ai/cloud/outposts/overview.md); I did not verify its license.
what_is_stored:
CLOUD SESSION: a server-side session object. Fields: session_id (`devin-` + 32 hex), status (new/claimed/running/exit/error/suspended/resuming) plus status_detail, title, tags, origin (webapp/slack/teams/api/linear/jira/automation/cli/desktop/code_scan), parent_session_id/child_session_ids, playbook_id, pull_requests[{pr_url, pr_state}], structured_output, category/subcategory, devin_mode, acus_consumed, security_profile, is_archived (https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/get-organizations-session.md). It also holds a chronological message log: {event_id, source: devin|user, message, created_at, origin, user_id, username} (https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/get-organizations-session-messages.md). Attachments and a finer-grained event stream sit beside it; Devin MCP can list, fetch or text-search the events (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/devin-mcp.md). The Progress tab logs every shell command (with output), code edit and browser action, and you can jump to any point in time; screen recordings are kept too (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/devin-session-tools.md). The VM's disk is not a durable record: every session boots from a fresh copy of the machine image (snapshot), and anything created mid-session, such as GPG keys, is discarded when the session ends (https://docs.devin.ai/integrations/gh.md). Dedicated tenants also store VM snapshots (https://docs.devin.ai/enterprise/security-access/security/customer-managed-keys.md).
SESSION INSIGHTS: these are LLM-derived artifacts, not raw history. Every session gets a lightweight classification at the end (category, languages, tools). L/XL sessions (>10 ACU, or >100 for enterprise) get a full analysis automatically at teardown; smaller ones on demand via UI or API, in about a minute (https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/session-insights.md). Analysis schema: issues[{id, label, impact, issue}], timeline[{title, description, color, issue_id}] (no timestamps), action_items, note_usage {good_usages, bad_usages}, skill_usage, suggested_prompt, classification, plus analysis_status started/completed/failed; a failed rerun may leave an older result in place (https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/get-organizations-session-insights.md).
LOCAL CLI: conversation history in a local SQLite 'session database' with schema migrations. It keeps messages from before compaction, supports resume/fork/revert by step, and /rm-session deletes a session irreversibly (https://docs.devin.ai/cli/changelog/stable.md, https://docs.devin.ai/cli/reference/commands.md).
OTHER: org Knowledge notes (deprecated and being migrated to Skills in Devin-managed Plugins; https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/knowledge.md) and encrypted Secrets (https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/secrets.md).
where_stored:
Server/cloud. Cloud sessions run on Devin-managed VMs and the CLI only streams them (https://docs.devin.ai/cli/cloud.md). The 'brain' is stateless and always runs in Cognition's cloud, whatever the deployment (https://docs.devin.ai/enterprise/deployment/overview.md).
- Multi-tenant Enterprise Cloud: the storage backend for transcripts is not documented. DPA subprocessors list AWS and Google Cloud for 'core processing, profile data, logs, and indices' and Azure for 'core processing', all US (https://cognition.com/legal/data-processing-statement, updated July 23, 2026). The deployment doc's diagram says Cognition's tenant is hosted on Azure, while the security pages say AWS (https://docs.devin.ai/admin/security.md). I could not resolve this.
- Dedicated (Enterprise Assured) tenants: customer data, 'including session data and VM snapshots', goes to Amazon S3 buckets in the dedicated tenant, encrypted server-side with KMS (https://docs.devin.ai/enterprise/security-access/security/customer-managed-keys.md).
- Outposts: commands, file edits and repo access run on customer machines, but the agent loop (inference and planning) and the session queue stay in Devin Cloud. So transcripts still go to Cognition (https://docs.devin.ai/cloud/outposts/overview.md).
- Code: in the customer's git host (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Azure DevOps) as branches and PRs (https://docs.devin.ai/integrations/gh.md).
- Local CLI: a SQLite DB under the CLI data dir. Only the logs path is documented (~/.local/share/devin/cli/logs/; https://docs.devin.ai/cli/troubleshooting.md); the DB filename is undocumented.
- Retention: data is kept 'for the duration of the relationship', and feedback and interaction data 'as long as needed ... as determined by Cognition' (https://docs.devin.ai/admin/security.md). Subprocessors delete within 30 days of DPA termination (https://cognition.com/legal/data-processing-statement). The API has no hard-delete for cloud sessions: Archive 'does not delete' and terminated sessions 'remain available for reference' (https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/post-organizations-sessions-archive.md, https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/delete-organizations-sessions.md). Per-session retention periods are not documented.
format_and_model:
An opaque server database exposed as JSON over a REST API (v3, OpenAPI 3.1, cursor pagination, errors as RFC 9457 problem+json; https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/get-organizations-session-messages.md). The data model is session-centric: a mutable session row (status, tags, title and archive flag all change in place) plus a chronological message/event list keyed by event_id. Sessions form a tree: parent_session_id/child_session_ids for coordinator-managed child Devins, and archiving cascades to descendants (https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/post-organizations-sessions-archive.md).
Local CLI exports:
- `--export` writes the conversation after each turn in ATIF (Agent Trajectory Interchange Format) JSON, with per-step telemetry and timing (https://docs.devin.ai/cli/reference/commands.md; changelog v2026.5.26).
- An OpenTelemetry exporter for agent events and metrics (v3000.11.1, Sep 21, 2026; https://docs.devin.ai/cli/changelog/stable.md).
- `devin list --format json|csv` lists sessions.
Dynamic Workflows keep a run journal: each agent() call's result is recorded against a run ID and keyed by a hash of prompt, schema and execution settings. Resume re-executes the script and replays recorded results. Scripts must not depend on time, randomness, environment or network (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/dynamic-workflows.md). Nothing documented describes hash-chaining, signing or tamper evidence for transcripts.
multi_writer_and_merge:
Each session's log is linear and the server owns it; transcripts are never merged.
- Many humans can write into one session: web, CLI, Desktop, API (sending a message resumes a suspended session) and multi-participant Slack threads with per-message names (https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/get-organizations-session-messages.md, https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/devin.md). Desktop's send queue lives on the server, so it survives reloads and shows up in the web app.
- Moving between machines creates a NEW session rather than syncing a log:
  - Local to cloud: `/handoff` packages repo, branch, uncommitted diff (including untracked files since v2026.5.6) and 'conversation context'. Called with no arguments it 'summarizes the current conversation', so the cloud session starts from a summary, not the transcript (https://docs.devin.ai/cli/handoff.md, https://docs.devin.ai/cli/changelog/stable.md). The cross-agent plugin puts `git diff HEAD`, truncated to 100KB, plus free-text --context into the session prompt and tags the session `handoff` (https://github.com/club-cog/devin-handoff).
  - Cloud to local: `/pickup` (or `/handoff` inside a cloud session) fetches the session's PR branch, switches the checkout and starts a fresh local session (https://docs.devin.ai/cli/cloud.md).
- Parallel work: a coordinator session spawns managed Devins, each on its own VM, and 'resolves conflicts' and compiles results. Merging happens in git through branches and PRs, including stacked PRs (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/advanced-capabilities.md).
- Local `/fork [step]` branches a session; `/revert` rewinds files and conversation (https://docs.devin.ai/cli/reference/commands.md).
realtime:
Yes for cloud sessions:
- The CLI streams the VM session into the terminal live; closing the terminal does not stop it (https://docs.devin.ai/cli/cloud.md).
- Web, Desktop and CLI views of a session stay in sync. Desktop connects over 'Remote ACP' and shows a reconnect banner when it drops (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/devin.md).
- `/handoff` shows live status lines (https://docs.devin.ai/cli/changelog/stable.md).
- Slack threads sync with sessions (https://docs.devin.ai/integrations/slack.md).
- Desktop 'Spaces' group local and cloud sessions, PRs and files; new sessions in a Space inherit shared context (`devin.spaces.shareContext`). How that context is stored or synced is not documented (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/spaces.md).
Local CLI sessions are not live-shared. `/share` uploads a conversation snapshot and returns an account-scoped link (changelog v3000.4.25), and OTel export can stream events to the user's own collector.
search_retrieval:
Cloud:
- List sessions; filter by is_archived and tags (https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/post-organizations-sessions-archive.md).
- List messages chronologically with cursors (https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/get-organizations-session-messages.md).
- Devin MCP: `devin_session_search` filters by tags, playbook, origin, schedule, user or time; `devin_session_events` lists, fetches and full-text searches event contents; `devin_session_gather` waits on many sessions (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/devin-mcp.md).
- List and get sessions with insights, and org metrics by category.
- Past sessions are fed back to the agent on purpose: paste a session link and Devin 'examines the session history' to explain failures or build playbooks (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/advanced-capabilities.md).
- Knowledge was recalled by LLM-matched 'trigger descriptions' or by pinning to a repo; that is now migrating to Skills (https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/knowledge.md).
Local: `/ls [--all]`, a type-to-filter resume picker, `devin -c` / `-r <id>`, and `devin list --format json|csv` (https://docs.devin.ai/cli/reference/commands.md).
Nothing documented covers semantic or vector search over transcripts, or exact-span recall APIs.
links_sessions_to_code:
Yes, but by reference: the PR points at the session URL, and the session points back at the PR. The transcript never goes into git.
- If the repo has no PR template, Devin's default PR description gets 'the session URL and requester appended automatically' (https://docs.devin.ai/integrations/pr-templates.md).
- The session API carries pull_requests[{pr_url, pr_state}] (https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/get-organizations-session.md).
- `/devin ...` PR comments start a session and reply on the PR with its link (https://docs.devin.ai/integrations/gh.md).
- Commit and PR attribution is configurable: 'Open PRs as' user or Devin, and commit authoring 'Devin only', 'Co-authored', 'You as author, Devin as committer' and so on. I did not verify the exact trailer format.
- The CLI sets `AI_AGENT=devin_<version>_agent` in agent shell commands (v3000.11.1; https://docs.devin.ai/cli/changelog/stable.md).
- The PR branch is the only return path from cloud to local (`/pickup`), and handoff sends the local branch and diff up.
- Desktop Spaces group sessions with PRs (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/spaces.md).
Nothing documented links individual commits to session steps.
scale:
No numbers for storage or throughput. Claims:
- 'Proven use cases deployed across hundreds of enterprises' (https://docs.devin.ai/use-cases/index.md).
- Coordinators fan out to many managed Devins, e.g. a 50-file migration (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/advanced-capabilities.md).
- Dynamic workflow runs have a default and maximum budget of 7 days (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/dynamic-workflows.md).
- Outposts: N workers serve N concurrent sessions; the rest queue (https://docs.devin.ai/cloud/outposts/overview.md).
- Session size buckets XS–XL by ACU, with enterprise thresholds ×10 (https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/session-insights.md).
privacy_security:
Encryption:
- In transit and at rest. SOC 2 Type II; the dates conflict across pages (March 2024 vs September 2024) (https://docs.devin.ai/admin/security.md, https://docs.devin.ai/enterprise/security-access/security/enterprise-security.md).
- Keys are held in AWS KMS (https://cognition.com/legal/data-processing-statement).
- Customer-managed AWS KMS keys exist only on Enterprise Assured. They encrypt S3 session data and snapshots, revocation makes the data unreadable, and the key is fixed when the tenant is created (https://docs.devin.ai/enterprise/security-access/security/customer-managed-keys.md).
Secrets:
- Encrypted at rest, with org, personal, repo and session scopes. They are bound as environment variables per command, or typed into the browser. Repo secrets are 'never written into your blueprint or snapshot' (https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/secrets.md).
- No documented redaction of secrets or PII from transcripts, insights or exports.
- `/handoff` uploads the uncommitted diff, untracked files included, with no documented secret scanning ('commit or stash anything you don't want sent'; https://docs.devin.ai/cli/handoff.md).
- CLI trace logs can contain Authorization headers (https://docs.devin.ai/cli/troubleshooting.md).
Training: paid plans can opt out, which also turns on zero data retention with model providers. Enterprise data is never used for training without written consent. Feedback and interaction data is retained at Cognition's discretion (https://docs.devin.ai/admin/security.md).
Prompt injection:
- Enterprise AI Guardrails screen user messages and PR comments, with log, warn or block actions recorded in audit logs. They do not cover tool output, web pages or recalled history (https://docs.devin.ai/enterprise/features/ai-guardrails.md).
- Security Profiles add network, MCP, git and Devin-MCP read-only allowlists (https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/security-profiles.md).
- In 2025, independent research showed indirect prompt injection (a web page or GitHub issue) leading to code execution on the DevBox and exfiltration of secrets. It was reported April 6, 2025, with no answer on fix status after more than 120 days (https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2025/devin-i-spent-usd500-to-hack-devin/, https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2025/devin-can-leak-your-secrets/).
- Feeding past sessions back to the agent by link is unenveloped by design (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/advanced-capabilities.md).
lesson_for_parinn:
Devin uses git only to carry code (cloud to local is 'check out the session's PR branch'), and it keeps the session record on its own server, tied to the code only by a session URL in the PR body and a pull_requests field on the session. Its local-to-cloud handoff is lossy and unverifiable: an LLM summary plus `git diff HEAD` (the plugin truncates it to 100KB) pasted into a new session's prompt. The new session therefore starts from a paraphrase, has no provenance, and puts anything in the diff or summary straight into the model's context.
For ParleyInn:
- Keep the same split. Git, or the forge's PR, carries the code and a stable cross-reference (a session ID or record-head hash in a trailer or the PR body); the hash-chained record travels separately through ParleyInn's own store.
- On a handoff between machines, ship either the record segment or a verifiable pointer to its head hash, never a summary standing in for history.
- Let the receiving agent recall that history only on demand and only inside the untrusted envelope (I2). Audit and count truncation (I6) instead of silently cutting at 100KB.
Corollary: Devin's Dynamic Workflows replay journal keys each step by a hash of its inputs and bans clock, randomness and environment reads. That is the same discipline as ParleyInn's I10, already shipping as a product feature, and evidence that deterministic replay over a recorded log works for agents.

name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) Cascade Memories and Rules
status: archived. Cascade Memories still ships, but only for a legacy agent. On June 2, 2026 Cognition renamed Windsurf to Devin Desktop and made Devin Local, a from-scratch Rust rewrite, "the successor to Cascade as our primary local agent". The announcement said Cascade "through July 1st" (https://devin.ai/blog/windsurf-is-now-devin-desktop). The current docs open with a warning: "Memories apply to the legacy Cascade agent only. The Devin Local agent — the default agent for new tabs — does not persist memories." Users are told to move memories into skills with the "Devin: Open Cascade Migration Wizard" (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/memories, https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/devin-local). The docs also say "New conversations never start on Cascade, but your existing Cascade conversations remain available", and admins can switch Cascade off with an "Enable Cascade" control. So it is superseded but still readable. One secondary source says Cascade is fully end-of-life since July 1, 2026 (https://businesstechnavigator.com/news/windsurf-devin-desktop-cascade-eol-2026). Some of its migration claims conflict with the official docs, so treat it as unverified. Rules and AGENTS.md carry over to Devin Local; auto-memories do not.
what_is_stored:
There are two kinds of content (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/memories).

(1) Auto-generated Memories. The agent writes these during a chat "if it encounters context that it believes is useful to remember". A user can also ask for one ("create a memory of ..."). They hold short facts and preferences, not transcripts. The docs say to use them for "one-off facts" and to prefer Rules or AGENTS.md for durable knowledge. The memory is written by the agent's `create_memory` tool, which needs no human approval (https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2025/windsurf-spaiware-exploit-persistent-prompt-injection/).

(2) Rules. These are Markdown instructions written by people, at four levels:
- global: a single global_rules.md, always on, up to 6,000 characters
- workspace: .devin/rules/*.md, or the legacy .windsurf/rules/*.md and .windsurfrules, up to 12,000 characters per file
- AGENTS.md in any directory
- system-level enterprise rules deployed by IT

Neither kind stores full session transcripts, prompts, diffs or provenance. Cascade conversation history is stored separately. The Devin Local "Share conversation" feature uploads a sanitized transcript to make a share link (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/devin-local).
where_stored:
Local files only.

- Auto-memories: "stored locally in ~/.codeium/windsurf/memories/", tied to the workspace that created them, "not committed to your repository" and "live only on your machine".
- Global rules: ~/.codeium/windsurf/memories/global_rules.md.
- Workspace rules: in the working tree at .devin/rules (preferred) or .windsurf/rules. They are discovered in the workspace, in its subdirectories and in parent directories up to the git root, and committed like ordinary files.
- System rules: /etc/devin/rules/*.md (legacy /etc/windsurf/rules), /Library/Application Support/Devin/rules/*.md on macOS, or C:\ProgramData\Devin\rules\*.md on Windows.

Source for all of the above: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/memories.

Community sources say Cascade conversations live as protobuf (.pb) files under ~/.codeium/windsurf/cascade (https://ptkd.com/journal/does-windsurf-cascade-leak-api-keys-in-the-prompt-history). This is not in the official docs and is unverified.

Devin Local adds two more locations: plans in ~/.devin/plans/plan-<session>.md, and config in .devin/config.json (committed) plus .devin/config.local.json (gitignored) (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/devin-local).
format_and_model:
Rules are Markdown files, one rule per file. Optional YAML frontmatter sets `trigger: always_on | model_decision | glob | manual`, plus `description` and `globs`. global_rules.md and the root AGENTS.md have no frontmatter and are always on. An AGENTS.md in a subdirectory acts as an automatic glob rule for that directory.

The on-disk format and schema of auto-memories are not documented officially. They are edited only through the Customizations UI, and I could not verify the file format.

The data model is a flat set of notes or rules per workspace. It has no versioning, no event log, no hash chain and no session or commit linkage (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/memories).
multi_writer_and_merge:
Auto-memories have one writer: a single user's agent on a single machine, in a single workspace. They are never shared, and the docs give no sync or merge mechanism. To share a memory, the docs tell users to have the agent write it into .devin/rules/ or AGENTS.md. From then on, multiple writers and merging are just git's normal handling of text files.

When several folders are open in one workspace, rules are "deduplicated and displayed with the shortest relative path". System rules "are merged with workspace and global rules ... without overriding user-defined rules", and the docs say .devin/ takes precedence over .windsurf/. No conflict resolution is documented beyond that (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/memories).

Spaces group local and cloud sessions, and new sessions in a Space inherit "project-level context". This is controlled by `devin.spaces.shareContext`. The docs do not say where that context lives or how it merges (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/spaces).
realtime: Not applicable to auto-memories. They are local, per workspace, with no cross-machine or cross-user sync. Rules spread only through git push and pull or MDM deployment. Spaces share context between sessions in the Agent Command Center, but the docs make no claim about real-time sync or its mechanism (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/spaces).
search_retrieval:
The model decides what to pull in: Cascade "retrieves them when it believes they're relevant". The retrieval algorithm is not documented. Third-party posts say memories are injected at session start (https://memu.pro/blog/windsurf-ide-ai-coding-agent-memory); this is unverified.

Rule activation is spelled out:
- always_on: full text in the system prompt on every message
- model_decision: only the description sits in the prompt, and the full file is read on demand
- glob: applied when the agent reads or edits a matching file
- manual: applied when the user types @rule-name

There is no user-facing search over memories beyond the settings UI (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/memories).
links_sessions_to_code: No. Memories are tied to a workspace, not to commits, files or sessions. Rules version with the repo only because they are files in it. Separately, Devin Desktop worktree sessions can be merged back into the workspace, and Spaces group sessions with their PRs in the UI (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/devin-local, https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/spaces). Neither records which prompt or session produced which code.
scale: No scale claims for memories. The documented limits are on rules: 6,000 characters for global_rules.md and 12,000 characters per workspace rule file. Memories cost no credits (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/memories).
privacy_security:
Privacy: auto-memories stay on the machine and out of the repo (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/memories). The docs say nothing about encryption at rest, redaction of memories or scanning memories for secrets.

Security: in May 2025 Johann Rehberger reported to the vendor that the agent's `create_memory` tool runs without human approval. He disclosed it publicly on August 22, 2025. An indirect prompt injection, for example in a code comment, can therefore write a malicious memory. That memory persists into future sessions and enables ongoing data exfiltration ("SpAIware"), and the UI cue for a new memory is easy to miss. The vendor did not respond for about three months and then promised fixes with no timeline (https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2025/windsurf-spaiware-exploit-persistent-prompt-injection/). I could not verify whether it was fixed before memories were dropped from the default agent.

Enterprise controls: read-only system rules deployed by IT. In Devin Local, transcripts shared through "Share conversation" are sanitized, with secrets redacted and system prompts and tool definitions dropped, and sharing can be switched off per organization (https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/devin-local).
lesson_for_parinn:
A memory that the agent writes and that is pushed into the prompt automatically is a prompt-injection channel that persists. Windsurf's create_memory needed no approval, so injected text turned into standing instructions across sessions (SpAIware). The vendor then dropped auto-memories from its new default agent and steered users to rules files that people write and review. For ParleyInn this supports invariant I2: recalled history must stay untrusted, pull-only and enveloped. Only content a human has pinned and that is held as trusted text should ever be re-injected. Durable knowledge meant for the team belongs in reviewed, version-controlled files, not in a store the agent writes without approval.

A second lesson: the split of private local memory in the home directory versus shared rules in the repo, with no history or links between them, is a gap ParleyInn's append-only record can fill. ParleyInn should still keep the same separation between "private, per machine" and "deliberately shared".
license: Proprietary, closed-source commercial product from Cognition. No source code or license is published for the memory system. Rules are plain Markdown in the user's repo.

name: Devin GitHub integration (PR-triggered sessions and session links on PRs), by Cognition
category: agent session link on PR (hosted, proprietary session store; git holds only code and PR metadata)
status: shipped. The docs were current when fetched on 2026-10-02, and a public example PR from August 2026 shows the pattern in use. This is a commercial SaaS product and has not been archived or superseded.
what_is_stored: Only pointers go into git or GitHub. A comment that starts with `/devin <prompt>` on an open PR "starts a new session with that repository, uses the PR as context (taking over the PR if appropriate), and replies on the PR with a link to the session" (https://docs.devin.ai/integrations/gh). PRs that Devin opens carry a "Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/<32-hex id>" line and a "Requested by: @user" line in the PR body. They are authored by devin-ai-integration[bot] and their commits carry a `Co-Authored-By: <requesting human>` trailer (example: https://github.com/flightcontrolhq/modules/pull/84). Commit and PR authorship can be set to Devin, the user, or user-only (https://docs.devin.ai/integrations/gh). Devin Review can also add a "Devin Review" link to the PR description and post bugs and security findings as PR comments (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/devin-review). Everything else stays on Cognition's side: the session itself (chat messages, Devin's actions, its VM with shell, browser and IDE), attachments, tags, a structured output, ACU consumption, AI-generated "insights" and a category, and parent/child session links. These are documented in the v3 Sessions API (https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/get-organizations-session.md, https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/get-organizations-session-messages.md). I could not verify from public docs whether full shell, browser and tool traces are exposed beyond the message list.
where_stored: On Cognition's servers and cloud (app.devin.ai). The docs place the stateless "Brain" always in Cognition's Cloud. The Devbox runs either in Cognition's multi-tenant cloud or, for Customer Dedicated Deployment, in a single-tenant VPC that Cognition hosts (https://docs.devin.ai/enterprise/deployment/overview.md). For dedicated deployments, "all customer data is stored within the customer's tenant" (https://docs.devin.ai/enterprise/security-access/security/enterprise-security.md). Git and GitHub hold only the code, the commits with their Co-Authored-By trailers, and PR bodies and comments that contain the session URL. No session content goes into git notes, refs or files.
format_and_model: The format is proprietary, exposed as JSON over a REST API. A Session (`session_id` with a `devin-` prefix) has url, status (new, claimed, running, exit, error, suspended, resuming), status_detail, origin (webapp, slack, teams, api, linear, jira, automation, cli, desktop, code_scan, other), user_id or service_user_id, org_id, parent_session_id, child_session_ids, playbook_id, automation_id, tags, title, category and subcategory, structured_output, acus_consumed, created_at and updated_at as integers, is_archived, a security_profile binding, and pull_requests, a list of {pr_url, pr_state} (https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/get-organizations-session.md). A SessionMessage has event_id, source (devin or user), message (a string), origin, user_id, username and created_at. Messages are listed in chronological order with cursor pagination (https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/get-organizations-session-messages.md). So the session-to-code link is a PR-URL list on the session plus a session URL in the PR body. It is a bidirectional pointer pair, not content addressing. Nothing indicates hashing or a tamper-evident chain.
multi_writer_and_merge: There is one hosted session per task, and the server is the only authority. Several humans can write into it: a later `/devin` comment on a PR that already has an active session "is sent to that session instead of starting a new one" (https://docs.devin.ai/integrations/gh). Devin also "automatically responds to comments on PRs its sessions are working on, as long as the session has not been archived" (same page). For parallel work, a coordinator session spawns child sessions, each in its own VM, and "resolves conflicts" at the code level (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/advanced-capabilities.md). Session history itself is never merged across replicas. Concurrent work is reconciled only through git branches and PRs, including stacked PRs.
realtime: Yes, but only through the hosted service. Sessions are live in the web app (IDE and browser iframes served from *.devinapps.com), and the workspace holds a secure WebSocket to Cognition's tenant (https://docs.devin.ai/enterprise/deployment/overview.md). PR comments are delivered to a running session as GitHub webhook events. Messages sent through the API resume a suspended session (https://docs.devin.ai/_llms/en/api.md). The PR shows nothing in real time beyond Devin's comments and pushes.
search_retrieval: Retrieval goes through the hosted UI and the API: list and get sessions, list messages, list attachments and tags, and session "insights" with AI-generated analysis (https://docs.devin.ai/_llms/en/api.md, https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/session-insights.md). Devin can "analyze past work" from inside a session (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/advanced-capabilities.md). Cross-session memory is curated, not raw: "Knowledge" entries and playbooks (https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/knowledge.md). There is no git-native search of session history, and I found no documented full-text search over transcripts.
links_sessions_to_code: Yes, at PR granularity. GitHub to session: the bot comment and the PR body carry the app.devin.ai/sessions/<id> URL plus "Requested by". Session to GitHub: the session record holds pull_requests [{pr_url, pr_state}]. Commits attribute the human through Co-Authored-By, or through author or committer settings (https://github.com/flightcontrolhq/modules/pull/84, https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/sessions/get-organizations-session.md, https://docs.devin.ai/integrations/gh). The link is not at commit or line level, and the session URL only works for signed-in members of the Devin org; a public reader of an open-source PR cannot follow it (inferred from the private-by-default product, not stated explicitly). Handoff from Claude Code, Codex and others through the open-source devin-handoff plugin sends the repo, branch and `git diff HEAD` (truncated to 100KB) inside the session prompt (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/devin-handoff.md).
scale: The docs make no numeric scale claims for session storage. Parallel managed sessions are pitched for migrations and bulk work, each in an isolated VM (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/advanced-capabilities.md). The Enterprise Cloud deployment is described as multi-tenant, and the dedicated one as an "auto-scaling, customer-isolated environment" (https://docs.devin.ai/enterprise/deployment/overview.md).
privacy_security:
Trust and identity:
- The GitHub App acts with org-level permissions, "not the permissions of the individual user running a session". It has read-write access to contents, PRs, issues, workflows, checks and statuses. It cannot create repositories.
- `/devin` triggers need write or admin access on the repo, a linked GitHub account, and Devin org membership. They are ignored on issues and on closed or merged PRs.
- Branch protection is recommended, and outbound traffic comes from published IPs that can be allowlisted (https://docs.devin.ai/integrations/gh).

Data protection:
- Data is "encrypted in transit and at rest", with AWS KMS keys rotated periodically, and customer-managed keys in the Enterprise Assured tier (https://docs.devin.ai/admin/security.md, https://docs.devin.ai/enterprise/security-access/security/customer-managed-keys.md).
- Cognition holds SOC 2 Type II (https://docs.devin.ai/enterprise/security-access/security/enterprise-security.md).
- Data is retained for the length of the customer relationship. Feedback and interaction data are kept "as long as needed and as determined by Cognition".
- Non-enterprise data may be used for training by default. Paid plans can opt out, which also enables Zero Data Retention with model providers (https://docs.devin.ai/admin/security.md).

Secrets:
- Secrets are encrypted at rest and scoped to org, personal, repo or session (https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/secrets.md).
- Credentials pasted into the chat when Devin asks are "scoped purely to the current session". I found no documentation saying they are redacted from the stored transcript, so I could not verify any transcript redaction.

Untrusted input:
- PR comments from anyone with write access flow straight into the agent's context. I found no documented treatment of PR or recalled content as untrusted, or any prompt-injection envelope.

Security profiles can restrict network, MCP, git and gh CLI access per org, automation or session (https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/security-profiles.md).
license: Proprietary commercial SaaS (Cognition AI). The devin-handoff plugin is open source (https://github.com/club-cog/devin-handoff); I did not check its license.
lesson_for_parinn: Separate the pointer from the payload, and make the pointer verifiable without the vendor. Devin puts only a mutable, login-gated URL (app.devin.ai/sessions/<id>) plus "Requested by" and a Co-Authored-By trailer into git and the PR. The history behind it lives on one hosted server: no hash, not reachable by OSS readers, gone when the customer relationship ends. It is also not reproducible offline, which conflicts with ParleyInn's I4 (no network) and I10 (rebuildable from the record). ParleyInn can keep the cheap, widely understood PR and commit linkage, a trailer or PR-body line, but should make the token a content address: the session id plus the hash-chain head (for example `ParleyInn-Session: <id>@<chain-head-hash>`). That way any holder of the append-only record can check that it matches what the PR cites, whatever transport carried it (git ref, bundle, sandbox export). Devin also forwards `/devin` PR comments straight into a live agent. ParleyInn should treat such inbound PR text as untrusted recall material, enveloped and pull-only, not as instructions (I2).

name: DiffMem (Growth Kinetics)
category: git-backed agent memory (conversational/persona memory, not coding agents)
status: shipped
what_is_stored: Two things. (1) LLM-written current-state Markdown memory files per user. Each user has a profile `{user_id}.md`, an auto-generated keyword `index.md`, entity files under `memories/people/`, `memories/contexts/` and `memories/events/`, and monthly `timeline/YYYY-MM.md` entries. Since v0.5 the folder layout comes from a pluggable ontology, `personal` or `corporate` (README "Repository layout" and Status at https://github.com/Growth-Kinetics/DiffMem/blob/48ecbb61e7fedca40d1b41bdfb217a5f80432b20/README.md ; schema https://github.com/Growth-Kinetics/DiffMem/blob/48ecbb61e7fedca40d1b41bdfb217a5f80432b20/src/diffmem/ontologies/personal/schema.json). (2) The raw session input itself, which the README layout leaves out. `process_session` writes every transcript verbatim to `sessions/{date}_{session_id}.txt` "for future replay/rebuild", and it is committed with the rest (writer_agent/agent.py L1208-1222, https://github.com/Growth-Kinetics/DiffMem/blob/48ecbb61e7fedca40d1b41bdfb217a5f80432b20/src/diffmem/writer_agent/agent.py#L1208-L1222). Git history holds every earlier state of each file. Entity files also carry derived metadata: YAML frontmatter, aliases, hard cues, and a "memory strength" score computed from git edit count and wall-clock recency (agent.py L669-689; frontmatter.py https://github.com/Growth-Kinetics/DiffMem/blob/48ecbb61e7fedca40d1b41bdfb217a5f80432b20/src/diffmem/frontmatter.py). Not stored: tool calls, code or structured agent events. Input is free-text chat transcripts from the Annabelle WhatsApp/Messenger persona (README "Live in Production").
where_stored: A local git repo on a mounted volume is the source of truth, `/data/storage` by default. It is created with `git.Repo.init`, which makes a non-bare repo; the code's docstring calls it "Bare-ish". The discovery note's "one bare repo" is therefore slightly off. Each user is an orphan branch `user/{user_id}`, checked out as a git worktree at `/data/worktrees/{user_id}` (local_storage.py L42-81, https://github.com/Growth-Kinetics/DiffMem/blob/48ecbb61e7fedca40d1b41bdfb217a5f80432b20/src/diffmem/storage/local_storage.py). A GitHub mirror is optional (`BACKUP_BACKEND=github`): one private repo holds every user's branch. Since the v0.4 refactor (commit dd2058a, 2026-04-17), GitHub is "a backup, not a database". Before 0.4 it was the primary datastore (README "Migrating from earlier DiffMem versions"). Job status lives in an in-process job store, or in Hatchet Cloud with `EXECUTOR=hatchet` (https://github.com/Growth-Kinetics/DiffMem/blob/48ecbb61e7fedca40d1b41bdfb217a5f80432b20/docs/api-surface.md).
format_and_model: Plain Markdown files with YAML frontmatter. Older files may instead end in a `## SEMANTIC INDEX` JSON block (frontmatter.py). The link consolidator weaves Obsidian-style wikilinks such as `[[memories/people/maya|Maya]]` into the prose. The data model is entities as files, a "current state" surface, plus git commits as the temporal "depth". One commit per ingested session, with message `Session {session_id} | {up to 8 entity stems}` (agent.py L1260-1279). Repair commits are prefixed `consolidate(dedupe|redistribute|link|reabsorb):` so they can be told apart from session commits (README "Consolidation"). Files are rewritten in place, so the record is mutable working-tree state: there is no append-only log, hashing beyond git's own, or signing. Derived files (`index.md`, semantic indexes, timeline entries) come from LLM calls, and memory strength reads `datetime.now()`. Replaying `sessions/` would therefore not deterministically rebuild the same state. The sample repo shows the format: 12 commits on `user/mr_utterson`, one per chapter of Jekyll and Hyde, with folders `memories/`, `sessions/`, `timeline/` and `.obsidian/` (https://github.com/Growth-Kinetics/diffmem_sample_memory).
multi_writer_and_merge: The design is a single writer per user. There is no git merge or conflict resolution.
